title: Engineering Manager, Data & Clinical Integration Teams
descriptionText: ABOUT CAREMESSAGE CareMessage is a social enterprise and the largest patient engagement platform for low-income populations in the United States. We deliver personalized health education and care coordination through text messaging — reaching patients where they already are, in the language they speak, at the moments that matter most. Unlike technology built for large health systems and adapted down, CareMessage is designed from the ground up for organizations serving low-income, historically marginalized communities. WHY JOIN US IN LEVERAGING TECHNOLOGY TO IMPROVE HEALTH EQUITY Many of us have had the experience of doing good work or building great products, but wondering if it is truly making an impact. At CareMessage, our mission is clear: improve health equity for low-income populations across the United States. Every role here connects directly to that purpose. We care deeply about the communities we serve, and we also hold a high standard for performance, collaboration, and integrity. Our ideal team members: - Deliver meaningful, measurable results - Invest in their teammates and build trust - Seek feedback and continually grow - Stay steady and solutions-oriented in ambiguity - Lead with integrity and responsibility - Communicate with clarity and empathy If you are motivated by impact, energized by collaboration, and ready to do some of the most meaningful work of your career, we encourage you to apply. If this sounds like you, we would love to meet you. _____________________________________ ROLE OVERVIEW The Engineering Manager, Data & Clinical Integration owns and drives the technical direction of the two teams responsible for CareMessage's data — the Clinical Integration team, which connects CareMessage to electronic health records (EHRs) and other clinical data sources (e.g. HIEs, Payor Data, etc.) across our customer base, and the Data team, which turns that data into trustworthy insights. CareMessage supports over 400 safety-net healthcare organizations including federally qualified health centers and free clinics that care for low-income and underserved patients nationwide, and these two teams are the engine behind our ability to measurably demonstrate impact on clinical outcomes, access to care, and the social drivers of health. This is a leadership role over existing teams: their systems and roadmaps are already in place, and your job is to lead, deepen, and scale them. A core part of this role is leading both teams to turn clinical data from our customers' many different EHRs into trustworthy, query-ready data that can measurably demonstrate health outcomes — and scaling those insights through both AI/ML and human analysis. The Clinical Integration team builds and maintains the integrations that connect CareMessage to leading EHRs (Epic, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, AthenaHealth, and others) over HL7, FHIR, Proprietary APIs, and direct-database interfaces using the Rhapsody integration engine, and it owns the first step of the clinical data pipeline — converting clinical data to FHIR and landing it in our FHIR Store and BigQuery. The Data team builds on top of that with a medallion (bronze/silver/gold) architecture in BigQuery using native Google Cloud services, and dbt, surfacing insights through Metabase dashboards such as our Health Equity and diabetes-outcomes views; and increasingly powering AI/ML-driven workflows that surface insights at scale. In this role, you will collaborate closely with Product, Customer Success, Data, Compliance, and Engineering to design and deliver the platform and integrations that deepen patient engagement and health outcomes, with direct ownership of technical decisions and customer-facing system behavior. Our ideal candidate is an experienced Engineering Manager (technical, people and process leader) who thrives in dynamic, fully-distributed environments and is energized by the intersection of healthcare interoperability and data. They are passionate about partnering with business stakeholders to develop the platform and processes that uncover data insights, and they are dedicated to the professional growth of engineers. They view themselves as a catalyst for organizational outcomes and accomplish that through enabling high-output team productivity and continuously seek ways to elevate Engineering and the organization as a whole. Above all, they share our mission-driven commitment and take pride in contributing to our objective of advancing health equity for low-income populations. One of the strongest skills we value here is taking a scientific approach to everything we do. We rely on evidence alongside intuition, and we look for data that challenges our assumptions before drawing conclusions. Our PRDs, documentation, and wikis reflect this mindset — we use data to guide decisions and validate our work. CORE REQUIREMENTS - Proven Track Record: At least 5 years of successful experience as an Engineering Manager over Integration and/or Data Engineering teams, in two or more early-to-growth-stage remote startup environments. - Strategic Leadership: Demonstrated ability to lead and drive the delivery of long-term technical projects across multiple teams driving measurable outcomes. - Technical Proficiency: Strong technical acumen with a deep understanding of SQL, data concepts, pipelines (ELT), and cloud data warehousing. - Modern & AI-Assisted Engineering: A track record of adopting modern development practices and leveraging AI-assisted tooling (e.g., Agentic coding, harnesses, and LLM-based workflows) to raise engineering velocity and quality — with the judgment to apply them responsibly in a healthcare/PHI context. You actively coach your teams to fold these tools into their day-to-day work. - Hands-on Experience: The ability to get hands-on with SQL and data tooling when needed. (This is predominantly a management position; however, you should be able to dig in to help answer key data questions and unblock the team.) - Collaborative Expertise: Exceptional collaboration and influencing skills, working effectively cross-departmentally to craft optimal solutions while navigating multiple constraints. - Situational Awareness: The ability to discern when to dive into technical details and when to maintain a higher-level perspective when working with Engineers, Product, and Design. - Cultural Advocate: A commitment to cultivating both individual growth and a high-performance engineering culture that attracts top talent. - Mentorship: A growth-oriented mindset with the capability to guide others on their development journey. - Communication Skills: Outstanding written and verbal communication skills, especially in a fully remote environment. - Autonomous Prioritization: Proficiency in identifying and managing priorities independently across two teams, ensuring an efficient workflow. - Diversity and Inclusion: Dedication to promoting diversity and inclusion within teams, especially given our global team composition. - This role requires the candidate to reside within the United States of America. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE - Experience managing or working closely with healthcare integration / interoperability teams (HL7, FHIR) in addition to Data teams. - Experience working in a Healthcare technology environment and the requisite Security and Compliance requirements (HIPAA/PHI). - Experience introducing or scaling agentic development workflows on a team, with attention to code quality, security, and compliance. - Experience applying AI/ML to large datasets to scale insight generation (e.g., summarization, classification, anomaly detection). - Experience with our Tech Stack: - Data: GCP / BigQuery, dbt, Python, Metabase, and a medallion (bronze/silver/gold) architecture. - Clinical Integration: Rhapsody integration engine (JavaScript), HL7, FHIR, FHIR Store, mainstream EHRs (Epic, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, AthenaHealth), Ruby on Rails, Postgres, GCP. - Background in TDD engineering environments. - Experience leveraging healthcare data and foundational data science concepts. JOB RESPONSIBILITIES - Technical Leadership: You are excited about and comfortable with taking responsibility for making sure that you understand and can defend the investments and decisions your team is making, helping to challenge, redirect and support their decisions cross-functionally. Demonstrating a personal understanding of our organizational objectives, and how the specific work you are directing is the most valuable investment to help achieve those within your scope of ownership. - Directly oversee and guide the Data and Clinical Integration teams, providing consistent, constructive feedback and conducting performance reviews to foster professional growth. - You know what the difference between good and great performance looks like and you know how to get that from your team members, including when to challenge, redirect, manage up and or out. - You know when and how to advocate for new team members or missing skillsets that would help the department accomplish more. - Actively participate in the recruitment, interviewing, and retention of top-tier engineering talent, and collaborate with other people managers to nurture team engagement and company culture. - Champion the adoption of modern, AI-assisted engineering practices across both teams by evaluating new tools, setting responsible-use guardrails (especially around PHI), and continuously raising the bar on productivity and quality. - Working with engineering and product leadership, refine and execute the technical strategy for converting EHR clinical data into trustworthy, query-ready data that measurably demonstrates health outcomes. - Manage shared roadmaps and dependencies between the two teams, given that Integrations owns the first step of the clinical data pipeline that Data builds upon. - Partner with Product to scale insight generation from our clinical data — combining AI/ML approaches with human analysis — while keeping it trustworthy and compliant. - Remain close to the solutions and, when necessary, play a hands-on role helping to communicate via prototypes, or vibe-coded example applications, answer key questions via SQL or other technical tools. - Stay abreast of emerging technologies and industry trends and advocate for best practices in the department; review and collaborate with engineers on technical specifications to ensure excellence in execution. - Work closely with Product and Design to conceptualize and define impactful solutions, often through Product Requirements Documents (PRDs). - Skillfully lead and facilitate team rituals such as Kickoffs, Retrospectives, and Tech Debt Reviews, and collaborate cross-functionally to understand estimates and prioritize the backlog, making pragmatic trade-offs. - Develop processes, tools, and systems that enhance the departments' overall effectiveness. - Contribute to the team by participating in the On-Call (PagerDuty) rotation. WITHIN 1 MONTH YOU'LL: - Gain a foundational understanding of our product, customers, and patients. - Meet key internal stakeholders and begin to understand policies and protocols (including our Security and Compliance posture). - Establish rapport with the engineers on both teams through Wiki contributions, 1:1s, and team rituals as well as with key peer collaborators (e.g. Product) - Develop a working understanding of the clinical data pipeline — from EHR integration through the medallion architecture and reporting. WITHIN 3 MONTHS YOU'LL: - Complete a product demo, demonstrating your comprehension of our overall product platform. - Gain a strong understanding of our technical environment and identify areas for growth in our processes, systems, and/or tooling. - Take over responsibility for performance management and feedback for the engineers you oversee. - Have a clear, shared roadmap across the Data and Clinical Integration teams, with healthy dependency management between them. - Have implemented at least one improvement that impacts the way all of Engineering operates. WITHIN 6 MONTHS YOU'LL: - Display strong leadership across both teams and within engineering management as a whole. - Have a deep understanding of our data platform and clinical integration landscape, and refine the technical roadmap and sequencing to meet our long-term data goals while ensuring compliance with all necessary requirements. - Work with engineering leadership to recruit and hire best-in-class engineers as needed. - Make contributions to processes, tooling, or technology that impact the way the company operates. If you are US-based, a note about visas: At this time, we are not able to sponsor work visas. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without sponsorship. CORE VALUES At CareMessage, we seek individuals who align with our values of Collaboration, Action, Results, and Empathy. Our ideal candidates embody these principles in their day-to-day work, whether through mentorship, onboarding support for new team members, or taking on initiatives that drive our mission forward. COMPENSATION DETAILS This role is currently set at an L3 Manager level, equivalent to someone who has held two or more engineering management roles with related experience and is extremely proficient in their craft. Our salary allocation for this role is $199,000. We believe in equal work for equal pay. All team members performing the same role at the same level are paid the same regardless of where they are in the world. Note: If you don't fit this description perfectly (especially if you come from an under-represented group) but have held an Integration and Data Engineering Manager role in the past, please apply! _____________________________________ WHAT WE OFFER We take care of our employees by being intentional in our compensation and benefits offerings. ON COMPENSATION - We believe in equal work for equal pay: all team members performing the same role at the same level are paid similarly, regardless of where they are in the world - Paid parental leave for biological and adopted children ON TAKING TIME TO RECHARGE - 18 paid company holidays, including a one week mid-year and one week end-of-year break - 9 wellness days to be used for self-care- or anything that comes up in life - 15 days of PTO - 1-month (20 working days) paid sabbatical after the 4-year anniversary, and every 4 years thereafter ON HEALTH, WELLNESS, AND OTHER BENEFITS - Generous medical, dental, and vision insurance for employees and their families - Health Savings Accounts and Flexible Spending Accounts - Short & long-term disability insurance - $100 per employee yearly wellness budget, with flexibility to spend on physical, emotional, and mental wellness resources - PerkSpot: Instant access to discounts on products & services from hundreds of vendors ______ As a healthcare technology company, we love innovation, and AI can be a great assistant but you are the main event in this interview process. While we recognize AI as a valuable tool and encourage thoughtful use, over-reliance on it may not truly reflect your unique strengths. Our interview process is designed to assess individual skills, critical thinking, and problem-solving abilities. We encourage candidates to ensure their work reflects their own experiences and approach. title: Chief Product and Technology Officer
descriptionText: ABOUT CAREMESSAGE CareMessage is a social enterprise and the largest patient engagement platform for low-income populations in the United States. If this sounds like you, we would love to meet you. _____________________________________ ABOUT THE ROLE CareMessage is seeking a Chief Product and Technology Officer who will decide where we place our product and technology bets, build the organization that delivers them, and prove that what we ship changes people’s health. Product management, product marketing, design, engineering, data and user research all report to this role, which replaces our outgoing Chief Technology Officer. We are a product-driven organization and have been since 2012. That describes how we decide, not whose work matters. Our engineering team built a platform that reaches millions of people reliably, integrates with the electronic health records our customers already use, and put an AI Assistant in the hands of frontline staff who kept using it. Three patents and 17 peer-reviewed studies sit behind our outcomes. The next build is harder, and you will need to be as serious about engineering as about product. The test of this seat is whether our strategy looks different because you are in it. You set the bets, how the organization is built to deliver them, and what we stop doing to make room. The Founders, in consultation with the Board, remain the authority on our mission, our values, and what health equity impact means here. Within that, the direction is yours. Other organizations leave the safety net as they scale. We go deeper into it. Our core operations are funded by our enterprise product, and philanthropy funds research into what comes next. Growing the core is what earns us the right to make bigger bets. More than anything, we want curiosity as a practice. Go find out. Be wrong out loud. Let what a clinic staff member tells you change your plan. The people we serve may be working two jobs, sharing a phone, or reading most easily in a language other than English. We can teach you this market. We cannot teach you to want to understand people whose lives look different from your own. WHAT YOU WILL DO A. BUILD THE ORGANIZATION’S CAPABILITIES TO DELIVER HEALTH EQUITY IMPACT THROUGH TECHNOLOGY 1. Lead, coach and develop 30+ people across product management, product marketing, design, software engineering, data, and user research, and grow those teams so they more directly own key outcomes that support how our organization intends to grow. Build the bench and succession beneath you so our capability outlasts any one leader. 2. Accelerate our organizational ability to deliver health equity impact. We were an early adopter of generative artificial intelligence and our AI Assistant is live and widely used by frontline staff. The larger opportunity is what this organization can achieve when we adapt innovative technologies both in our products and within our internal teams, so that we scale our impact without scaling our cost base proportionally. 3. Leverage our Board, advisors, and broader ecosystem as core enablers and force-multipliers. Tapping into their deep line of sight across healthcare and tech ensures we lock onto the highest-impact focus areas with speed. B. DECIDE WHERE CAREMESSAGE PLACES THE PRODUCT AND TECHNOLOGY BETS THAT MAXIMIZE IMPACT ON HEALTH EQUITY - Set the direction across access to care, clinical outcomes and the social drivers of health, toward demonstrating 5 million people had a measurable health equity improvement a year by 2028. Set the technical direction that delivers on this, grounding everything you do in what you learn from patients and safety-net staff, not in a playbook you brought with you. - Decide how we allocate. Every invested dollar lands in one of three places. Work that moves health equity outcomes, work that keeps us competitive in a crowded market and maintenance, and technical debt that keeps the platform standing. Push as much as you can into the first without letting the other two decay, and be plain with the Executive Team about what the split is and why you chose it. Deciding what we will not pursue is part of the same call. We hold several hypotheses about how to scale our impact, and the discipline is to test them without risking what funds us. - Related to the above, grow the enterprise product that funds our core operations and reaches our target populations at scale, and find the room that remains in the healthcare safety-net market. Our model is that philanthropy invents a capability and earned revenue keeps it, so deciding what has proven itself and is ready to graduate into the Core is part of this job. C. PROVE OUR PRODUCTS MEANINGFULLY SOLVE FOR HEALTH EQUITY OUTCOMES AND MAXIMIZE THEIR REACH 1. Own adoption. We serve 1 in 6 FQHCs and 1 in 7 Free and Charitable Clinics, alongside Tribal health organizations and their networks. But a signed contract is not an outcome because real impact requires active usage. Resource-constrained clinics will not adopt software just because it is good. Your job is to convert one-time campaigns into self-sustaining workflows and build low-touch paths so the smallest organizations succeed independently. Partnering with our Chief Growth Officer on pricing, packaging, and positioning, you will ensure no segment is left behind by balancing commercial growth with mission impact. 2. Own our intellectual property. Our core IP is behavior change, backed by patents on sequential messaging and 17 peer-reviewed studies. This makes us the only patient engagement platform with published clinical outcomes for low-income populations. You will direct our IP strategy: deciding what we protect, what we publish, and how we generate clinical evidence far faster than traditional trial cycles allow. 3. Own the technical partnerships and infrastructure. Patients navigate clinics, food banks, and housing programs that operate in silos. We build the connective tissue through deep EHR integrations, a unified cross-organization patient record, and scalable APIs that let new partners plug in without custom code. You will own our technical partner relationships and the underlying infrastructure that connects the safety net. WHAT YOU WILL ACHIEVE WITHIN 30 DAYS: BUILD A FIRST-HAND POINT OF VIEW ON HOW WE HAVE CHOSEN OUR ORGANIZATIONAL BETS 1. Build a durable practice for staying close to our users and use it immediately. By day 30 we expect you to name at least one assumption in our current plan that your own first-hand learning has already changed. 2. Deliver an honest read on the product and engineering organization: where the talent and leadership gaps sit, where the risks are, and what you would do about them in the next 60 days. 3. Build a working command of our strategy, our financial picture, and how enterprise product revenue funds our operations. WITHIN 60 DAYS: SET THE DIRECTION AND COMMIT THE ORGANIZATION TO IT 1. Deliver a first draft of the product and technology strategy to the CEO and Executive Team naming the bets worth making, the sequence, what we will decline to build, and how the stretch bets get tested without risking the Core. 2. Deliver a candid diagnostic of the product, the technical debt, and the organization's capacity to deliver against that strategy. 3. Agree with the Chief Growth Officer on one experiment in pricing, packaging or adoption that tests where room remains in the safety-net market. WITHIN 90 DAYS: DEVELOP A PLAN TO SUPPORT THE ORGANIZATION’S APPROACH TO TECHNOLOGY FOR HEALTH EQUITY 1. Move the direction from a document to a commitment: the bets funded and sequenced through 2027, a named owner against each, and the tradeoffs the Executive Team has accepted. By day 90, this organization should know what it is building, what it is not, and who is accountable. 2. Deliver a plan to accelerate how the team uses artificial intelligence and to strengthen technical leadership in the function, naming the gaps and how you will close them. 3. Outline your reasoning behind the two or three external technical/infrastructure partnerships most worth pursuing and/or deepening against our outcomes trajectory, and your plan to pursue/deepen them. KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS FOR THIS ROLE MAY INCLUDE: 1. Health equity outcomes we can prove at scale, meaning measurable clinical and social outcomes attributable to our products. 2. Adoption and reach among safety-net organizations with limited capacity to adopt anything, including a viable low-touch path for the smallest organizations, and the health of the enterprise product that funds our operations. 3. Organizational leverage, meaning the impact we produce per person and per dollar as we grow. We intend to scale what we deliver without scaling our cost base proportionally, and that depends on how well this organization uses technology internally rather than only inside product and engineering. Delivering at one to two dollars per patient per year is the standard we hold ourselves to, and the health and retention of the team that makes it possible is part of the same measure. WHAT YOU WILL BRING 1. You have run multiple functions together, and you can point to outcomes you owned rather than features your team shipped. You have set a direction an organization followed, presented to a board, and built people who went on to bigger jobs. 2. You have changed an engineering organization's technical direction without authority over it, and you can explain the argument well enough for an engineer to judge it. This one is not negotiable. 3. You are curious as a practice. You go find out. You are willing to be wrong out loud. Your view of patients and frontline staff came from being around them. 4. You want to go deeper into the safety net, not upmarket. Most product leaders build a career moving toward better-funded customers. This job runs the other way, and it will not suit someone who sees low-income populations as a stage. 5. title: Chief Technology Officer
descriptionText: GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We support high ownership and real professional growth. Curious about what it's really like to work here? Read our values and hear from the people who do. If they resonate, this could be a great fit! Priority application deadline: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Early applications are heavily encouraged. We’re growing at incredible speed, and expect to hit $1B in revenue in 2026 with significant growth forecast for 2027. We’re hiring a Chief Technology Officer to lead the building and rebuilding of the technology, systems and ways of working that will enable a sustained $5B+ p/a operation. You will build software that safely and securely moves billions of dollars to millions of vulnerable people in some of the poorest and highest need parts of the world. This will require applying excellent engineering, team building and organizational judgment to complex, high-stakes operations: identity and fraud management, machine learning on large but imperfect datasets (cell phone data, satellite imagery, government registries), mobile money integrations, low-connectivity environments, rapidly evolving requirements all in diverse regulatory environments and country contexts. You’ll need to keep our legacy technology stack stable and performant, while in parallel building new systems from the ground up for our next level of scale. You will lead engineering, data, security and enterprise technology – with a small, mighty and rapidly growing engineering team of ~15, and the expectation that this can at least double to ~30 in the next 12 months if you want it to. You’ll report to a CEO with deep experience running technology companies, and partner with our VP Product. This role is remote, with working hours between US Eastern Time and East African Time, and some preference for candidates in our office hubs of New York, London, or Nairobi. What we’re looking for: An exceptional hirer, manager and organizer of technical talent. Proven record identifying, hiring, developing and retaining excellent engineers and engineering leaders, and creating team processes that consistently deliver software with quality and velocity. Deep technical judgment, applied close to the work. You can evaluate major designs, pressure-test architecture and build-vs-buy decisions, and recognize when a team is heading the wrong way, without becoming the primary implementer. Low-ego: you’ll investigate a problem yourself when that’s what the situation requires. Business judgment and decisiveness under ambiguity. You’re not just a technical leader, you’re also a business executive. You understand the business, are a strong cross-functional partner, and have a history of good judgment when navigating tradeoffs of long vs. short term, speed, reliability, security, flexibility, cost, technical quality, and user impact. AI first. You have a point of view on where AI meaningfully changes engineering productivity and organizational capability, and you’ve moved a team from experimentation to real, measured use. You can set the tools, culture, goals, and guardrails that leverage the opportunities and mitigate the risks of an AI first engineering culture. Embody and set an example for GD values. We take our values incredibly seriously, and expect our leaders to embody, nurture, and promote them in the way they work and the teams they build. Advantages, not requirements. Experience in an operationally complex or regulated domain (fintech, payments, humanitarian response, global development); systems involving financial controls, fraud risk, identity, or sensitive recipient data; operating across multiple countries, particularly lower-income or infrastructure-constrained ones; leading both modern product engineering and enterprise technology. What you’ll do Define our technology vision and target stack. Own the technical strategy for technology-first delivery at $5B+/year: architecture, platforms, build-vs-buy, and what we retire. Work with executive, product, finance, risk, and data leaders to turn program and product strategy into a sequenced, credible portfolio of technical investments. Balance a demanding portfolio. You'll manage six workstreams that all matter and won't all move at once: (1) building our new cash delivery stack (remote-first verification, fraud prevention, massive volume) (2) stabilizing our legacy stack until switchover, then managing the migration; (3) donor-facing fundraising products; (4) our global emergency cash system (and eventual white-labelling of that product); (5) enterprise technology; (6) internal tooling, platform, and cybersecurity. Deciding sequencing and staffing across these (and saying "not yet" credibly) is the job. Build and grow an exceptional technology organization. Recruit outstanding engineering and technology talent, design the org GiveDirectly needs at its next stage of scale (engineering, product, data, security, infrastructure, enterprise systems), and create the accountability, decision rights, and career paths to sustain high talent density. Grow the engineering team from 15 to ~30 with a lean but durable management structure. Own the technical direction and quality bar. Guide consequential decisions on integrations, data, security, reliability, and technical debt. Ensure our systems can safely support a major increase in transaction volume, geographic reach, and organizational dependence on technology. Set a pragmatic quality bar appropriate to high-stakes financial delivery while preserving speed. Lead across organizational boundaries. Serve as a member of GiveDirectly’s executive team, reporting to the CEO and bringing technology into major strategic and operating decisions. Help non-technical leaders understand technical constraints and costs, build credibility with country and functional leaders by understanding their realities, and force clarity when priorities, ownership, or tradeoffs are ambiguous. Travel. Approximately 4–6 trips per year, including visits to GiveDirectly countries of operation. Compensation At GiveDirectly, we strive to pay our employees generously and equitably. We use an accredited third party salary aggregator to calculate what we believe to be competitive pay based on role, location, and cost of living. We also have a no negotiation policy so pay is consistent across comparable roles. title: Country Director, Uganda
descriptionText: GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. Location: This role must be based in Kampala. About GiveDirectly Uganda Since 2013, we've delivered over $94M directly to more than 120,000 people across more than 16 districts in Uganda, including long-term self-reliance programs for refugees, poverty relief projects in Karamoja and other districts, and anticipatory cash ahead of climate-related disasters. We've proven the model. Now we're ready to go much bigger. Over the next few years, our ambition for Uganda is to dramatically scale transfer volume—reaching thousands more recipients—while building the efficiency to do it sustainably. This isn't incremental growth. It's a step-change in what's possible, and we're hiring the person who will lead it. This person will also lead a talented team deeply committed to the communities they work in and to helping more households move out of poverty. The role The Country Director is the most senior GiveDirectly presence in Uganda, with full accountability for the country office: programs, operations, external relations, team, and strategy. Most of the job is delivery. You own whether transfers go out on time, at target cost, and at GD's quality bar, and whether that holds as volume grows. The rest of the job exists to protect and extend that: controls that keep money and recipients safe as the operation gets bigger, a team that can execute, partnerships that lower our cost or widen our reach, and a strategy that concentrates effort on what actually moves impact. What you'll own Program management Accountable for GD Uganda's programs running on time, at target efficiency, and at GD's quality standards: Own the delivery plan: Drive operational excellence across all Uganda programs through a comprehensive project management plan. Own the KPIs: Throughput, cost per recipient, payment success/error rates, recipient experience, and enrollment-to-payment cycle time. Fix problems at the root: Diagnose delivery issues structurally—redesign processes, staffing models, or systems rather than managing by escalation. Be a thought partner: Provide analytical support to help the team clear execution bottlenecks. Build for scale: Design the operation needed for the next order of magnitude, not just the one that exists today. Steward the budget: Manage country spend to maximize the ratio of donor funds converted into transfers. Manage risk: Identify, evaluate, and mitigate strategic and operational risks across programs. Risk, safeguarding, and integrity Delivering cash creates real risk, and it scales with volume. Every new district, partner, and payment channel is a new surface for fraud, exclusion error, and harm to recipients. We expect the Country Director to own that exposure personally, not to delegate it to a committee. Own fraud and safeguarding outcomes for the country office: design the prevention controls, monitor the leading indicators, and act on what they tell you before problems compound. Set a culture where staff and recipients report concerns and trust that something happens when they do, including accessible recipient feedback and grievance channels. Chair the country's internal audit, safeguarding, and program coordination forums, and partner closely with GD's global internal audit, compliance, finance, and safeguarding teams. Provide leadership and oversight of investigations into alleged misconduct, and handle disciplinary outcomes with zero tolerance for fraud or safeguarding violations. Ensure country compliance with global standards, and translate global policy into protocols that make sense in the Ugandan context. Team management Lead a large team across programs, field operations, finance, HR, procurement, internal audit, and safeguarding, directly managing the country management team. Build managers who can run their own functions: clear expectations, real feedback, visible growth paths. Lead workforce planning and succession, keeping the team lean as the operation grows. Set the tone on GD's values. Partnerships and government relations Own GD's relationship with the Government of Uganda, line ministries, district authorities, and the government-led social protection and relief programs we coordinate with. Secure and maintain the government permissions that programs depend on at the national and district levels. Build and deepen the commercial and delivery partnerships that improve impact per dollar: mobile network operators and payment providers, data and identity systems, and implementing or referral partners who extend our reach. Represent GiveDirectly publicly in Uganda, to government, media, and the sector. Steward existing donor relationships and host funder and partner visits to the field, working with GD's global fundraising team, which leads donor sourcing and proposal development. Shape ambitious program designs and budgets that global fundraising can take to funders. Strategic planning Lead vision-setting and strategic planning for the Uganda country office. Set country operational and revenue goals and create a roadmap for success. Make and defend hard deprioritization calls. Bring Uganda's perspective into GD's global strategy, policy, and cross-country planning. What you'll bring We're looking for an experienced operator who has led complex delivery at scale, knows the operation through its numbers, and has built the systems, teams, and controls it takes to grow. The core of what we're looking for: 5–10 years of experience in a similar role or function. People management experience (experience hiring and building a team preferred). Strong relationship management, including hands-on experience engaging government at national or district level, not necessarily as the principal. Exceptional communication skills: speaking, writing, presenting, and negotiating, especially with senior audiences and funders. Outstanding project management skills. Analytical problem solver: you approach problems with an analytical, iterative mindset and a strong prioritization framework. You can run robust analyses to inform management and programming decisions. Enthusiasm for fast-paced environments, which may lack a predefined playbook for success and involve significant “learning by doing.” Experience in partnerships and business development. Strong alignment with GD values. Strongly desired Experience working in Sub-Saharan Africa and fluency in the operating context. Compensation At GiveDirectly, we strive to pay our employees generously and equitably. We use an accredited third party salary aggregator to calculate what we believe to be competitive pay based on role, location, and cost of living. We also have a no negotiation policy to ensure we are paying staff equitably across roles. Read more about our compensation philosophy here. descriptionText: GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. About this Role We are currently planning for a significant increase in scale, and we are building the People function that can carry it. This is a new role with two halves. First half: you will be the dedicated people partner to our Global Shared Services (GSS) teams [~200 employees], who do not have one today, working primarily with people leaders on structure, workforce planning, talent, and the people decisions that come with growth. You will partner with and coach senior leaders across GSS, up to VP level, including those who are strong operators still growing as people leaders. Second half: you will build how we handle behavior and performance concerns across the organization: the standards, the decision framework, and the enablement that lets people managers and our HR teams in the field handle them well. The first year is weighted toward that build, with partnering also focused on performance and talent management as the most pressing needs. As the standards land, the balance shifts toward deeper partnering, while you continue to own the employee relations model. The reason for this weight: the employee relations build is our most acute gap today, but should not be construed as a ceiling of the job. Over time, the partnering half opens up well beyond performance and conduct into org design, workforce planning, talent, career development, and the full range of people strategy for our global functions. We're hiring a broad, senior people partner who can build the ER model as their first major deliverable, not an employee relations specialist. If your instinct on reading this is that the ER work is the whole job, this role probably isn't the right fit, and the reverse is also true: if you're only interested in the strategic partnering and not the build, year one will frustrate you. Job type: Full-time Reports to: Head of People Level: Director Location: Remote, with a requirement to overlap with an East Africa timezone by at least 3 hours, and meaningful overlap with US Eastern hours. We can only employ people in certain places at the moment, so it's worth checking our current list of eligible countries to see if yours is included. If you're based elsewhere, it's not an automatic no, but do flag it early with your recruiter. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas in the U.S. or U.K. at this time. Travel: Approximately 3-4 trips per year, including at least one to a country of operation and one to a key in-person leadership moment, with occasional additional travel as sensitive or time-critical situations require. What you'll do Partner with our Global team: Act as the trusted advisor to GSS leaders (managers up to VPs) on anything involving their people: how their teams are structured, who they need, who is at risk, and what is not working. Some of this is work the Head of People holds today and will hand over as you establish credibility. Lead org design and workforce planning for global functions as we scale: structure, role definition, levels, sizing and sequencing, in partnership with function leads, Finance and Talent Acquisition. Own talent and succession for the population: who is ready for more, who is a flight risk, and where the single points of failure sit. Partner on performance and compensation decisions for global staff, including calibration, promotion cases and band placement. Coach senior leaders, on their own leadership as much as on their teams. Lead people-side change for global functions: restructures, leadership transitions, and the team-level fallout of both. Act as the People representative for global staff, holding employment decisions within our framework in the way HR Managers do in their countries. Coach global managers through behavior and performance conversations, rather than taking those conversations from them. Build how we handle behavior and underperformance: Define what these categories actually are and communicate them across the organization, so that a concern can be routed rather than defaulting into a disciplinary process. Audit how each country handles cases end to end, and write one global standard per category covering intake, escalation, who is responsible at each stage, and documentation. Build from what already works and flex only where local law genuinely requires it. Build the employment decision framework with Legal, including a delegated authority matrix setting out who decides what and when, and the escalation route when a case falls outside it. Design and deliver enablement for the three groups who have to use all of this: managers, HR Managers, and staff. Work with our central investigations function to stand up a single record of outcomes, so that patterns and inconsistencies become visible. Within your first 90 days, recommend who should support behavior and underperformance cases in each country, and what that requires. Hold consistency across the organization: Coach HR Managers through cases in their countries, and act as the technical escalation point when they need one. Provide the People input at triage on which category a concern belongs in. Watch outcomes as they accumulate, and raise it when something looks inconsistent: comparable facts resolving differently, one country diverging, or a pattern clustering around a team or a manager. What this role is not: Not an investigations role. Misconduct investigations sit with our Central Intake and Investigations Hub. We would want you to have investigative capability we can draw on for surge, or for cases where the hub is conflicted, but it is not the job and someone who wants to investigate will be frustrated here. Not a caseload role. Cases in country belong to managers and to HR Managers. Your value is standards, judgment and partnership, not throughput. You define what managers need to know about employee relations; they own the curriculum and the channel. An organization that was growing fast, restructuring, or both, where the systems you needed did not exist and you built them while the volume was already arriving. title: Risk Management Program Manager (DRC)
descriptionText: GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. About this role The Risk Management Program Manager is responsible for preventing, detecting, mitigating and investigating the field-based risks associated with delivering millions of dollars to thousands of poor households across a portfolio of countries. The Program Manager (PM) will work with the Internal Audit Director and the wider Internal Audit team to design innovations to manage the risks associated with cash transfers. Reports to: Director, Internal Audit Level: Manager Location: Remote - Goma/Bukavu/Kinshasa, DRC with a requirement to overlap with an East Africa timezone by at least 3 hours. Role Summary Supports overall Global Internal Audit (IA) strategy. Overall risk manager for the countries in their portfolio. In partnership with the Country Director (CD), lead the development of the country IA strategy. Supports on all project design at all stages (project inception, proposal creation, project design, risk register creation, ongoing project risk management, project closure). Leads (or where relevant, delegates) all country syncs with CD. HR oversight (not direct management) for all countries in their portfolio. Takes direct lead on certain, more sensitive and high risk investigations in portfolio (as determined by CD and IAD). Manages Internal Audit for each country in their portfolio Manages Internal Audit Manager (IAM) directly. Supports admin oversight and procurement for the IA team in country (ensuring docs are in order etc). Carries out regular spot checks on country operations and ensures IAM is doing their checks and documenting them. Seeks to develop and analyze data we have but also look for new ways to spot and reduce fraud. Visible point of contact for country team and part of country management team where relevant. Leads coordination with other internal teams (such as Safeguarding, Programs, and Tech) as well as external partners, such as Telcos where needed. Visits each country in portfolio at least 1x per year for field visits. Roles and responsibilities: Project Design (25%) Represent IA in country project design conversations, including development of strategic risk management measures. Owning development of project-specific Internal Audit proposals detailing audit rates, audit approaches, e.t.c. for new projects and discussing these with CD. Oversee community risk scoping exercises and ensure full scoping report is submitted to IAD and CDs for all new projects. Ensure that customized risk registers are created for all new projects; ensure that risk registers for ongoing projects are updated regularly. Review implementation tools, e.g. enrollment surveys, to better align them to risk detection, mitigation and prevention. Systems Orientated risk monitoring (45%) Owning and monitoring IA metrics / KPIs in countries of portfolio and owning correction of dropping or critically missed metrics. Overall owner (accountable) of country project workbooks detailing workplans and staffing, tech related requirements and activity timelines. Define and review risk classifications based on projects and country level activities. Hold weekly (or bi-weekly) meetings with Country Directors in each country you are assigned. Lead the development of escalation protocols for different types of risks and monitor implementation of the protocols by country managers. Lead the transparent, accountable and where needed collaborative investigation of high risk cases. Support the IAM to undertake community based fraud intelligence monitoring exercises and escalate any identified risk trends to the CD and IAD. Monitor the traffic and trends of risk reporting and flag high risk countries and projects to the CD and IAD. Support the IAD with tech-related fraud prevention innovations work through different inputs as may be requested from time to time. Where relevant, build in-country relationships with fraud management stakeholders (for example, MoMo provider telcos) for sustainable fraud resolutions in-country. Conduct spot checks on both the programs and IA operations to ensure high quality and identify any abnormalities. Build and manage in-country project related stakeholder relationships; working with different in-country teams to ensure IA deliverables are tracked as per workplan. Write and share with the IA - Director, quarterly productivity reports and/or project specific retrospectives (or progress reports). People Management (10%) Directly manages Internal Audit Managers in all countries you are assigned. Conduct regular check-ins with Direct Reports. Conduct performance reviews for direct reports every quarter and provide a report of the same to the IA-Director and CD where relevant. Indirectly support the AFMs and FOs in the countries you are assigned. Develop a team with a high capacity for problem solving, critical thinking, and strong analytical and communication skill. Conduct regular skip-level meetings with AFMs. Hiring: Directly responsible for hiring IAMs in the countries you are assigned. Create a strong overall team Manage conflicts and other risks within the team and escalate where appropriate. Promote effective team culture by encouraging recognition of positive achievements and other team-building initiatives. Model ethical behavior that encourages the team to report misconduct within GD staff, partners, community and recipients. Conduct staff career growth needs assessments (through structures surveys and 1:1 sessions) and liaise with the HR manager to deliver robust professional development sessions internally and externally. Culture Building (10%) Act as the custodian of ‘Recipients First’ Value within the team by ensuring compliance to policies and protocols of GiveDirectly. Maintain an active, visible and consistent commitment to a common standard of behavior that is required throughout every aspect of the organization as stipulated in the Code of Conduct Statement. Manage a team that is driven by individual accountability involving moving beyond corporate ‘rules-based’ behavior to ‘values-based’ behavior that promotes a greater focus on promoting individual integrity.” Identify sub-cultures within the organization that may result in safeguarding and fraud risks to recipients. Conduct annual training to country Programs teams on fraud and safeguarding mitigation requirements as outlined in GD policies. Other responsibilities (10%) Supports Director on reflecting on and rethinking the Global IA strategy and mandate. Supports Director on utilizing AI and technology to improve GD’s fraud risk management systems. Participates in weekly IA management meetings and weekly sprints to discuss cross-team activities. Support on country external audits where requested. Support on non-field based fraud management on an as-needed basis in your countries of operation. Proactively identify and flag ways to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of IA’s operations. Support other country of operations outside of portfolio where necessary. What you’ll bring: Internal audit / risk management background - 3+ years leading audit, compliance, or risk functions, ideally in a role that combined strategy design with hands-on fieldwork (not just desk audits). Fraud investigation experience - has personally led or overseen sensitive/high-risk investigations, not just routine checks. People management - directly managed a team, including hiring, performance reviews, and conflict management. Cross-country or multi-site portfolio experience - managed risk/audit across several countries or regional units simultaneously, since this role owns a country portfolio. Field-based operations exposure - comfortable with in-person field visits (at least 1x/year per country) in low-resource or humanitarian/development settings, not purely office-based audit work. Stakeholder management - experience liaising with external partners and internal cross-functional teams (Safeguarding, Programs, Tech). Data/analytics fluency - experience using data to detect fraud trends, build KPIs/metrics, and monitor risk reporting, plus openness to AI/tech-driven fraud prevention tools. Program/project design experience - has contributed to project design, risk registers, and proposal creation, ideally in an NGO, cash-transfer, or development-sector context. Report writing at a senior level - track record producing strategy documents, quarterly reports, and retrospectives for leadership. Fluency in both English and French. Alignment with GiveDirectly Values and active demonstration of our core competencies: emotional intelligence, problem solving, project management, follow-through, and fostering inclusivity. Why work at GiveDirectly? At GiveDirectly, we work to ensure that you have everything you need to excel in your role and on your team, including: A positive and supportive team with opportunities for advancement A demonstrated commitment to helping all staff develop and grow A competitive salary, including bonus A robust health benefits plan (exact details will vary by country) Unlimited PTO (that we encourage staff to take!) Read more about our ongoing diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts here and about our decision to move our central support teams to remote first here. Compensation At GiveDirectly, we strive to pay our employees generously and equitably. We use an accredited third party salary aggregator to calculate what we believe to be competitive pay based on role, location, and cost of living. We also have a no negotiation policy to ensure we are paying staff equitably across roles. Read more about our compensation philosophy here. Unless otherwise noted, the benefits stipend may be used to cover benefits or taken as additional taxable income. At Code for America, you contribute to exciting work while learning and developing in a supportive and flexible environment. Code for America is looking for a talented Director of Delivery Operations who will establish and embed the delivery practices, standards, and governance mechanisms that build on existing best practices while enabling our teams to execute with consistency and confidence across a growing portfolio of government-facing projects — from kick-off through to successful project completion. About the role: Code for America works across a portfolio of complex, high-stakes projects — from products to technology-enabled advisory services — all aimed at helping millions of people access critical government benefits and services. As our portfolio grows and the demands on our government partners intensify, the consistency and discipline of how we deliver matters as much as what we deliver. The Director of Delivery Operations will build and steward the systems, standards, and practices that make our project delivery excellent and repeatable. This is an internal-facing, enabling role: you won't manage individual projects directly, but you'll shape how every Safety Net advisory project runs — from the moment a partnership is handed off from cultivation through to project close. You'll work closely with Program Directors, Project Sponsors, and key project and discipline leaders to embed practical delivery practices into day-to-day work, and you'll partner with senior program leadership to ensure our operating model stays grounded in what actually works in the field. This is a new role at Code for America, and the person who takes it on will have real strategic ownership — setting the priorities for how we invest in delivery infrastructure, making deliberate tradeoffs about where to standardize versus where to leave room for project-specific judgment, and bringing the best of delivery practice, AI-enabled tools and capabilities, and human-centered approaches to improving government services to keep Code for America at the leading edge of how this work gets done. This role will report to the Senior Director of Safety Net and is expected to travel no more than 15% of the time. Code for America is based in California and can employ those who reside full-time within the United States. This is a remote position. This role may eventually support in growing out a team, adopting direct reports as management needs evolve. Provide day-to-day support to project leaders to ensure delivery standards are understood and consistently applied across their projects Roll out training, tools & resources, and onboarding support to build project management capability across program teams Drive adoption of delivery standards through intentional change management — not just defining the practices, but creating the conditions for people to use them consistently Anticipate any resistance to new delivery practices before it surfaces, and work to understand and address it proactively, rather than waiting for adoption to stall Design and facilitate feedback loops — through quality assurance reviews, retrospectives, and structured check-ins — that surface what's working and what needs to evolve Identify patterns across projects (recurring risks, scope issues, handoff breakdowns) and translate them into updated guidance and coaching Project Support & Scope Management Ensure strong communication and feedback loops with project teams to track delivery effectiveness, surface emerging risks, and provide hands-on support when projects need to course-correct from a project management perspective. Support scope revision processes from a project management perspective, helping teams manage and reset expectations in a structured way — partnering closely with leaders across disciplines throughout. Partner with the Partnerships team to ensure smooth handoffs at the transition from cultivation to delivery, with clear shared accountability and no loss of critical context. Governance & Portfolio Visibility Continually assess effectiveness and efficiency of existing and new governance mechanisms, including regular project check-ins, reporting, and communication processes that give senior leadership timely visibility into project status, risks, and delivery effectiveness across the portfolio. Recommend and implement changes to improve them. Track adoption of delivery standards across projects and flag gaps proactively Support Program Directors in preparing for project reviews and escalations with consistent, well-structured information Partner with senior program leadership to ensure delivery operations stay aligned with evolving program priorities and organizational strategy Anticipate systemic challenges across the portfolio before they become blockers, and develop solutions that address root causes rather than individual project symptoms Other duties as assigned Engage in ad hoc projects and initiatives as required by the organization's evolving needs. title: Senior Technical Program Manager - Pricing and Manufacturability
descriptionText: Xometry (NASDAQ: XMTR) powers the industries of today and tomorrow by connecting the people with big ideas to the manufacturers who can bring them to life. Xometry’s digital marketplace gives manufacturers the critical resources they need to grow their business while also making it easy for buyers at Fortune 1000 companies to tap into global manufacturing capacity. Role Overview As the first individual-contributor hire in our nascent TPM organization, you will set the bar for program excellence across Product & Technology. You will architect, run, and continuously improve the operational frameworks that keep our highest-value initiatives on track from roadmap definition and cross-team execution to release management and post-launch optimization. Partnering closely with Engineering, Product, Design, Data Science / ML, and Business Operations, you will both deliver complex programs and shape what it means to be a TPM at the company. Initial Project Xometry’s Instant Quoting platform is the core of how buyers get a price, lead time, and manufacturability signal on a part. Pricing & Manufacturability (P&M) owns the engines and models behind that experience: Auto-Quote pricing and cost, Design for Manufacturability (DFM) / geometry analysis, Drawing AI (CAD and 2D drawing interpretation), and the ML models that predict cost, lead time, and drawing intelligence. The Sr. Technical Program Manager will work with senior leadership, engineering, product, data science, and business teams to deliver these capabilities end to end from model and service work through product integration, operations, and post-launch improvement. That includes coordinating how CAD models and drawings move through geometry, DFM, and Drawing AI services, how ML models are trained, evaluated, productionized, and monitored, and how those outputs show up as price, DFM feedback, and quoting decisions for buyers and staff. This role requires a hybrid schedule (3 days a week) at our North Bethesda, MD or Waltham, MA office location. How You'll Contribute Own end-to-end program management for the Pricing & Manufacturability portfolio, with initial focus on Auto-Quote pricing/cost, DFM, Drawing AI, and related ML model work. Drive program planning from concept through execution and post-launch analysis, including model evaluation, staged rollouts, and production monitoring. Partner with Engineering, Product, Data Science / ML, Operations, Sales, and Finance to set realistic goals, timelines, and milestones across engine, model, and product workstreams. Translate CAD/geometry, DFM, and Drawing AI work into a single sequenced plan clarifying what the models own, what product/UX owns, and where Buyer Experience, Pricing Experience, and P&M must handshake. Implement lightweight, rigorous project management processes that increase execution speed, transparency, and accountability across multi-squad, model-plus-product delivery. Lead risk management and mitigation model quality, data/labeling capacity, service latency, integration dependencies, and go-live readiness so blockers are visible before they slip dates. Collaborate with senior leadership to prioritize initiatives, sequence model vs. product work, and manage stakeholder expectations. Provide clear, concise, actionable communication on progress, risks, model/product trade-offs, and outcomes to executive teams. Drive continuous improvement in execution and process, using quoting, DFM, and model-quality data to inform decisions. Foster a high-performance culture across teams, keeping delivery aligned to company goals in a fast-paced, high-stakes environment. What You'll Bring to Xometry Design and institutionalize lightweight but rigorous operating rhythms (intake, planning, risk management, status reporting, post-mortems) that scale with the business. Drive end-to-end execution of strategic, multi-team programs clarifying scope, aligning stakeholders, forecasting resources, and unblocking delivery. Serve as a senior thought partner to the Director of Technology Operations, codifying TPM best practices, mentoring future hires, and evolving the career ladder for the function. Act as a trusted communications hub, producing crisp executive readouts and facilitating decision-making forums that keep leadership focused on the right trade-offs. Champion continuous improvement by synthesizing lessons learned into updated playbooks, tooling, and training. descriptionText: Senior Architect – Solution Owner AI-native product and delivery leader who owns the throughline from strategy to software delivery to measurable business impact. Facilitating client conversations about AI tooling, delivery approach, and value realization — bringing the data to support investment decisions and communicating tradeoffs to senior stakeholders. Strong executive communication skills — commanding conversations, driving decisions, and tailoring messaging to diverse client stakeholders with a focus on value and business impact. descriptionText: ABOUT RAD AI At Rad AI, we’re on a mission to transform healthcare with artificial intelligence. Founded by a radiologist, our AI-driven solutions are revolutionizing radiology—saving time, reducing burnout, and improving patient care. With one of the largest proprietary radiology report datasets in the world, our AI has helped uncover hundreds of new cancer diagnoses and reduced error rates in tens of millions of radiology reports by nearly 50%. Rad AI has secured over $140M in funding, including a recently oversubscribed Series C ($68M round) led by Transformation Capital, bringing our valuation to $528M. Our investors include Khosla Ventures, World Innovation Lab, Gradient Ventures, Cone Health Ventures, and others—all backing our mission to empower physicians with cutting-edge AI. Our latest advancements in generative AI are used by thousands of radiologists daily, supporting more than one-third of radiology groups and healthcare systems and nearly 50% of all medical imaging in the U.S. at partners including Cone Health, Jefferson Einstein Health, Geisinger, Guthrie Healthcare System, and Henry Ford Health. Recognized as one of the most promising healthcare AI companies by CB Insights and AuntMinnie https://www.radai.com/news/auntminnie-recognizes-rad-ai-omni-reporting-as-2023s-best-new-radiology-software, and ranked by Deloitte https://www2.deloitte.com/us/en/pages/technology-media-and-telecommunications/articles/fast500-winners.html as the 19th fastest-growing company in North America, we are building AI-powered solutions that make a real impact. Most recently, Rad AI was named to CNBC’s Disruptor 50 https://www.cnbc.com/2025/06/10/2025-cnbc-disruptor-50-see-the-full-list-of-companies.html list, highlighting the innovation and momentum behind our mission. If you’re ready to shape the future of healthcare, we’d love to have you on our team! ABOUT CONTINUITY: Continuity is Rad AI’s care coordination and follow-up product, helping radiology teams make sure important findings do not fall through the cracks. The team builds and operates the applications, APIs, and integrations that turn clinical data into actionable workflows for customers, with a strong emphasis on reliability, scalability, and operational excellence in a sensitive healthcare environment. This work sits at the intersection of product, engineering, implementations, and customer needs, and is central to helping Rad AI deliver measurable value for health systems and radiology practices. WHY JOIN US: We’re seeking a Senior Software Engineer to join our team building the future of radiology. This role will work alongside our high-performing cross-functional team of Full Stack Engineers, ML Engineers, Product Leaders, and various other teams internally and externally to develop this responsive and performant application. WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING: - Develop on large-scale progressive and single page web applications that streamline user workflows and increase their efficiency and effectiveness - Develop our Python, FastAPI backend services including a REST API and ML pipeline services - Build new features that support our rapidly growing number of customers - Write code that meets our internal standards for security, style, maintainability, and best practices for a high-scale HIPAA web environment - Work with Product Management, ML, Data Science, Customer Success and other stakeholders to iterate on new features and address defects - Advocate for improvements to product quality, security, and performance that have impact across your team - Proactively seek out ways to improve our code base and product as a whole through code reviews, design collaboration, and development of strong engineering practices. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR: - Minimum of 5+ years of industry engineering experience with single and multi-tenanted environments - In-depth knowledge of Python and FastAPI, or equivalent modern languages/frameworks - Knowledge of relational and document based databases, as well as other large scale data storage paradigms - Knowledge of modern web architecture and best practices - Experience with unit and integration testing - Experience working on a distributed team and strong version control skills using git - Experience with performance and optimization problems, particularly at large scale, and a demonstrated ability to diagnose and prevent these problems - Experience using AI-assisted development tools and workflows to improve engineering productivity, while maintaining high standards for code quality, reliability, and security. NICE TO HAVES: - Experience with PostgreSQL - Experience with 3rd-party integrations such as Auth0, Amplitude - Experience working at an early-stage startup - Experience in a HIPAA-compliant environment, especially with FHIR and HL7 - Experience working on machine learning Join our world-class team as we build and deploy AI solutions that empower physicians and transform patient care—making a meaningful impact on millions of lives. Driven by our mission, we prioritize transparency, inclusion, and close collaboration, bringing together exceptional people to revolutionize healthcare. If you're passionate about driving innovation and delivering impactful healthcare solutions, we'd love to hear from you! To learn more about what it's like to work at Rad AI, visit https://www.radai.com/life-at-rad-ai and be sure to follow us on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/radai/?utm_campaign=Recruiting_2026&utm_content=recruiting-job-posting-website&utm_source=recru%5B%E2%80%A6%5Db-posting-website to stay up to date! title: Staff Product Manager, Financial Systems
descriptionText: Xometry (NASDAQ: XMTR) powers the industries of today and tomorrow by connecting the people with big ideas to the manufacturers who can bring them to life. Xometry’s digital marketplace gives manufacturers the critical resources they need to grow their business while also making it easy for buyers at Fortune 1000 companies to tap into global manufacturing capacity. Every dollar that moves through Xometry passes through Financial Systems: what a buyer is quoted and invoiced, what a partner is paid and when, what gets disputed, what gets recognized as revenue, and what finally lands in the ledger. As Staff Product Manager for Financial Systems, you will sit at the intersections of the order-to-cash and procure-to-pay lifecycles. You will collaborate with cross functional product teams making Xometry the most dependable marketplace for partners and customers. This is an individual contributor position that requires product manager proficiency and a deep understanding of financial and accounting operational functions and internal control concepts. You will be expected to read a journal entry, trace a transaction through to the general ledger, and understand why a control exists, or doesn’t, before you create a solution. Day to day, you will gather requirements from customers, partners, and our own Accounting team, and translate what you learn into products & features that serve all three. You will translate finance requirements into PRDs that engineers can design and build from. How You'll Contribute: Identify & Prioritize: Identify, define, and prioritize features & product enhancements that matter. You will communicate the value to the organization, and develop the metrics using data that supports the business case. Know the Personas: Develop a deep understanding of finance, procurement and operational persons and their end to end workflows from both the customer and internal accounting teams perspective so that requirements reflect how the work actually gets done from both the Procure to Pay and Order to Cash lenses. Cross Functional Alignment: Act as the hub between Engineering, Finance and Accounting, Sales, Order Operations, Partner Experience, Legal, and Tax, so that launches land with the field ready and users are informed. Own Release Enablement End to End: For every release, you own the communication, documentation, SOPs, and training, and coordinate with Marketing to inform customers and partners. Ensure that the work done turns a deployed feature into an adopted one. Build Controls into the Product: Partner with Accounting, Controllership, Tax, and Internal Audit so that segregation of duties, approval thresholds, the audit trail, revenue recognition treatment, and SOX-relevant controls are designed into workflows rather than reconciled around them afterward. Collaborate with other product managers to guide them through finance required specifications necessary for feature sign off and acceptance. Apply automation and AI where it is verifiable: Target the highest volume of manual work such as cash application, invoice exception handling, dispute triage, payout inquiries with automation that is measurable, reversible, and gated by human review where the cost of a silent error is high. Deconstruct Complex Problems: Break large, ambiguous problems into smaller pieces that deliver iterative wins, without losing sight of the outcome they add up to. Research & Auditing: You will work with accounts receivable and accounts payable teams and research/troubleshoot complex sales orders, purchase orders, general ledger postings and determine a course of action. What You'll Bring to Xometry: 8+ years of product, program or project management experience, and 4+ years in an accounting related role such as book keeping, staff accounting or audit. Accounting fundamentals are at the core of this position. Working fluency with accounting fundamentals, accrual concepts, revenue recognition, chart of accounts, reconciliation, month end close, audit and SOX controls sufficient to partner with Controllership and Accounting as peers rather than as requesters. Experience working with accounting software platforms (Sage Intacct, NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, or similar) that include the general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable or procurement subledgers, and how journal entries are recorded between ledgers; or homegrown systems that act as the subledger. Experience designing policy driven workflows (credit limits, approval routing, tiered sign-off, exception queues, escalation logic) rather than single user tools. Track record integrating with ERP platforms and third party solutions such as Stripe, Avalara, High Radius, Zuora, and eProcurment providers such as Coupa and Ariba. Exceptional written and verbal communication, with the ability to distill financial and operational complexity into a clear narrative for engineers and executives alike. Proven ability to operate autonomously with a passion for problem solving and diving deep into transactional ecosystems to understand the micro details that are recorded in accounting systems. Bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, or business, or 10+ years in an accounting related field; advanced degree (MBA,MS, MAcc) and ASC 606 a plus The estimated base salary range for new hires into this role is $180,000–$207,000 annually + bonus, depending on factors such as job-related skills, relevant experience, and location.
