descriptionText: CAE Project Engineer This is a hybrid position and requires onsite work at our Towson, MD Design Center 3 days per week. Towson, MD, United States Come build something that matters. It takes great people to achieve greatness. People with a sense of purpose and integrity. People with a relentless pursuit of excellence. People who care about making things better For Those Who Make The World™. Sound like you? Join our top-notch team of more than 50,000 diverse and high-performing professionals globally who are making their mark on some of the world’s most beloved brands, including DEWALT®, BLACK+DECKER®, CRAFTSMAN®, STANLEY®, CUB CADET®, and HUSTLER®. Position Overview: We are seeking an experienced CAE Project Engineer to join our Towson CAE team. In this individual contributor role, you will collaborate with cross-functional teams to utilize advanced simulation tools for analyzing and optimizing the durability and performance of our power tool products. Your expertise in CAE simulation technologies will be crucial in driving product development and ensuring high-quality outcomes. Key Responsibilities: Utilize CAE simulation technologies to support product development. Translate product design requirements into simulation project specifications, employing appropriate simulation techniques to ensure quality and performance. Conduct structural analysis using FEA tools in areas including linear static, non-linear static, transient dynamic, noise and vibration, material damage, fatigue life prediction, fluid structure interaction, design optimization, co-simulation, and multi-physics simulation. Verify simulation results with theoretical methods and test data. Analyze simulation results to inform sound design and business decisions in complex technical situations. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to achieve optimal product development solutions. Study the fundamental physics behind products using CAE and other analytical tools. Develop advanced methods and processes to enhance simulation capability and efficiency. Manage and deliver multiple projects with increasing technical complexity. Work effectively in a fast-paced team environment, communicating efficiently with cross-functional teams. Qualifications: Master’s degree or higher in Mechanical Engineering, Engineering Mechanics, Material Science, Physics, or a related field. 6+ years of hands-on experience in FEA modeling within the consumer products industry. Proficiency in major FEA tools (e.g., ANSYS, LS-DYNA, ABAQUS, Hypermesh, or equivalent). Strong knowledge of FEA theory, material failure criteria, solid mechanics, and fracture mechanics. Experience in one or more of the following areas: advanced dynamic impacts, advanced material modeling, fatigue calculation, vibration modeling, wear phenomena modeling, programming, and design optimization. Experience with 3D CAD & PLM systems. Ability to verify simulation results using sound engineering principles. Understanding of mass production manufacturing methods, such as die casting, plastic injection molding, and forging. Proven ability to work independently and collaboratively within a cross-functional team environment. Ability to manage multiple projects and flexible to adjust project priorities based on current business needs. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a keen attention to detail. Ability to generate and evaluate creative ideas. Excellent technical documentation skills and strong written and verbal communication abilities. Preferred Skillsets: 10+ years of hands-on experience in applying FEA within the consumer products industry. Experience in FEA modeling specifically for power tools. Expertise in structural FEA tools, particularly ANSYS Mechanical and ANSYS DYNA. Advanced material modeling expertise for metals, plastics, rubber, concrete, wood, etc., including material damage and removal modeling, fatigue life prediction, and noise and vibration prediction. Experience in CFD workflows, such as: airflow, thermal (including conjugate heat transfer), and particle simulation. Experience in MBD workflows, such as: mechanism simulation with rigid and flexible bodies. Proficiency in programming languages such as Python or MATLAB. Experience in CAE automation and AI applications. Experience in designing and executing validation tests to verify analytical models and calibrate results with empirical data. Who We Are We’re the World’s largest tool company. We design and develop the tools that are used to change the world every day here in our engineering headquarters in Towson, Maryland. Our design teams are involved with every step of the process bringing these world class products to life. From conducting end user research to identify new needs, to designing and prototyping tools to ensure we meet our customers high expectations, to creating robust tests to guarantee the tools we make stand up to the toughest environments, our engineers own every aspect of the process along the way. Who You Are You’re a strong problem solver who loves digging into the details to fully understand what is going on. You have fixed a lot of problems, so you know how to sort out what is meaningful and what is not to be as efficient as possible. You have run DOE’s and done the statistics to make well informed decisions. You like getting your hands dirty and want to be the one disassembling a problem to find out what is broken and how to fix it. You are comfortable taking the lead, and enjoy coaching, teaching, and developing talent. You are looking for a high-visibility role where you can make an immediate and lasting impact. You can lead the complete design of a complex electro-mechanical product. You’re agile and adaptable but work with precision to ensure we deliver top-notch customer experiences, always. You want to work on a project where you can see the fruits of your labor come to life and enjoy seeing the finished product on the shelves of major retailers around the globe. You also have: Job Summary The Micro-Hydraulic Lead Engineer is responsible for leading the design, development, integration, and validation of Micro-Hydraulic systems, subsystems, and components for product platforms and customer applications. This role provides technical leadership for handheld and stationary micro-hydraulic system design activities, including architecture definition, component selection, system analysis, prototype development, testing, and production launch support. The position requires strong cross-functional collaboration with electrical, software, motor controls, suppliers, and manufacturing teams to deliver high-quality hydraulic solutions that meet performance, cost, schedule, and reliability objectives. Experience contributing to intellectual property development, invention disclosures, and patent-support activities is highly valued. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent is required 7 to 10 years of mechanical design experience in micro-hydraulic system design and development. Demonstrated experience leading engineering projects or technical workstreams. Strong knowledge of hydraulic system principles, fluid power components, and system integration with background in high pressure micro-hydraulics. Experience creating and interpreting hydraulic schematics and engineering documentation. Experience creating and interpreting engineering drawings. Proficiency in hydraulic calculations, component sizing, and system troubleshooting. Experience with product development processes from concept through production launch. Knowledge of GD&T, DFM/DFA, DFMEA, and root cause analysis methodologies. Excellent communication skills with the ability to work effectively with a global team, including suppliers and manufacturing operations. Ability to provide direction and mentorship to engineers and designers and lead project teams independently. Preferred Qualifications Experience with micro-hydraulic, high pressure compact hydraulic, or electro-hydraulic system applications. Familiarity with regulated, safety-critical, or high-reliability product environments. Experience supporting supplier qualification and component validation activities. Advanced analytical capability in system performance optimization and failure investigation. Leadership and Behavioral Expectations Self-motivated, creative, goal-oriented, and a strong team player. Holds self-accountable for results and behaviors, overcomes obstacles, and partners with others to deliver on commitments. Demonstrate understanding of quality, performance, schedule, and cost objectives in a cross-functional and/or technical environment. Provides strong technical leadership and sound engineering judgment in a collaborative environment. Key Skills and Competencies Hydraulic system design and integration; specifically high pressure. Fluid power engineering Technical leadership System analysis and troubleshooting Product development and validation Cross-functional collaboration Risk assessment and DFMEA What You’ll Do As a Lead Project Engineer, you’ll be part of our Global Tools & Storage team located in Towson, MD. Specifically, you’ll: Lead the design and development of micro-hydraulic systems, subsystems, and components for product platforms and customer applications. Translate product requirements into micro-hydraulic architecture, subsystems, documentation, schematics, component specifications, and system performance criteria. Perform micro-hydraulic system sizing, pressure and flow calculations, load analysis, thermal analysis, and performance optimization. Lead technical decision-making for hydraulic system design activities across assigned engineering projects and technical workstreams. Develop and execute plans for project sample builds, prototype development, and engineering validation activities. Define validation plans and support testing activities to verify hydraulic system functionality, durability, efficiency, and safety. Troubleshoot hydraulic performance issues during prototype, testing, pilot, and production phases. Lead technical feasibility studies, design reviews, risk assessments, and DFMEA activities. Participate in hands-on concept development, prototyping, product testing, and data collection, while providing technical feedback and recommendations. Collaborate with motor controls, electrical, and software teams to integrate electro-hydraulic systems and ensure proper system behavior. Drive design standardization, modularity, and reuse of proven hydraulic solutions across programs. Support supplier selection, technical reviews, and component qualification activities. Ensure designs comply with applicable industry standards, regulatory requirements, and internal engineering processes. Manage engineering deliverables, schedules, and technical execution for assigned projects. Successfully deliver projects that achieve quality, performance, schedule, and cost objectives in a cross-functional environment. Participate in cross-functional meetings to communicate technical status, risks, issues, and recommended solutions. Support cost reduction, quality improvement, and continuous improvement initiatives related to hydraulic systems. Provide direction, mentorship, and technical guidance to project engineers, engineers, and designers, and lead project teams independently. title: Senior Performance Marketing Analyst
descriptionText: About Us: Grow was born to tackle a critical challenge: making mental health care more effective and accessible for everyone. Since launching in 2020, 15 million sessions have started on Grow, and we've barely scratched the surface. We do it through a three-sided marketplace that empowers providers, augments insurance payors, and serves patients. Every solution we build reveals ten more waiting to be delivered, and that's just what gets us going. We've backed that ambition with more than $328M in funding, including our Series D at a $3B valuation from Sequoia Capital, Transformation Capital, TCV, SignalFire, Menlo Ventures, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, and others. At Grow, the work you do can literally change someone's life. Your work here doesn't stay on a screen; it impacts whether someone can find, afford, and access quality care. That ambition sets us apart, and offers you an endless runway to impact one of the world's most urgent issues. We don’t have passenger seats here. Everyone is driving something that matters. This work deserves real commitment. So if you thrive on meeting problems head on, untangling serious complexity, and working at pace with the sharpest yet kindest people around, you've come to the right place. The Opportunity We're looking for a performance marketer who wants to get their hands on the channels where most people first discover Grow. You'll sit on our paid media team focused on client acquisition, supporting day-to-day buying, analysis, and creative testing across paid social - Meta, TikTok, YouTube - plus creator and affiliate paid partnerships and a growing set of emerging channels. You'll report to our Performance Marketing Manager leading paid social. This role is a blend of hands-on-keyboard media buying, real analytical work, and creative judgment. The best fit for this role questions assumptions and digs deeper when the numbers don't add up, rather than accepting surface-level explanations. You have a deep understanding of how paid social channels work and are motivated by the thought of helping us to build a best in class program. You balance attention to detail with a bias toward action - you ship experiments quickly, learn fast, and iterate. title: Human Resources Manager
descriptionText: GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We support high ownership and real professional growth. Curious about what it's really like to work here? Read our values and hear from the people who do. If they resonate, this could be a great fit! Role Overview GiveDirectly Malawi has grown steadily since its introduction in 2019 and in 2025 launched our most ambitious program and research agenda yet, delivering funds across an entire district alongside the largest-ever randomised trial on unconditional cash. To deliver our ambitious plans for scale, we are looking for a Human Resources Manager who can operate as a strategic, agile thought partner to the Country Director someone with a strong grasp of Malawi labour law and demonstrated, hands-on experience across the HR lifecycle, who is just as comfortable advising on organisational design and workforce risk as they are personally running payroll and compensation. The HR Manager ensures that GiveDirectly Malawi attracts, develops, and retains the talent needed to deliver on our mission, focus on the strategic and technical work that most shapes the organisation's ability to perform. The role will reward exceptional interpersonal skills, sound judgement in navigating people and organisational challenges, and a deep commitment to building a workplace where staff feel supported, valued, and connected to the work. As GiveDirectly continues to scale, this role ensures that our people practices are consistent, compliant, and fit for purpose, balancing the pace of a fast-growing organisation with the rigour and care that good HR demands and doing so with the agility to build or improve systems rather than simply administer the ones already in place. The HR Manager will play a critical role in strengthening the infrastructure of the country office, designing and improving systems for recruitment, onboarding, performance management, and staff development that can grow with the organisation. This position also plays an important role in safeguarding organisational culture and integrity, supporting leadership in upholding GiveDirectly's values and ensuring staff experience reflects the standards we set for ourselves. Strategic Partnership & Talent Management Serve as a strategic thought partner to the Country Director on organisational design, workforce planning, and people-related risk Own the end-to-end recruitment process for all open positions in Malawi, partnering with hiring managers to define role requirements, develop job descriptions, and build targeted sourcing strategies that attract strong candidates from various talent pools. Lead candidate screening and selection, including structured CV reviews, interview coordination, and skills assessments where relevant, ensuring a consistent, respectful, and efficient experience for all candidates from application through to offer. Lead periodic salary benchmarking exercises using credible market data and sector comparators, producing clear analysis and recommendations to ensure GiveDirectly's compensation remains competitive, internally equitable, and aligned with local labour market realities. Drive professional development planning across the team, working with managers and staff to identify individual growth needs, co-create learning plans, and source, coordinate, and evaluate training interventions both internal and external that build capability at every level of the organisation. Payroll & Compliance Personally manage payroll, ensuring salaries, relevant allowances, and other entitlements are processed accurately, on time, and in compliance with both internal policies and local labour regulations Act as the primary point of contact for staff on HR policy questions, providing clear, fair, and consistent guidance, and lead the management of disciplinary and grievance processes in line with GiveDirectly's HR manual and Malawi labour law. Design and continuously improve a structured onboarding programme for all new hires, covering orientation on GiveDirectly's HR manual, policies, and organisational values, as well as seamless set-up of benefits enrolment, payroll, and system access from day one. Actively identify opportunities to modernise or automate HR processes Administration & Record-Keeping (in partnership with the HR Associate). Set direction and quality standards for staff benefits administration, leave management, and timesheet processes, with the HR Associate handling day-to-day coordination, vendor liaison, and record maintenance. Maintain oversight of accurate, confidential, and audit-ready personnel files for all staff, ensuring records are kept in line with GiveDirectly's data policies, local labour regulations, and best-practice HR record-keeping standards. Performance Management & Tracking Provide support during the performance review cycle including stakeholder communications, documentation, and ensuring HR systems and records are promptly updated to reflect any changes in role, title, or compensation. Work closely with the Country Director and line managers to identify and action professional development opportunities for staff, tracking individual development plans and following up to ensure commitments translate into tangible growth. Organisational Culture & Engagement Take ownership of planning and delivering a calendar of team-building activities and staff engagement events that strengthen relationships, sustain morale, and reinforce a sense of shared purpose across the Malawi team. Proactively generate and champion initiatives that bring GiveDirectly's culture and values to life, embedding them into key moments across the employee lifecycle including hiring, onboarding, performance conversations, and team gatherings. Serve as a trusted culture steward, creating regular channels for staff to share feedback, surfacing themes and insights to leadership, and helping the organisation stay responsive to the needs and sentiment of its people. Desired Qualifications 5–7 years of progressive experience in operations, with demonstrable exposure to human resources management, ideally within an international development, NGO, or high-growth organisation context candidates from fast-paced or tech-enabled environments are encouraged to apply Direct, hands-on payroll and compensation experience able to personally run payroll and lead benchmarking exercises, not only oversee others doing so. A track record of building, redesigning, or modernising an HR process or system, ideally including use of automation or digital tools, rather than solely administering existing ones. Degree in a relevant field (e.g. Human Resources Management, Business Administration, Operations Management, or equivalent). title: Slalom Flex (Project Based) - Analytics Engineer/PowerBI Developer
descriptionText: Location: Onsite in Atlanta, GA - 5 days a week (local candidates only) Who You’ll Work With At Slalom, personal connection meets global scale. Our vision is to enable a world in which everyone loves their work and life. We help organizations of all kinds redefine what’s possible, give shape to the future—and get there. What You’ll Do Design, develop, maintain, and optimize interactive Power BI dashboards and reports that support business functions across sales, engineering, operations, product, and digital teams. Build, enhance, and support semantic models, DAX measures, KPIs, Power Query transformations, and Row-Level Security (RLS) frameworks to deliver secure, scalable, and high-performing analytics solutions. Develop and maintain reusable datasets, data marts, and analytical models that enable consistent reporting and self-service analytics across the organization. Leverage DAX, Power Query (M), SQL, and data modeling best practices to create scalable, reusable, and maintainable reporting solutions. Support data engineering activities, including data pipeline development, ETL/ELT processes, data validation, data reconciliation, migration efforts, and troubleshooting of analytical data flows. Partner closely with business stakeholders to gather requirements, understand business objectives, and translate needs into actionable technical solutions and insights. Generate recurring and ad hoc reporting that drives operational excellence, performance management, and strategic decision-making. Contribute to reporting and analytics modernization initiatives, including platform enhancements involving Microsoft Fabric, Amazon Redshift, Azure-based technologies, and modern data architectures. Investigate and resolve production issues, including data quality concerns, report discrepancies, refresh failures, and reporting platform performance challenges. Conduct root cause analysis and implement sustainable solutions to improve reporting reliability and data integrity. Create and maintain comprehensive documentation for dashboards, semantic models, business logic, data workflows, pipelines, schemas, and operational processes. Participate in knowledge transfer activities and collaborate with team members to ensure continuity of key analytics and reporting capabilities. Explore opportunities to leverage AI-enabled analytics, automation, and modern data platforms to improve business outcomes and decision-making. What You’ll Bring Strong experience with Power BI, including dashboard development, data visualization, semantic modeling, DAX, Power Query, performance optimization, and Row-Level Security (RLS). Advanced SQL skills and experience with data validation, troubleshooting, query optimization, and reporting support. Hands-on experience with analytics engineering and data engineering concepts, including ETL/ELT processes, data modeling, pipeline support, and data warehousing. Experience working with modern data platforms such as Microsoft Fabric, Amazon Redshift, Azure SQL, Azure Data Factory, Synapse Analytics, Databricks, or similar technologies. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills with the ability to effectively partner with business and technical stakeholders. Experience supporting reporting modernization, cloud migrations, or enterprise analytics initiatives. Preferred experience with Python, Spark, AI-enabled analytics, and high-volume operational or telemetry data environments. A proactive, ownership-oriented mindset with strong documentation habits and a commitment to collaboration, knowledge sharing, and continuous learning. About Us Slalom is a fiercely human business and technology consulting company that leads with outcomes to bring more value, in all ways, always. From strategy through delivery, our agile teams across 52 offices in 12 countries collaborate with clients to bring powerful customer experiences, innovative ways of working, and new products and services to life. We are trusted by leaders across the Global 1000, many successful enterprise and mid-market companies, and 500+ public sector organizations to improve operations, drive growth, and create value. At Slalom, we believe that together, we can move faster, dream bigger, and build better tomorrows for all. Compensation and Benefits Slalom prides itself on helping team members thrive in their work and life. As a result, Slalom is proud to invest in benefits that include meaningful time off and paid holidays, 401(k) with a match, a range of choices for highly subsidized health, dental, & vision coverage, adoption and fertility assistance, and short/long-term disability. We also offer yearly $350 reimbursement account for any well-being-related expenses, as well as discounted home, auto, and pet insurance. Slalom is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. For this position, the pay range is $70/hr to $85/hr. Actual compensation will depend upon an individual’s skills, experience, qualifications, location, and other relevant factors. The salary pay range is subject to change and may be modified at any time. We are committed to pay transparency and compliance with applicable laws.

title: Lead, Executive Experiences: Gifting & Events
descriptionText: Job Summary: We are seeking a highly organized, detail-oriented, and discreet individual to lead a curated program of executive relationship experiences on behalf of our CEO. This role is responsible for systemizing and scaling the CEO's personal and professional connections, from meetings and events to personalized gifts and follow-ups, into a consistent, thoughtful, and highly personalized program of ongoing engagement. The ideal candidate combines exceptional attention to detail with strong research and writing skills, is comfortable operating behind the scenes, and has a passion for leveraging technology, AI, and external partners to create scalable, efficient processes that enhance the program's impact and reach. Key Responsibilities: Relationship Program Management: Build and maintain a systemized program to track and follow up on the CEO's key relationships, ensuring consistent, timely, and thoughtful engagement over time. Contact List Stewardship: Maintain and continuously refine a master list of key internal and external relationships, ensuring each contact has a customized engagement plan. Personalized Gifting at Scale: Research and coordinate thoughtful, customized gifts for individual contacts. Media and News Monitoring: Monitor news and interview feeds for mentions or appearances by individuals on the relationship list, flagging timely opportunities for connection. Event Hosting Support: Support the CEO in hosting small-group virtual sessions for internal and external groups, and assist with related logistics, communications, and materials. Cost and Program Analysis: Manage the program budget and maintain ongoing cost, benefit, and ROI tracking, including quarterly financial reporting and analysis. Client Event Planning and Execution: Plan and execute client events, including managing vendor relationships, sourcing new vendors as needed, tracking client RSVPs, coordinating restaurant reservations, and partnering with local offices to align on guest experience, meals, and event logistics. Other: Regular in-office attendance, Monday-Friday 9:00am-5:00pm, at Seattle location is a requirement of this role. Ability to lift up to 50 pounds as part of daily operations. Must have a valid driver’s license and access to a reliable vehicle for running errands. Up to 15% domestic travel is expected for client meetings, events, and conferences; flexibility based on business needs. Flexibility with hours often necessary due to events. Initial engagement is temporary Qualifications: Experience: 3–5 years of experience in relationship management, executive support, CRM/marketing operations, account management, or a similar role; experience with personalized outreach, gifting, or client experience programs preferred. Education: Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Communications, or a related field is preferred. Skills: Exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail. Strong research and writing skills, with the ability to personalize correspondence at scale while maintaining authenticity. Proficiency in Salesforce, including contact/relationship management, campaign creation, tracking, and reporting, as well as Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Copilot) and Canva. High level of discretion and confidentiality; comfortable managing sensitive and high-profile relationship information discreetly. Strong program and time management skills, with the ability to manage a large, ongoing contact list and recurring outreach cadences. Demonstrates strong initiative and sound judgment; comfortable working independently and behind the scenes. Strong problem-solving skills and ability to think creatively about customized, individualized experiences at scale. Report into the Global Executive Assistant team, collaborating and working closely with other executive assistants. title: Vice President Engineering, Maryland Design Center
descriptionText: The Company It takes great people to achieve greatness. People with a sense of purpose and integrity. People with a relentless pursuit of excellence. People who care about making things better For Those Who Make The World™. Join our top-notch team of more than 43,000 high-performing professionals globally who are making their mark on some of the world’s most beloved brands, including DEWALT®, STANLEY, CRAFTSMAN, BLACK+DECKER, and other strong brands. The Role Stanley Black & Decker (NYSE: SWK) is seeking an Engineering Vice President, Power Tools North America to lead engineering for the company’s flagship DEWALT professional power tools business in North America. Reporting to the Engineering Leader of Americas/EMEA, this role will lead the Maryland Design Center — spanning Mechanical Engineering, Electronics/Electrical Engineering, Embedded Software, Industrial Design, Packaging Engineering, and Shared Services/CAE — approximately 450 engineers and engineering professionals. The Maryland Design Center in Towson, MD is the engineering heart of Stanley Black & Decker’s global power tools business. It owns the design, development, factory introduction, and sustaining of the DEWALT professional power tool systems portfolio and provides technology and methodology leadership across mechanical, electrical, software, industrial design, platforming, program management, and computational analysis disciplines. The center is the primary engineering liaison with Category and Product Management, Supply Chain, and Manufacturing, and partners closely with engineering centers in Germany, Israel, Mexico, and Asia. The VP Engineering, Maryland Design Center will build and lead a high-performing, integration-first engineering organization. The leader owns total product accountability across all North America programs, and develops the next generation of engineering leadership talent at Stanley Black & Decker. This position is based at our Tools & Outdoor headquarters in Towson, Maryland. Primary Accountabilities Own total engineering delivery for the Towson Design Center. Serve as the single accountable leader for all cross-functional program execution — on time, on budget, and to quality specification — across the DEWALT professional power tools portfolio. This is a direct accountability, not a coordination role. Drive new product development excellence. Partner with the commercial teams and to shape and execute a compelling NPD pipeline. Ensure programs are scoped and resourced for success from the outset, and that the organization delivers with the speed and quality DEWALT’s market position demands. Own Towson engineering talent. Build a best-in-class engineering leadership team. Drive succession planning, high-potential identification, performance management, and capability building across all Towson engineering disciplines. Set expectations and hold leaders accountable for people development, not just program delivery. Integrate across functions. Serve as the primary Towson engineering liaison with Global Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Quality, and the Mexico engineering ecosystem. Ensure products are designed for manufacturability and that the Towson organization is a proactive, collaborative partner — not a downstream recipient — in the product creation process. Champion platforming and design-to-value. Actively support the Chief Engineer community and the platform architecture mandate. Drive a Design-to-Value mindset across Towson programs, partnering with the Americas/EMEA Systems Engineering & Processes function to identify and pursue cost reduction, complexity reduction, and platform commonality opportunities. Partner with the Systems Engineering & Processes Director to embed engineering process rigor and quality standards across Towson programs. The two leaders must operate as a unified leadership team on standards, gate discipline, and technical readiness expectations. Shape the technology agenda for DEWALT professional power tools. Work alongside business leaders and the enterprise innovation team to ensure Towson is anticipating and integrating relevant technology trends — including electrification, embedded systems, connectivity, AI-assisted tools, and advanced materials — into the product development roadmap. Manage engineering agility and productivity metrics. Own and improve Towson’s KPIs for development cycle time, first-pass quality, engineering productivity, and design-driven cost reduction. Connect structural and process changes directly to measurable business outcomes. Build a high-performance engineering culture. Establish clear expectations, consistent accountability, and a culture that values both technical depth and cross-functional collaboration. Model the leadership behaviors required to attract, develop, and retain world-class engineering talent. Candidate Profile Senior engineering leadership experience at a design center, business unit, or enterprise level, ideally from a company known for engineering excellence in complex, electrified mechatronic products. Consumer power tools, automotive, appliances, or precision manufacturing backgrounds are highly relevant. 15+ years of progressive experience in engineering, product development, and technology leadership, including direct experience leading large, multidisciplinary engineering organizations (300+ people) in a design center or site leader capacity. Demonstrated track record of delivering cross-functional new product development programs — on time and to specification — across hardware (mechanical + electrical) and software-integrated products. The leader must be credible and accountable across all engineering disciplines, not just their functional background. Deep familiarity with systems engineering principles, total tool or total product accountability, and the integration challenges that arise in complex electrified products. Experience implementing or maturing systems engineering capability in a product development organization is a strong differentiator. Electrification, embedded systems, and platform engineering experience. The Towson portfolio is increasingly software-defined and platform-centric. The leader must understand these domains with sufficient depth to set direction, assess technical risk, and develop capability. Significant platforming and modular architecture experience. The ability to drive reuse, reduce complexity, and establish platform discipline across a broad product portfolio is essential. Proven people leader and talent developer. A track record of building high-performing engineering leadership teams, managing through multiple layers, driving succession, and developing technical talent into broader leadership roles. This leader must be as strong on the people dimension as on the technical and program dimensions. Strong change leadership capability. The Towson organization is in transformation — the leader must be comfortable driving change, holding the line on expectations, and building commitment through clarity and credibility. Cross-functional partnership skills. Able to operate as a peer to Product Management, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and Marketing leadership — not as a service provider to them. Must bring a business perspective to the engineering agenda, not just a technical one. Technical degree required; Masters or Ph.D. in Engineering preferred. MBA or equivalent business education is a meaningful differentiator. Professionally active in engineering societies, professional associations, or external networks. Personal succession potential and genuine desire to build leadership capability for future roles at Stanley Black & Decker. This is a VP-level role with a clear path to expanded enterprise leadership responsibility. The Details: You will receive a competitive salary and a great benefits plan, including: Medical, dental, life, vision, wellness program, disability, 401(k), Employee Stock Purchase Plan, paid time off, and tuition reimbursement. Discounts on Stanley Black & Decker tools and other partner programs. And More: We want our company to be a place you’ll want to be – and stay. Being part of our team means you get to: Grow: Be part of our global company with 20+ brands to grow and develop your skills along multiple career paths. Learn: Have access to a wealth of learning resources, including our digital learning portal. Belong: Experience an awesome place to work, where we have mutual respect and a great appreciation for diversity, equity, and inclusion. Give Back: Help us continue to make positive changes locally and globally through volunteerism, giving back, and sustainable business practices. At Stanley Black & Decker, you will get that pride that comes from empowering makers, doers, protectors, and everyday heroes all over the world. We’re more than the #1 tools company. More than a driving force in outdoor power equipment. More than a global leader in industrial. We’re visionaries and innovators. As successful as we’ve been in the past, we have so much further to go. That’s where you come in. Join us! descriptionText: About Us: Grow was born to tackle a critical challenge: making mental health care more effective and accessible for everyone. Since launching in 2020, 15 million sessions have started on Grow, and we've barely scratched the surface. That ambition sets us apart, and offers you an endless runway to impact one of the world's most urgent issues. We don’t have passenger seats here. Everyone is driving something that matters. This work deserves real commitment. So if you thrive on meeting problems head on, untangling serious complexity, and working at pace with the sharpest yet kindest people around, you've come to the right place. Grow Therapy is growing our Revenue Operations team, and we’re looking for a GTM Engineer to join the builders architecting the systems, data, and automation layer behind our commercial engine. This is a role built for range: you could be re-architecting the referral engine that turns physician outreach into inbound patient referrals for our Primary Care (PCP) motion, standing up a brand-new 0-to-1 system connecting benefits consultants, employers, and employees for our Employee Assistance Program (EAP), or building the recruitment, credentialing, and retention systems that let Grow recruit and retain the therapists and prescribers on our platform through Provider Experience. Every one of these is a real engineering problem, not a process-improvement exercise, and every one of them directly expands access to mental healthcare. This is a high-ownership, builder-first role for someone who wants to work at the intersection of GTM strategy and hands-on systems engineering: architecting the data model, shipping the automation, and building the AI agents that let Grow’s commercial teams do more without growing headcount linearly. You’ll work in close partnership with the GTM Engineering Lead, Enterprise & GTM Architecture, who sets the standards for Grow’s GTM systems architecture end-to-end, and with the broader GTM Systems team as it takes shape. A taste of the systems you could be building: - Primary Care (PCP): Design the data model and automation that convert physician-office outreach into a repeatable, inbound referral engine, and automate referral intake, validation, and routing. - Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Map the end-to-end consultant → employer → employee journey and build the staging environment and data model from scratch to support a brand-new motion. - Provider Experience: Build the recruitment, credentialing, and retention pipeline that moves a provider from first application to an active, engaged member of Grow’s network. What You’ll Be Doing - Architect the system: Design and ship the end-to-end technical architecture for your assigned motion, spanning data model, automation logic, and integration patterns. - Build AI agents, not just workflows: Design and deploy AI agents (built on Claude) that autonomously perform GTM tasks (referral triage, document parsing, account research) rather than workflows that simply call an LLM API. - Run an experimentation loop: Treat new automations and agent behaviors as experiments: ship fast, measure impact, and iterate or kill based on data, not intuition. - Evolve the stack: Continuously evaluate the GTM tech stack (HubSpot, n8n/Workato, Segment, Gong, Aircall/Nooks, Clay) and recommend consolidation or upgrades as your motion matures and scales. - Sandbox everything: Implement rigorous testing and deployment so no logic goes live unvalidated. - Document the system: Maintain a technical schema map of your systems so the organization understands the logic behind every automation. - Own data governance: Define and enforce data governance standards (field definitions, ownership, quality rules, and access controls) for your data model as a core part of data strategy. - Build for resilience: Build monitoring and self-healing automations that alert the team when data syncs fail or logic breaks. - Align on shared architecture: Partner with the GTM Engineering Lead, Enterprise & GTM Architecture to apply consistent technical standards and governance practices across your systems and the rest of Grow’s GTM architecture. title: Director, Regulatory Affairs (Licensure, DSCSA, and Trade Compliance Programs)
descriptionText: McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care. What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you. Position Summary The Director, Regulatory Affairs provides strategic leadership, enterprise governance, and regulatory risk ownership for the Licensure, Trade Compliance, and Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA) programs supporting a large, multi-facility pharmaceutical third-party logistics (3PL) organization. The Director is accountable for establishing the regulatory strategy, control framework, decision rights, and escalation mechanisms necessary to maintain compliant operations while enabling sustainable business growth. The role reports to the VP, Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs. This role serves as the enterprise regulatory authority for assigned programs and is responsible for identifying, assessing, communicating, accepting within delegated authority, mitigating, and escalating regulatory risk. The Director translates evolving federal and state requirements into durable business controls, advises executive leadership on material exposure and response options, and ensures that residual risk is transparent to the appropriate decision-makers. The position leads a team of regulatory professionals and partners closely with Quality, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Information Technology, Security, Finance, Customer Solutions, and Supply Chain leadership. This Director owns the regulatory risk posture and control effectiveness of the assigned programs, with authority to require corrective action, elevate material risk, and recommend operational restrictions when compliance cannot be reasonably assured. Key Responsibilities: Regulatory Leadership and Risk Ownership Develop and execute the 3PL regulatory affairs strategy for Licensure, Trade Compliance, and DSCSA, aligned with business objectives, customer commitments, and the organization's risk appetite. Own the regulatory risk framework for assigned programs, including risk identification, assessment, control design, monitoring, escalation, remediation, and formal communication of residual risk. Exercise independent regulatory judgment and provide clear recommendations when legal requirements, agency expectations, operational realities, and industry practices are not fully aligned. Establish decision rights, governance forums, escalation thresholds, and documented risk-acceptance pathways for material regulatory issues. Provide executive leadership with timely, decision-ready assessments of regulatory exposure, business impact, alternatives, and recommended actions. Require corrective or preventive action when regulatory controls are ineffective and recommend suspension, limitation, or redesign of activities when compliance cannot be reasonably assured. Serve as a senior company representative during regulatory inspections, inquiries, audits, and significant customer or agency engagements involving assigned programs. Licensure Program Oversight Direct 3PL licensure programs supporting multiple facilities, legal entities, service models, and regulated jurisdictions. Ensure appropriate governance over state board of pharmacy, wholesale distributor, 3PL, controlled substance, and other applicable licensing obligations. Oversee licensing applications, renewals, amendments, change notifications, reporting obligations, and evidence retention. Assess and communicate licensure implications associated with new facilities, expansions, acquisitions, reorganizations, new services, operational changes, and customer implementations. Maintain risk-based visibility to license status, renewal timeliness, regulatory commitments, dependencies, and exceptions across the network. Define controls to prevent regulated activity from occurring outside the scope or effective dates of required authority. DSCSA Compliance Leadership Provide strategic oversight and risk ownership for the enterprise DSCSA compliance program. Ensure governance for product tracing, electronic interoperable exchange, verification, saleable returns, suspect and illegitimate product investigations, recordkeeping, and applicable notifications or reporting. Partner with Information Technology, Operations, Quality, customers, and trading partners to establish compliant and resilient serialization and traceability capabilities. Direct the evaluation and implementation of applicable statutes, FDA guidance, enforcement policies, industry standards, and emerging interoperability expectations. Ensure exceptions, system failures, data-quality issues, and trading-partner risks are assessed, contained, escalated, and remediated using documented risk-based processes. Provide regulatory leadership for significant DSCSA events and determine when matters require escalation to executive leadership, customers, regulators, or legal counsel. Trade Compliance Program Oversight Lead the regulatory governance of trade compliance activities supporting domestic and international movement of pharmaceutical and healthcare products. Oversee risk-based controls for import, export, customs, sanctions, classification, documentation, recordkeeping, and cross-border distribution obligations, as applicable to the organization's operating model. Partner with Legal, Compliance, Operations, Finance, brokers, freight forwarders, and customers to clarify accountability and resolve complex trade-compliance issues. Assess the regulatory implications of new trade lanes, countries of origin, product categories, business models, service offerings, and customer requirements. Monitor material exceptions and trends and ensure corrective actions address both immediate events and underlying systemic causes. Escalate trade compliance risks that may affect product movement, customer commitments, financial exposure, or regulatory standing. People and Organizational Leadership Lead, coach, and develop a team of approximately 3-4 regulatory affairs professionals, establishing clear accountability, priorities, and performance expectations. Build organizational capability through talent development, cross-training, succession planning, and disciplined workload and resource management. Foster a culture of regulatory integrity, constructive challenge, timely escalation, practical problem-solving, and continuous improvement. Ensure the team maintains the technical knowledge, business acumen, systems proficiency, and stakeholder relationships required to execute assigned programs effectively. Manage external consultants or service providers, as appropriate, and ensure clear deliverables, accountability, and oversight. Cross-Functional Leadership and Business Enablement Lead regulatory assessments for new customers, services, facilities, technologies, system changes, acquisitions, and strategic initiatives. Partner with Quality, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Information Technology, Security, Finance, Customer Solutions, and Supply Chain teams to embed regulatory requirements into business processes and system controls. Support customer due diligence, audits, proposals, contracting discussions, and implementation planning by providing accurate regulatory requirements and risk-based recommendations. Influence stakeholders without direct authority and resolve conflicts between compliance obligations, operational constraints, customer expectations, and commercial objectives. Communicate complex regulatory matters in concise, decision-oriented terms appropriate for executives, customers, operational teams, and regulators. Monitoring, Assurance, and Continuous Improvement Establish meaningful key risk indicators, key performance indicators, management review mechanisms, and reporting for assigned programs. Assess program effectiveness through trends, exception data, audits, regulatory developments, control testing, and stakeholder feedback. Ensure regulatory gaps, audit findings, agency observations, and recurring exceptions are assigned, tracked, remediated, and verified for effectiveness. Maintain an enterprise regulatory horizon-scanning process and ensure emerging requirements are assessed, prioritized, resourced, and implemented in a controlled manner. Drive simplification, standardization, automation, and process improvements without weakening regulatory control or accountability. Decision Authority and Escalation Authorized to interpret assigned regulatory requirements and establish 3PL program standards, subject to Legal consultation where appropriate. Authorized to require risk assessments, corrective actions, control enhancements, and documented remediation plans within assigned program scope. Authorized to escalate material or unresolved risk directly to senior Quality, Regulatory, Compliance, Legal, Operations, or executive leadership. Expected to recommend operational restrictions, implementation holds, or other interim controls when regulatory compliance or product traceability cannot be reasonably assured. Does not unilaterally accept material enterprise risk outside delegated authority; ensures such decisions are documented and made by the accountable business or executive owner with appropriate Regulatory, Quality, Legal, and Compliance input. Qualifications Bachelor's degree or equivalent in Regulatory Affairs, Pharmacy, Life Sciences, Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, or a related field. 10 or more years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical regulatory affairs, quality, compliance, distribution, supply chain, or another highly regulated environment. 5 or more years of people leadership or significant program leadership experience, including accountability for complex regulatory or compliance programs. Demonstrated knowledge of pharmaceutical distribution requirements, state licensing frameworks, DSCSA, and regulatory risk management. Experience leading cross-functional initiatives and interacting with regulators, auditors, customers, legal counsel, and senior leaders. Demonstrated ability to convert complex requirements into practical controls, governance, metrics, and executive-level recommendations. Ability to travel approximately 25% and work effectively in a hybrid environment. Preferred Qualifications Advanced degree such as PharmD, JD, MBA, MS, or a related discipline. Experience in pharmaceutical wholesale distribution, third-party logistics, manufacturing, or healthcare supply chain operations. Deep experience with multi-jurisdictional licensure, DSCSA serialization and traceability, and trade compliance programs. Experience overseeing regulatory programs across multiple facilities, legal entities, or operating models. Regulatory Affairs Certification (RAC), Certified Customs Specialist (CCS), Licensed Customs Broker, or other relevant professional credential. Work Environment and Travel This position operates on a hybrid work schedule and requires approximately 25% travel to company facilities, customer locations, regulatory meetings, industry events, and other business locations. The role requires the ability to collaborate across functions, facilities, and time zones and to respond to significant regulatory events as business needs require. title: Senior Director, Corporate Counsel
descriptionText: 1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $400M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing. About 1Password At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work. If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future. As Senior Director, Corporate Counsel, you’ll oversee 1Password’s Corporate Legal function and provide strategic legal guidance across a broad range of matters. Reporting to the VP, Legal & General Counsel, you’ll play a key role in supporting 1Password’s growth, M&A activity, international expansion, financing activities and corporate and subsidiary governance. This role also oversees compliance, equity, litigation, intellectual property and marketing matters. You’ll partner closely with leaders across Finance, Marketing, People, Corporate Development and other business functions. This role requires a pragmatic, business-minded lawyer who can operate effectively in a fast-paced environment, manage complex projects, and provide clear advice on matters involving multiple stakeholders and jurisdictions. This is a remote opportunity within the United States and Canada. How we’re using AI today On the Legal team, AI helps us move faster without sacrificing quality. We use it to draft and review commercial agreements, implement negotiation playbooks, and prepare the groundwork for legal review. AI also helps us stay on top of regulatory developments, synthesize research across jurisdictions, and identify risks in novel situations like new product launches or partnership structures. The result is a team that can operate at higher volume with greater consistency, while creating more time for the judgment calls, collaboration, and meaningful decisions that matter most. What we're looking for: - Juris Doctor with active bar membership in Canada or the United States and at least 10 years of relevant experience, including time at a nationally recognized law firm and ideally a mix of late-stage private and public company work. Experience in technology or SaaS is preferred. - Experience leading or supporting mergers and acquisitions, including due diligence, negotiations, transaction documentation, and post-closing integration. - Strong knowledge of corporate governance, securities laws, entity management and experience preparing for or managing public company compliance. - Experience advising on international expansion, including subsidiary formation and regulatory requirements across multiple jurisdictions. - Experience supporting financing transactions and related securities law compliance. - Ability to identify legal and business risks, develop practical mitigation strategies, and communicate recommendations clearly to senior stakeholders. - Experience managing external counsel and coordinating cross-functional teams on complex legal matters. - Excellent judgment, written and verbal communication skills, and attention to detail. - A practical, collaborative, and solutions-oriented approach to legal work. - Ability to manage competing priorities independently while maintaining a high standard of execution. What you can expect: - Lead the legal workstreams for mergers and acquisitions, including due diligence, negotiations, drafting and reviewing transaction documents, and coordinating with external advisors and internal stakeholders. - Advise on legal considerations and regulatory requirements related to international operations and expansion. - Oversee corporate entities, corporate records, and related governance processes, including the incorporation and ongoing management of global subsidiaries - Provide guidance on corporate governance matters, including developing and implementing corporate policies and procedures. - Support Finance on a variety of matters, including insurance renewals, tax planning, financial statements, employee equity, commission plans, and other strategic projects. - Review marketing materials and advise on applicable compliance requirements. - Develop and deliver compliance training programs for employees on relevant legal and regulatory topics. - Identify legal risks across the organization and develop strategies to mitigate those risks. - Manage litigation and dispute resolution matters, including overseeing external counsel, developing case strategies, and supporting negotiations. - Manage 1Password’s intellectual property portfolio, including trademarks, copyrights, and patents. - Serve as a trusted legal partner to leaders across the business, balancing thoughtful risk management with the needs of a fast-moving company. USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $269,000 USD and $404,000 USD, plus immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs. Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $234,000 CAD and $351,000 CAD, plus immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs. At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set. This posting is for an existing vacancy. Our culture At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone https://blog.1password.com/inside-the-culture-powering-1passwords-next-chapter/. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. How we work with AI We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. title: Encryption & Post-Quantum Architect
descriptionText: Position Summary The Encryption & Post-Quantum Architect is responsible for Stanley Black & Decker's enterprise cryptographic strategy, cryptographic architecture, and post-quantum readiness program. This role serves as the organization's subject matter expert for encryption technologies, cryptographic risk management, Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), certificate services, key management, and emerging post-quantum cryptography requirements. The position is responsible for identifying cryptographic dependencies across the enterprise, developing remediation and modernization roadmaps, and partnering with technology teams to ensure cryptographic controls continue to meet business, regulatory, and security requirements. As the organization's post-quantum readiness program matures, this role will lead cryptographic migration planning efforts and coordinate remediation activities with application, infrastructure, cloud, product security, and manufacturing technology teams. This position aligns directly with the Future Readiness workstream, including crypto inventory, vendor readiness assessments, cryptographic modernization, and post-quantum readiness planning. Key Responsibilities Develop and maintain enterprise cryptographic architecture standards and technical guidance. Maintain visibility into cryptographic assets, certificates, keys, encryption dependencies, and cryptographic trust relationships across the enterprise. Lead post-quantum cryptography readiness assessments and cryptographic inventory initiatives. Evaluate vendor, supplier, and technology partner readiness for post-quantum cryptography migration. Develop cryptographic modernization and remediation roadmaps. Identify cryptographic risks, technical debt, and improvement opportunities. Partner with infrastructure, application, cloud, manufacturing, and product teams to drive remediation activities. Provide technical leadership for PKI, certificate lifecycle management, encryption services, cryptographic controls, and digital trust technologies. Support security reviews, audits, and regulatory compliance initiatives involving encryption and cryptographic controls. Develop metrics and reporting related to cryptographic maturity, readiness, and risk reduction. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Engineering, or related field. 7+ years of experience in information security, enterprise architecture, infrastructure engineering, security architecture, or related technical disciplines. Experience with PKI, certificate management, key management systems, and cryptographic protocols. Experience developing technical standards and enterprise architecture guidance. Experience supporting cloud and hybrid enterprise environments. Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills. Preferred Qualifications Experience with NIST cryptographic standards and post-quantum cryptography initiatives. Experience with certificate lifecycle automation and enterprise PKI programs. Experience supporting manufacturing, operational technology, or global enterprise environments. CISSP, CCSP, SABSA, TOGAF, or comparable certifications. Experience conducting enterprise-wide technology assessments and remediation programs. The Salary range for this position is $110,600.00 - $178,000.00 This is the lowest to highest annual full-time salary range we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. The salary range may vary for other locations.​ The successful candidate may be eligible for annual merit increases. ​ Medical, dental, life, vision, disability,401(k), Employee Stock Purchase Plan, paid time off, and tuition reimbursement in addition to programs & benefits in support of your well-being. ​ Discounts on Stanley Black & Decker tool sand other partner programs. We Don’t Just Build The World, We Build Innovative Technology Too. Joining the Stanley Black & Decker team means working in an innovative, tech-driven and highly collaborative team environment supported by over 43,500 professionals in 60 countries across the globe. Here, you’ll get the unique chance to impact some of the world’s most iconic brands including STANLEY TOOLS, DEWALT, CRAFTSMAN, MAC TOOLS and Black + Decker. Your ideas and solutions have the potential to reach millions of customers as we work together to write the next chapter in our history. Come build with us and take your career to new heights. Who We Are We’re the World’s largest tool company. We’re industry visionaries. We are committed to ensuring our state-of-the-art “smart factory” products and services provide greater quality to our customers & greater environmental and social value to our planet. Job Description Clinical Pharmacist Biologics by McKesson, Shepherdsville, KY (Onsite, Mon–Fri, 8am–5pm) Make an Impact Where It Matters Most! At Biologics by McKesson, our mission is simple but powerful: simplify access to specialty medications and deliver personalized care that helps patients achieve the best possible outcomes — one patient, one partner, one therapy at a time. As a Clinical Pharmacist, you’ll play a critical role at the intersection of clinical excellence, patient advocacy, and pharmacy operations. This is more than dispensing medication — it’s about driving safety and quality, and supporting patients through some of the most complex therapies available today. The Clinical Pharmacist serves as the clinical and operational tram player for an assigned patient care team. You will ensure safe, complaint, and compassionate pharmacy operations while acting as a trusted clinical resource for patients, caregivers, clinicians, and internal partners. And most importantly, you’ll ensure every patient receives the highest standard of care. Shift – onsite at the Shepherdsville, KY, Monday through Friday 9 – 6pm. No evenings or weekends. Target comp: $60 – $65 per hour with eligibility for a 5% MIP bonus. What You’ll Do Clinical – Patient Care Conducts a comprehensive clinical review of pharmacotherapy for each patient including drug utilization, counseling, compliance, drug interaction screening, side effect profiling and drug administration support to ensure the patient’s treatment plan is in line with evidence-based recommendations. Documents results of pharmacotherapy review in patient chart so that the nursing team performing follow-up assessments are aware and educated. Counsels patients on new drug therapy in accordance with clinical management models so that patients are educated on the specifics of their planned treatment. Completes REMS training and follows program SOPs accordingly. Job Description: About the Role The Brocade Switch and Networking (BSN) business unit of Broadcom is seeking a highly skilled Software QA Test Engineer – Brocade Switch & Networking (BSN) to test, verify, and automate the security validation of Brocade’s storage area network (SAN) based networked solutions. In this role, you will be an integral part of a high-performing test team responsible for verifying Brocade’s Fabric OS (FOS), associated hardware switching platforms, management APIs, and developing robust, automated security and functional test suites with focus on the lifecycle of the product line. The ideal candidate possesses a solid foundation in software and hardware engineering principles, a deep understanding of system quality assurance, and a proven track record of designing, executing, and automating complex test plans. We are looking for a professional who can bridge the gap between QA automation engineering and offensive/defensive cybersecurity, with hands-on experience configuring, troubleshooting, and verifying enterprise network operating systems, AAA infrastructures, and cryptographic boundaries. Primary Responsibilities As a Software QA Test Engineer focused on Security and Test Automation, you will own the end-to-end quality assurance and automation processes for critical FOS security features. Your day-to-day responsibilities will include: Security Test Strategy & Planning: Translate complex security technical specifications, regulatory standards, and break fix changes into comprehensive automated and manual test plans covering functional, integration, regression, performance, and security testing. Automation Framework Development: Design, develop, and maintain robust test automation frameworks and scripts (primarily in Python) to automate CLI and API testing, improving testing efficiency, execution speed, and coverage. Hardware & Software Backward Compatibility: Test security policy persistence, cryptographic boundary alignment, and config persistence during firmware migrations with mixed FOS versions (e.g., FOS v10.x, and v9.x). Ensure seamless security enforcement on Gen 6 and Gen 7 hardware platforms alongside modern Gen 8 platforms. SNMP: Design and execute test plans validating SNMP GET, GETNEXT, GETBULK, SET, and TRAP/INFORM operations against device MIBs. Verify custom and standard MIB objects (OIDs) return accurate, correctly typed values consistent with actual device/system state. Test SNMP trap generation, timing, and content for fault, performance, and configuration-change events. Test SNMPv1/v3 support, including authentication and encryption. Perform interoperability testing with common NMS/monitoring tools to confirm real-world compatibility. Develop and maintain automated python test scripts to Test SNMP behavior across builds and regression cycles. Identify, document, and track SNMP-related defects (incorrect OID values, missing traps, malformed responses, memory leaks under polling load) through resolution. Authentication & Multi-Factor/Federated Authentication (MFA/FA): Verifying port-level authentication (DH-CHAP E-Port and F/N-Port, FCAP E-Port) and federated authentication (FA) utilizing OAuth 2.0 / JWT tokens with external Identity Providers (IDPs) such as Azure/Entra ID, including M2M (machine-to-machine) flows. Network & Firewall Policy Validation: Test firewall policies, verifying INPUT and OUTPUT rulesets, ephemeral port restrictions, and default rate-limiting mechanisms. Secure Shell & Secure File Transfers: Test SSH/SCP/SFTP basic functionality, client/server options, SSH rekeying, host key management and outbound secure file transfers. Auditing & Event Messaging: Test secure syslog-ng, client authentication, security RAS logs, CLI history completeness, PII/CDA sanitization (GDPR compliance), and TLS/SSL failure records. Cryptographic & Certificate Management: Verify classic and quantum-safe cryptographic parameters (such as TLSv1.3 ciphers, HTTPS Key Encapsulation Mechanisms - KEM, and post-quantum algorithms like ML-DSA and ML-KEM), certificate operations, CSR generation, SAN/CN validation, and path/revocation validation. Defect Management & Advisory: Partner with development teams to identify, document, investigate, and track software defects and security vulnerabilities using industry-standard tools. Advise area leads on the overall quality status of assigned features. Qualifications & Requirements (Must Have) Education: Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering (Computer Science, Cyber Security, Electrical, or equivalent). Experience: Minimum of 8 years of hands-on software testing experience, with a heavy focus on security testing and test automation. Automation Scripting: High proficiency in Python for test automation, with hands-on experience automating APIs and CLI-based tools. QA Methodologies: Robust understanding of software testing methodologies, including functional, negative, boundary, performance, scale, and longevity/stress/soak testing. Networking & Protocols: Solid foundational knowledge of enterprise networking, routing, cryptography, and core communication protocols (TCP/IP, SSL/TLS, SSH, HTTPS, SFTP, SCP, and cryptographic handshake mechanics). Operating Systems & Virtualization: Hands-on experience with the installation, configuration, usage, and troubleshooting of Linux, Windows, VMware environments, AAA infrastructure (LDAP, RSA, RADIUS, TACACS+), Federated IDP infrastructure (SAML, OIDC), PQC infrastructure, and vulnerability/intrusive scanner applications. Storage Systems: Solid foundational knowledge of SAN/Storage technologies. Professional Skills: Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, exceptional written and verbal communication, and a proven ability to prioritize, multitask, and manage parallel projects in a fast-paced environment. Active Cybersecurity Certifications (at least one required): OSCP (Offensive Security Certified Professional), GWAPT (GIAC Web Application Penetration Tester), GXPN (GIAC Exploit Researcher and Advanced Penetration Tester), CASE (Certified Application Security Engineer - Python), CSSLP (Certified Secure Software Lifecycle Professional), or CISSP (Certified Information Systems Security Professional). Security Frameworks & Tooling: Familiarity with secure coding principles, threat modeling methodologies (e.g., STRIDE), and standard vulnerability ranking metrics (CVSS). Hands-on experience with scanners such as Qualys, Nessus, or Burp Suite. Work Arrangement: This position requires 100% on-site attendance. Highly Desired Skills & Experience Standards & Compliance: Experience with pursuing product certification or compliance with regulatory bodies and standards such as FIPS (140-3), CC (Common Criteria / NDcPP), BSI, EUCC, NIST2, DORA, and CRA. Storage Protocols: In-depth SAN protocol knowledge (Fibre Channel, FCIP, FICON). Storage Systems: Solid foundational knowledge of SAN/Storage technologies.
