If you already have a Candidate Account, please Sign-In before you apply. Job Description: The Product Owner (PO) at Broadcom sits between the Product Manager (PM) and the Development Team. The PO's primary responsibility and value come from understanding and contributing towards the product strategy, and then executing that strategy by breaking down large strategic ideas and intentions into development items with concrete outcomes and then further into manageable work items—such as enablers or user stories—with the development team. The role requires a PO to navigate priorities across the mainframe software portfolio. Broadcom's Precision design system is a modern user interface framework, including both design assets and developer SDK, that delivers a consistent and intuitive user experience adopted by over 35 mainframe products in the Mainframe Software Portfolio. These distinct products are consumers of Precision assets, and by understanding all of the varied personas and use cases along with the value of the capability in the market, the PO is to prioritize features and capabilities across the development roadmap. Delivering user experiences that differentiate from the competition and are realized in the market within the solutions at the right time. This role requires negotiation across value streams and offering teams. The PO is the voice of the customer to the development and engineering processes, ensuring the right work is done at the right time to achieve the best outcomes for our customers—both external users and internal product teams who consume Precision assets. Product Owner Core Responsibilities Operates as part of an extended Product Management team, usually reporting to Product Management. Understands how the Enterprise backlog model operates with Epics, Capabilities, Features, and User Stories. Uses Program Increment (PI) Objectives and Iteration Goals to communicate with management. Establishes and sequences backlog items based on program priorities, events, and dependencies with other teams. Coordinates with other Product Owners, the System Team, and shared services in the Agile Release Train (ART) PI Planning meetings. Works with other Product Owners and the Product Management team throughout each Iteration and PI. The Product Owner owns the Definition of Done (DoD) and sets clear Acceptance Criteria, ultimately holding final authority to accept or reject completed user stories at the end of sprints. Team Backlog Ownership The principal responsibility of the PO is to maintain a backlog of work items with order and detail sufficient for the team to work on for the current and next iteration. A story must satisfy the team’s definition of ready. Cross-Team and Management Reporting To maintain cadence across many teams globally, PO communication is key to ensure inter-team dependencies are communicated and risks to team productivity are shared and mitigated. The PO is responsible for raising information to enable management by exception and is accountable for communication with their PO peers, PM's, engineering managers and Mainframe executives if needed. Customer Engagement Our business success is driven by our customers and in turn by their success. In order to ensure our products solve our customers' challenges we continually iterate on our solutions asking our customers for their feedback. A PO works with their PM and field peers, creating opportunities to visit customers and observe users in their environment whenever possible. Regular Sprint Reviews are one of the responsibilities of the PO who decides when it is appropriate to share progress and with which internal and external stakeholders. In establishing the Sprint Review event, the PO will invite their customers describing the value they may expect to receive. Typically performed over Zoom, a Sprint Review will showcase the most recent development. When a support case is escalated to the development team for further action, the PO must be aware of the case and may manage the case to completion. Collaboration with Product Manager(s), Engineering Manager(s) and Executives The Product Owner stands back to back with the Product Manager(s) and Engineering Managers(s), working together on the same broader problems but each tackling different areas of work and levels of detail. While the Product Manager(s) are considered ‘outward facing’ meeting potential customers and buyers, the Product Owner is considered ‘inward facing,’ focused on existing customers and colleagues in development and support. The Product Manager(s) answers the question “Why” do we choose to do this. This PO role will collaborate across many product managers and solution areas to negotiate business priorities and partners with cross value stream engineering leads and executives to secure the right priority and decision when this is needed. Collaboration with Development Team Consisting of architects, UX designers, developers, QA, Information Engineers and R&D management, the Development Team produces the vast majority of consumable output and answers the question “How” will this thing get done. In this role, you will architect, build, and secure core Linux infrastructure components. Job Description: Role Overview As a Software Engineer on the ESXi OS Services team, you will lead the design and delivery of high-impact functionality across User Space OS services, container services, distributed control planes, and application infrastructure. You will help define technical direction for enterprise-class virtualization, Kubernetes platforms, and modern cloud-native workloads. Key Responsibilities Design and implement advanced operating system techniques for managing virtual systems on x86 architectures. Architect and develop scalable container services, container runtimes, and Kubernetes platform capabilities tightly integrated with ESXi and vSphere. Develop highly available platform infrastructure to run customer workloads that span across clusters and zones, supporting their specific network and storage requirements. Maintain open source code for security fixes, and upkeep upstream Kubernetes features. Drive development of platforms supporting SaaS, CaaS, and FaaS workloads. Partner closely with Product Management to define requirements and translate business needs into technical solutions. Collaborate with UI/UX designers, system architects, test teams, and cross-functional stakeholders across the organization to deliver high-quality, end-to-end solutions. History of leading System software projects/teams. Experience architecting distributed software solutions. Familiarity with cloud-native technologies, containerization (Docker/containerd), and Kubernetes architecture. You have an analytical mind and a passion for the craft of software engineering, and you love solving problems and learning new things. You are looking for an opportunity to work for a company whose software is utilized by every Fortune 500 company with profound impact across all industries. You want to be part of a collaborative team that cares about the product they build, how they create it, and the impact it has on achieving customers' business goals. The foundation of VMWare by Broadcom's virtualization technology is the ESXi hypervisor. ESXi is an operating system and virtualization infrastructure built from scratch for the explicit purpose of running virtual machines. It is the leading data center operating system in the world, and is used by most large corporations, due to its advanced capabilities, security, performance, and quality. ESXi OS Services team is responsible for all User Space aspects of the ESXi OS. This includes various operating system services, distributed control plane, container runtime and application infrastructure. You will be a hands-on Principal Software Engineer setting direction for high-impact and/or long-range strategic and technical projects. You will lead major initiatives and work with various cross-functional teams to design and deliver new functionality, targeted for distributed control planes, container runtime and new virtualization workloads. You will design and develop novel operating system techniques and algorithms for managing virtual systems in x86 architecture, developing platforms to deploy SaaS, CaaS and FaaS. You will implement advanced container runtime and Kubernetes features, with emphasis on scalability, performance, reliability, and support of upstream open-source technologies. You will work with multiple engineering teams to architect, design, implement and deliver new products based on the enterprise-class vSphere virtualization platform. You will learn the tools and processes necessary to become a successful OS Services engineer. The tool groups consist of replicated, custom, semi-custom, or purchased wafer level probers and testers performing analog DC, Linear and Non-Linear RF parametric (sampled) and wafer sort (100%) measurements. These tools are used to characterize and measure advanced silicon based MEMs wafers for development and production. The TUPE is responsible for the hardware system design and \ or specification of the tool. Each tool can be a turnkey system purchased externally, or build as a custom\semi-custom system from purchased or custom designed components and instruments. The TUPE is responsible for specifying and verifying the measurement capability of each element. The TUPE also writes the software needed to setup, interface, configure and run the testers as well as interface with the Manufacturing Execution System (MES) data systems. One of the most important items in the scope and role of the Test Unit Process Engineer (TUPE) is to fully understand the technical details of the test that is being performed and the technical details of the test equipment with which the measurement is being made. An additional critical criteria for the TUPE is to understand the accuracy and the repeatability or variance of the test being performed. Both of these critical fundamentals allow the test engineer to distinguish between the measurement system and the product being measured as a gauge of test quality. As a WSD Fab Test Unit Process Engineer (TUPE), you will have a mix of both tactical and strategic responsibilities. The tactical responsibilities of the TUPE are to keep the owned test tool sets functioning as expected ensuring the continuous flow of lots and wafers through the various test operations. The Virtual Machine Monitor Group (“Monitor Group”) is responsible for the core CPU and memory virtualization technology used in all of Broadcom's VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) Division products. You will have the opportunity to work with bleeding edge CPU technology, VT-x/AMD-V, interrupt virtualization, memory virtualization/management, and virtualization of other forms of compute technologies and accelerators. The VCF Division works to build products and solutions that power the hybrid cloud. Working alongside other highly motivated and capable engineers you will get to interact with our largest customers to define the next generation of Broadcom's industry-leading VMWare Cloud Foundation platform. Success in the Role: What are the performance outcomes over the first 6-12 months you will work toward completing? The Monitor Group’s principal function is to maintain and develop the virtual CPU and memory aspects of the virtual machine platform that runs guest operating systems. In the first 6 months, you will be expected to get up to speed with one of the specialization areas, such as new CPU feature enablement, x86_64 instruction set (ISA) virtualization, confidential computing, modernization of the monitor architecture, hardware accelerators, power-aware compute or aspects of guest timekeeping. By year 1 you would be expected to have impactful, core engineering contributions and enhancements in your area of specialization. The Work: What type of work will you be doing? What assignments, requirements, or skills will you be performing on a regular basis? This role requires you to possess a deep understanding of processor architecture and low-level OS kernel internals, system software including memory management, resource management, and interrupt architecture. The principal programming language used is C, with assembly code used whenever needed to deal with machine-specific constructs. You will work independently and as a member of a team of software engineers to design and deliver features in support of new processors or a proposed enhancement for the virtual machine monitor architecture. As an example, you might be involved in the design and implementation of upcoming CPU instruction set updates in a virtualization context. Similarly, you may be assigned to contribute to an aspect of memory virtualization/management features as part of a monitor modernization effort. For more senior roles you would be expected to make proposals that help define the design roadmap, or drive a technical effort leading other engineers. What is the leadership like for this role? What is the structure and culture of the team like? You will be joining as a Virtual Machine Monitor Engineer as part of the Monitor Group. The Monitor Group is a part of the VMWare Cloud Foundation (VCF) Division under Broadcom. This organization handles all aspects of virtual machine engineering and has deep roots in the history of the company. The Monitor Group is highly collaborative in nature, with a well-established culture of engineering discipline. Here you will have the opportunity not only to interact with other team members within the Group, but also other groups working on core aspects of vSphere. You will lead your part within the projects, as well as frequently be given the opportunity to present your work to others and learn about the novel work of other engineers. descriptionText: At Capital One, we have been relentlessly innovating since Day 1. We are a nationally recognized brand and a leading tech company touching over 100 million households. Founder-led, Capital One has grown to annualized ~$75 billion in revenue in just over 20 years.We consider ourselves the bank a technology company would build. We are the only large bank who is all-in on the cloud, and we build our own software, contributing heavily to the open-source community. We are at the frontier of AI not just in our industry, but in the world at large. Our world-class AI and ML talent (Ranted #1 in the Evident AI index for AI Talent) shapes the frontier of AI; we are in the top 5 US organizations in AI patent application volume – and our papers are routinely featured at top AI conferences (e.g., ICML, NeurIPS, etc.). Many companies claim to be tech companies – we actually live it. About the team & role: The Enterprise AI and Machine Learning (AIML) team builds the AI & ML platforms that our company leverages to build all things AI. The platforms deliver the infrastructure, foundation models, and a host of reusable capabilities that enable teams to build cutting-edge AI use cases across the business servicing, marketing, credit underwriting, fraud detection, and more. Capital One is a platform company, and these platforms are the de-facto way to build with AI at Capital One. As a Senior Business Manager on Capital One’s AIML Product Strategy team, you will apply your strategic and analytical skills to shape the destination of AI at Capital One.You will work alongside a team of strategists and our AIML senior leadership to identify the key leverage points and define the strategy for our world-leading organization. You will solve critical business problems, and help us shape Capital One’s AI strategy, in support of our mission to be at the Frontier of AI. You will do it all as part of a highly collaborative, agile team environment - where you will unlock tremendous learning and growth. Key focus areas: Setting the destination vision for our AI & ML platforms, working alongside leaders in our AI organization and business Working back from our customers and internal partners, to identify the outcomes we seek and the reusable capabilities and services we needBuild storylines and materials to roll out our AIML strategy across the company Help bring our vision to life by working with stakeholders in our lines of business and our AIML teams on “on-the-ground” problem solving Shaping our strategy and the continuous delivery and improvement of our AI platform capabilitiesWho we are looking for:We are looking for a general athlete, strategic and analytical thinker, and a world-class communicator. title: Senior Account Executive - Mid Market ,  New York Metro Area -Financial Services
descriptionText: 1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $400M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing. About 1Password At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work. If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future. As a Senior Commercial Account Executive, you will own a focused territory of strategic high growth accounts and existing customers with 500-2,500 employees, with an emphasis on Fortune 1000 organizations. Your mandate is to create new executive relationships, build qualified pipeline, win complex multi-product platform opportunities, expand 1Password’s strategic footprint across an existing book of business and secure new logos to add to our customer base. This is not a transactional or single-product sales role. You will lead an enterprise-wide security conversation, starting with a customer’s most urgent problem and building the strategic case for Unified Access across humans, AI agents, and machines. You will engage and multi-thread with CISOs, CIOs, IT and security leaders, IAM teams, DevOps and platform teams, engineering leaders, security architects, finance, procurement, and other executive stakeholders. The Senior Commercial Account Executive role also requires experience selling to financial-services organizations headquartered in or operating from New York City. You will bring sector fluency and demonstrated experience and understanding of how to navigate and win within complex financial institutions. This is a remote, field-based opportunity. Candidates must be based in the New York metro area and should expect regular in-person customer meetings, industry events, and travel throughout the territory, including travel to New York City as required. How we’re using AI today Across GTM, we’re transforming the way we work with AI. We expect every seller, CSM, and team member to become a power user, using it daily to work smarter and move faster. AI is already embedded in how we operate – from real-time coaching that sharpens how we sell and interact with customers, to surfacing insights that help us anticipate needs – creating more time for meaningful customer engagement. If you’re excited to reshape how you think, make decisions, and drive growth with AI, you’ll feel right at home here. Note: All go-to market roles will have an in-person onboarding in Toronto. What we're looking for: - 6+ years experience selling to Fortune 1000 organizations and high growth companies spanning 500-2,500 employees, with 2+ years of substantial cybersecurity sales experience. - A consistent record of exceeding $1.5M+ annual quotas, including experience carrying quotas in the $1.5M-$3M+ range and closing complex, multi-product opportunities. - Multiple years of elite sales performance and company recognition, such as President’s Club or equivalent top-performer awards. - Demonstrated success selling multi-product platforms and broader solution transformations, rather than only transactional or standalone point products. - Experience selling identity, Zero Trust, cloud security, endpoint security, privileged access, developer security, or adjacent cybersecurity platforms. - Established, credible relationships with enterprise CISOs, CIOs, senior security and IT leaders, IAM leaders, and identity/security architects within the territory or relevant named-account segment. - Proven ability to engage IAM, IT security, DevOps, platform engineering, and engineering leaders and connect their technical priorities to an executive business case. - A record of winning net-new strategic logos and expanding existing accounts through cross-sell, upsell, and multi-year platform agreements. - Strong executive presence and the ability to communicate credibly with C-suite leaders and deeply technical audiences. - Rigorous account planning, pipeline creation, opportunity management, forecasting, and negotiation skills. Bonus points for: - Strong knowledge of identity and access management, privileged access management, credential security, machine identities, agentic AI security, SaaS governance, device trust, or secrets management. - Experience competing and winning against major enterprise identity and cybersecurity platform providers. - Proficiency with MEDDPPICC, Salesforce, Slack, Zoom, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Outreach, and AI-enabled sales tools. - Experience developing opportunities through channel partners, cloud alliances, systems integrators, or technology partners. What you can expect: Own and grow a strategic commercial territory - Develop and execute sophisticated account and territory plans across your customer and prospect book. - Create new executive relationships with CISOs, CIOs, identity leaders, security architects, and other senior technology buyers to accelerate access and credibility. - Identify whitespace, competitive displacement opportunities, and compelling events across identity security, AI adoption, privileged access, SaaS governance, developer workflows, and device security. - Build and maintain the pipeline coverage, account engagement, and deal velocity required to consistently achieve or exceed a significant annual quota. Sell the full platform story - Elevate conversations from an individual point-product need to a strategic Unified Access vision spanning people, AI agents, and machines. - Connect 1Password’s capabilities to measurable outcomes, including reducing credential and access risk, eliminating standing privilege, governing SaaS and shadow AI, protecting developer and machine workflows, strengthening device trust, and improving auditability. - Land with the customer’s most urgent use case, then build an executive-backed roadmap for adoption and expansion across Enterprise Password Manager, SaaS Manager, Credential Broker, Device Trust, and Privileged Access. - Translate complex identity, access, cloud, endpoint, developer, and AI-security concepts into clear business value for executive and deeply technical audiences. Lead complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles - Orchestrate 4-6+ month sales cycles involving security, IAM, IT, DevOps, platform engineering, application engineering, finance, legal, procurement, and executive sponsors. - Build consensus across large buying groups and establish clear business, technical, economic, and decision criteria. - Lead executive presentations, discovery sessions, workshops, business-value assessments, commercial negotiations, and close plans. - Create and maintain mutual action plans and apply MEDDPPICC or a comparable enterprise qualification methodology with discipline. - Structure and negotiate complex, multi-year, multi-product agreements with material ARR and platform expansion potential. Expand strategic customer relationships - Build broad, durable relationships throughout customer organizations rather than relying on a single champion. - Uncover business and security priorities beyond the initial use case and turn them into platform expansion opportunities. - Partner with Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, product specialists, and services teams to create adoption and expansion plans tied to measurable outcomes. Operate as one team - Collaborate closely with BDR, Solutions Engineering, Channels, Alliances, Customer Success, Onboarding, Product, Marketing, Legal, and Deal Desk. - Co-sell with strategic partners, cloud alliances, channel teams, and systems integrators where they can expand reach or accelerate a decision. - Represent 1Password at executive briefings, customer meetings, trade shows, and industry events. - Maintain accurate opportunity data, next steps, forecasts, and account plans in Salesforce. - Use AI and modern selling tools thoughtfully to improve research, preparation, coaching, and execution while creating more time for customer engagement. New York financial-services expertise: - Significant experience selling complex cybersecurity platforms to major banks, capital-markets firms, insurers, asset managers, fintech companies, or other financial institutions headquartered in or operating from New York City. - Ability to build a network of CISO, CIO, CTO, security, identity, infrastructure, cloud, engineering, architecture, risk, and procurement leaders within New York financial-services accounts, relationships you can confidently activate to open strategic conversations. - Strong familiarity with financial-services buying cycles, including security and architecture review, third-party risk management, regulatory and compliance requirements, procurement, legal review, testing, implementation planning, and executive approval. - Working knowledge of the technology stacks and infrastructure common to large financial institutions, including hybrid and multi-cloud environments, identity and privileged-access systems, endpoint controls, developer platforms, legacy infrastructure, and highly regulated production environments. - A demonstrated record of mapping complex stakeholder groups, building internal consensus, navigating incumbents and competitive dynamics, and winning large, multi-year cybersecurity agreements within New York financial-services accounts. How you work: - You lead with curiosity and strong discovery, uncovering the broader security and business problem rather than stopping at the initial product request. - You create a compelling platform narrative while keeping the customer’s priorities, maturity, and path to value at the center. - You combine strategic thinking with operating rigor; your account plans, pipeline, forecasts, and close plans are current, specific, and dependable. - You are resilient, accountable, collaborative, and motivated by ambitious targets and complex opportunities. - You hunt daily for new opportunities and consistently hit pipeline generation targets. - You leverage AI daily to expedite your administrative work and identify strategic opportunities across your book. - You are coachable, apply feedback quickly, and continuously improve your craft. - You thrive in a remote, field-based environment and prioritize meaningful in-person customer engagement. USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $96,000 USD and $139,000 USD, and is commission-eligible. This role is also immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs. At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set. This posting is for an existing vacancy. Our culture At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone https://blog.1password.com/inside-the-culture-powering-1passwords-next-chapter/. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. How we work with AI We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password. This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to

title: Principle Engineer
descriptionText: 岗位定位 面向电动工具及相关机电系统的下一代技术发展需求，负责先进控制理论、系统建模方法、CAE AI应用及模型驱动开发体系的研究与落地。该岗位将聚焦复杂机电系统的控制与建模前沿方向，探索可转化为产品竞争力和研发效率提升的关键技术，并推动相关研究成果在平台开发、新产品预研和软件开发流程中的工程化应用。 本岗位适合具有扎实控制理论基础、较强科研创新能力和工程转化意识的高层次博士人才。 核心职责 1. 前沿控制与系统建模研究 面向电动工具及相关复杂机电系统，开展先进控制理论、系统建模方法和智能化研发技术研究。 研究鲁棒控制、自适应控制、优化控制、智能控制、数据驱动建模等方向在实际产品中的应用潜力。 跟踪国内外前沿技术发展趋势，识别对未来产品平台和研发体系具有战略价值的关键技术方向。 2. CAE AI与智能工程方法探索 探索CAE与AI融合技术在产品设计、性能预测、参数优化、故障分析和研发提效中的应用。 推动仿真驱动、数据驱动和模型驱动方法在电动工具研发中的结合应用。 研究面向复杂系统的智能建模、代理模型、参数识别、虚拟验证等新方法。 3. 基于System Modeling的软件开发方法建设 推动基于System Modeling / Model-Based Development的软件开发方法在控制系统开发中的应用。 建立从系统需求、功能建模、控制设计、仿真验证到软件实现的开发流程与方法框架。 支持控制策略、系统架构和软件实现之间的一致性设计与验证。 4. 研究成果工程化转化 将前沿研究成果转化为可复用的研发方法、分析工具、建模规范、设计标准和技术平台能力。 支持研发团队将先进控制与建模方法应用于新产品开发、平台开发和关键技术攻关。 与机械、电子、电机、软件、测试等团队协同，推动研究成果在工程场景中的落地与验证。 5. 技术影响力与创新体系建设 参与或主导高水平技术课题、联合研究项目和外部技术合作。 推动专利、论文、技术白皮书、内部方法论和标准体系建设。 为团队提供系统控制、建模仿真和智能研发方向的技术指导，提升组织在前沿技术领域的能力积累。 任职资格 教育背景 博士学历，控制科学与工程、电气工程、自动化、系统工程、机电控制、机械电子工程或相关专业。 优先考虑国内外Top高校或知名研究团队背景。 研究与工作经验 具备先进控制、系统建模、模型驱动开发、智能控制、CAE相关方向的深入研究基础。 有复杂机电系统、电驱系统、机器人、汽车电控、工业装备、航空航天控制或相关领域研究/开发经验者优先。 具备将理论研究转化为工程方法、工具链或产品能力的经验者优先。 有高水平论文、核心专利、重大科研项目或产学研合作经历者优先。 专业能力 具备扎实的控制理论基础，对系统动力学、建模、控制与优化有深入理解。 熟悉一种或多种先进控制方法，如鲁棒控制、自适应控制、最优控制、预测控制、智能控制等。 熟悉系统建模、仿真分析和模型驱动开发方法，能够建立复杂系统的分析与设计框架。 了解CAE工具链、数据驱动方法、AI在工程研发中的应用逻辑。 具备较强的软件思维，理解控制算法到软件实现的转化过程。 具备优秀的科研能力、问题抽象能力、技术判断能力和跨团队协同能力。 优先条件 有MATLAB/Simulink、Modelica、AMESim、Ansys Twin Builder、Python或相关建模/仿真/算法工具使用经验。 有数字孪生、虚拟验证、代理模型、参数辨识、智能优化等方向经验者优先。 有电动工具、园林工具、手持设备或高动态机电产品相关经验者优先。 有技术路线规划、平台方法建设或研究团队带领经验者优先。 关键产出方向 前沿控制与系统建模方向的技术突破与方法沉淀 CAE AI与模型驱动开发在研发流程中的应用落地 支撑新产品平台开发的建模、分析与控制方法体系 高价值专利、论文、技术标准及内部研发资产 组织在先进控制与智能工程方向的能力提升 We Don’t Just Build The World, We Build Innovative Technology Too. title: Legal Counsel, Emergency Cash & U.S. Programs
descriptionText: GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We support high ownership and real professional growth. Curious about what it's really like to work here? Read our values and hear from the people who do. If they resonate, this could be a great fit! About this role GiveDirectly is building a faster model for humanitarian response – using data, technology, and partnerships to identify people affected by crises and deliver cash within days. Making that possible requires legal pathways that can be established before a crisis and activated quickly when one occurs. We are seeking a Counsel to build and lead that legal model. Approximately 70% of the role will focus on Emergency Cash, from preparing for future responses to leading the legal and regulatory work required during an active emergency. When a response is underway, EC work will take priority. You will also serve as legal partner to GiveDirectly’s U.S. programs, which work with governments, funders, researchers, and community organizations to deliver cash to low-income Americans. The portfolio includes programs such as Rx Kids, guaranteed-income initiatives, and housing-stability programs. You will help teams design and expand these programs, structure partnerships, and navigate the legal issues affecting delivery and recipients. This is a delivery-focused role for a practical lawyer who can build for scale, exercise clear judgment under pressure, and help ambitious programs move from idea to implementation. Reports to: Head of Legal Level: Senior Manager Location: Remote, with a requirement to overlap with an East Africa timezone by at least 3 hours. We can only employ people in certain places at the moment, so it's worth checking our current list of eligible countries to see if yours is included. If you're based elsewhere, it's not an automatic no, but do flag it early with your recruiter. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas in the U.S. or U.K. at this time. Travel Requirement: ~ 3–4 trips per year, plus travel as needed during active emergency responses. What you’ll do: Build and deliver the Emergency Cash legal model Serve as the primary legal partner to Emergency Cash across program strategy, design, launch, and delivery. Build a repeatable legal model for emergency responses, including approaches to country entry, regulatory review, government engagement, contracting, data use, and the engagement of local counsel. Develop response-readiness tools, templates, and decision frameworks that allow common issues to be addressed quickly while escalating matters requiring legal judgment. During active responses, lead the legal work needed to launch and operate on emergency timelines, providing clear recommendations when information is incomplete. Coordinate with country teams, program-facing Counsel, and local advisors to use existing knowledge and relationships while retaining legal ownership of the response. Apply GiveDirectly’s global standards for MNO data and remote enablement to individual responses, working with the Corporate & Strategic Affairs Counsel on novel or cross-cutting issues. Draft and negotiate the partnership, technology, vendor, data-sharing, and other agreements required to deliver emergency programs. Capture lessons from individual responses and use them to strengthen the EC legal model over time. Lead legal support for U.S. programs Serve as legal partner to GiveDirectly’s U.S. programs across program design, implementation, expansion, and ongoing operations. Advise on the legal design and delivery of U.S. cash programs, including eligible recipient populations, interactions with public benefits, tax treatment and reporting, payments involving minors or caregivers, family-law considerations, privacy and data use, and state-specific requirements. Structure and negotiate program-specific agreements with governments, research institutions, community organizations, payment providers, and other partners. Develop reusable guidance for recurring issues and coordinate state-specific or specialist counsel where needed. Contribute across Legal Work with the Corporate & Business Affairs Counsel on organization-wide standards and initiatives affecting Emergency Cash or U.S. programs. Partner with the Africa Programs & Country Operations Counsel when emergency responses occur in countries within that role’s portfolio. Work with Legal Operations support to delegate recurring contracting, research, coordination, and administrative work appropriately. Support other priority legal matters as needed as part of a small, global Legal team. What you’ll bring: Exceptional alignment with GiveDirectly Values and active demonstration of our core competencies: emotional intelligence, problem solving, project management, follow-through, and fostering inclusivity. We welcome and strongly encourage applications from candidates who have personal or professional experience in the low-income and/or historically marginalized communities that we serve. Qualification as an attorney in at least one jurisdiction, with relevant post-qualification legal experience. Experience advising on complex program, commercial, or regulatory matters in fast-moving or high-pressure environments. Strong commercial contracting skills, including drafting and negotiating complex partnership, technology, vendor, or data-related agreements. Ability to quickly understand unfamiliar legal and regulatory frameworks and advise where precedent, time, or information is limited. Strong legal and business judgment, including the ability to identify meaningful risks, assess tradeoffs, and recommend a practical path forward. Ability to translate complex legal requirements into clear, actionable guidance for colleagues without legal backgrounds. Experience coordinating external counsel, consultants, or other specialist advisors. Working knowledge of data privacy and data protection law. Ability to operate independently, manage competing priorities, and reprioritize quickly during active emergency responses. Excellent written and verbal communication skills; English fluency. Preferred: Experience in emergency response, humanitarian operations, or other crisis-context legal work. Experience supporting the launch of programs or operations in new countries. Experience with U.S. public-benefits, family-law, charitable-assistance, or government-program matters. Experience working across multiple jurisdictions, particularly in emerging markets. Experience supporting programs involving vulnerable populations or sensitive personal data. Experience in international development or another mission-driven organization. Compensation At GiveDirectly, we strive to pay our employees generously and equitably. We use an accredited third party salary aggregator to calculate what we believe to be competitive pay based on role, location, and cost of living. We also have a no negotiation policy to ensure we are paying staff equitably across roles. Read more about our compensation philosophy here. Unless otherwise noted, the benefits stipend may be used to cover benefits or taken as additional taxable income. Beyond direct care, the role drives quality assurance and operational compliance by auditing clinical documentation, monitoring outcome metrics such as CORE-10, preventing clinical drift, and managing affiliate network relationships and onboarding. Requiring a Master’s degree in Clinical or Counseling Psychology, three to six years of progressive clinical experience—preferably in EAP or corporate mental health environments—and fluency in English and Hindi, the Jr. CCM blends high-level clinical risk assessment with detail-oriented case management to ensure high quality, scalable care across the provider network.Purpose of the Job: To manage clinical operations, facilitate referrals, and monitor the quality of care delivered by the provider network.It is a permanent position focused on operationalizing high-quality clinical care.Working Hours: 48 hours per week.Schedule: 5 or 6 days a week; various shifts may be applicable.Hybrid Work: Hybrid working can be considered as per the need of the job.Responsibilities: 1. Helpline & Crisis ManagementServe as the primary first point of contact for employees and their dependents accessing the Lyra helpline via telephone, live chat, or email.Provide immediate "in-the-moment" clinical support to callers in distress, utilizing psychological first aid and stabilization techniques.Conduct comprehensive clinical risk assessments for every contact to identify potential self-harm, ideation, or risk to others, adhering to Lyra’s established risk protocols.Manage emergency interventions and coordinate with local emergency services or internal senior clinical leads when high-risk situations are identified.2. Clinical Intake & TriageConduct detailed clinical intake interviews to assess the user’s presenting concerns, history, and level of psychological distress.Evaluate the appropriateness of short-term counseling versus higher-acuity care pathways based on the clinical assessment.Utilize internal decision-making frameworks to assign clients to the most suitable professional within the in-house team or the partner provider network, matching based on clinical specialty and language preference.Accurately capture and document all clinical intake data, including CORE-10 scores and work impact metrics, in the database to ensure a seamless handover to the treating clinician.3. Delivery of Clinical SessionsProvide high-quality, professional counseling and psychotherapy sessions to clients within a structured, short-term framework.Utilize evidence-based interventions (such as CBT or solution-focused therapy) to address client queries and specific mental health concerns.Ensure all clinical sessions are workplace-focused when appropriate, helping the service user improve their level of functioning and productivity.Maintain accurate, contemporaneous clinical notes for every session, ensuring they meet the legal and professional standards of the Indian healthcare landscape.Monitor client progress through regular outcome measurement and adjust the treatment plan as necessary, or escalate to the Senior CCM for complex case review.4. Documentation Oversight & Quality AssuranceConduct systematic monitoring of all active clinical cases from initiation to closure to ensure strict adherence to Lyra’s clinical documentation standards.Proactively follow up with internal clinicians and affiliate providers to secure missing or delayed clinical notes, treatment plans, and discharge summaries.Audit case files for the accurate inclusion of outcome measurements, specifically tracking the consistent use of CORE-10 and work impact scores.Ensure all clinical documentation is captured within the database in a timely manner, maintaining a high standard of data integrity for audit readiness.Identify and escalate recurring documentation gaps to the Senior CCM to facilitate targeted provider training and performance management.5. Affiliate Network & Specialty SupportServe as the primary point of operational contact for the partner provider network, offering continuous support regarding administrative and portal requirements.Maintain and verify the accuracy of the affiliate database, ensuring all partner providers have professional, updated bios that reflect their current clinical expertise.Routinely audit and update provider specialties and language proficiencies to ensure the intake team can perform precise referral matching.Assist in the onboarding process by training new affiliates on Lyra’s specific clinical protocols, risk management procedures, and case referral workflows.Support partner providers in navigating cross-border referral processes and understanding local compliance nuances.6. Protocol AdherenceIntervention Alignment: Rigorously audit treatment plans to ensure all clinical interventions align with Lyra’s evidence-based, short-term, and solution-focused models.Workplace Focus Integration: Evaluate clinical goals to ensure they are specifically designed to improve the service user’s level of functioning within the workplace, focusing on "Work Impact" and productivity restoration.Goal-Oriented Care: Verify that every treatment plan includes clear, measurable objectives that can be reasonably achieved within the prescribed short-term session limit.Clinical Gatekeeping: Identify and address "clinical drift" where therapy may be deviating from the brief intervention framework or losing its workplace-centric focus.Standardized Assessment Review: Monitor the consistent application of clinical outcome measures (such as CORE-10) to validate that the intervention protocol is resulting in measurable symptom reduction.Provider Consultation: Provide direct feedback and consultation to partner providers when treatment plans do not meet Lyra’s specific clinical protocols or service level agreements.Case Escalation: Manage the transition of cases that require longer-term or higher-acuity care, ensuring the handover remains compliant with Lyra’s global clinical standards and local professional guidelines.7. MiscellaneousUpholding Lyra Values: Act as a brand ambassador by consistently demonstrating Lyra’s core values of clinical excellence, innovation, and empathy in every interaction with colleagues, providers, and service users.Task Ownership & Accountability: Ensure all allotted clinical and administrative tasks are performed with high precision and within agreed-upon Service Level Agreements (SLAs).Process Optimization Initiatives: Proactively identify gaps in current workflows and take the initiative to propose and implement solutions that enhance operational efficiency and clinical outcomes.Cross-Functional Coordination: Collaborate seamlessly with the Clinical Lead, Client Success, and Product teams to ensure the delivery of the highest quality care to both clients (companies) and individual customers.Workshop Delivery & Training: Participate in opportunities to deliver onsite or online workshops and training sessions for client organizations as requested.Content Creation: Contribute to the development of clinical content, training manuals, and affiliate-facing materials to maintain Lyra’s position as a thought leader in mental health.Event Participation: Represent Lyra Health at professional events, webinars, and industry conferences to promote Lyra’s transformative care model and clinical research.Experience: Qualification: Masters in Clinical or Counseling Psychology; RCI registration is desirable.Experience Level: 3–6 years of progressive working experience in a clinical setting.Specialized Experience: Strong preference for candidates with a background in EAP or workplace mental health, particularly with work-impact cases.Global Exposure: Experience navigating diverse healthcare systems and cultural nuances is preferred.Technical Skills: Proficiency in Google Suite and CRM systems.Linguistic Skills: Must be bilingual in Hindi and English.About You:Clinical Acumen: Strong clinical understanding with the ability to identify and assess clinical risk within a case management framework.Problem Solver: Analytical approach to solving operational bottlenecks and navigating network challenges.Autonomous & Accountable: Able to manage individual caseload responsibilities and escalate clinical concerns accurately.Detail-Oriented: Meticulous attention to detail in monitoring clinical notes and auditing outcome measurements (CORE-10).Communicator: Clear verbal and written skills for managing relationships with external providers and internal teams.Proactive & Adaptive: Continuous improvement mindset to refine referral and coordination processes.Organized: Exceptional ability to prioritize operational tasks and meet reporting deadlines under pressure.Collaborative: Collaborates effectively with internal stakeholders to achieve a seamless global account experience."We are an

descriptionText: About TailorCare TailorCare is transforming the experience of specialty care. Our comprehensive care program takes a profoundly personal, evidence-based approach to improving patient outcomes for joint, back, and muscle conditions. By carefully assessing patients' symptoms, health histories, preferences, and goals with predictive data and the latest evidence-based guidelines, we help patients choose and navigate the most effective treatment pathway for them every step of the way. TailorCare values the experiences and perspectives of individuals from all backgrounds. We are a highly collaborative, curious, and determined team passionate about scaling a high-growth start-up to improve the lives of those in pain. TailorCare is a remote-first company with our corporate office located in Nashville. About the Role As a Care Advocate, you will be responsible for engaging prospective patients through proactive outbound calls and multichannel outreach to drive awareness and enrollment in TailorCare’s musculoskeletal (MSK) care navigation program. You’ll often serve as the first point of contact, guiding patients through the value of our services and creating a personalized, empathetic, and compelling experience. This is a high-volume, outbound call center role focused on healthcare engagement, where you will connect with patients and their caregivers to identify barriers and motivate them to take action toward improved musculoskeletal (MSK) care. This is a non-exempt (hourly) position. Location & Schedule This is a 100% remote role. Candidates must be available to work hours aligned with Eastern, Central, or Mountain Time Zones. Responsibilities Conduct high-volume outbound calls and multichannel outreach (phone, SMS, email) to eligible patients to introduce TailorCare’s services and support program enrollment. Build and maintain a working knowledge of TailorCare’s MSK program, including core conditions, care pathways, eligibility criteria, and the enrollment process, to explain the program clearly and accurately. Clearly and empathetically communicate TailorCare’s value proposition, tailoring the conversation to patient goals, health literacy, concerns, and motivations. Build trust and rapport quickly using active listening, genuine empathy, and a compassionate approach that puts patients at ease and encourages engagement. Develop and apply foundational motivational interviewing (MI) techniques — including open-ended questioning, affirmations, reflective listening, and summarizing — to support patient-centered conversations. Identify and address common patient questions, barriers, or objections using established techniques while maintaining a calm, supportive tone; seek guidance and escalate appropriately when patient needs or situations fall outside your scope. Demonstrate empathy, professionalism, and consistency across all patient interactions, representing TailorCare’s values and mission. Document all patient interactions accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner within internal systems to support care coordination, data integrity, and reporting. Meet or exceed performance targets related to outreach volume, patient engagement, caseload management, and call quality. Use personal performance data and coaching feedback to identify trends in your own outreach and drive continuous self-improvement. Use AI-enabled tools and new technologies with curiosity, openness, and responsibility to improve personal productivity and outreach effectiveness. Adapt to changing scripts, tools, and workflows with a positive, growth-oriented mindset. Coordinate patient handoffs with internal care teams. Participate in regular team meetings and daily standups, contributing to a positive, inclusive culture of learning and collaboration. Surface observations, feedback, and ideas on patient trends, outreach barriers, or script effectiveness to appropriate team members for continuous improvement. Perform other duties as assigned. Qualifications Required: Experience in outbound call center, inside sales, telephonic outreach, or patient engagement roles—preferably in a healthcare, health plan, or health tech environment. Strong written and verbal communication, persuasion, and active listening skills. Willingness to learn and apply motivational interviewing techniques in patient conversations. Ability to manage a high call volume while maintaining accuracy and empathy. Comfortable working with productivity targets and quality metrics in a fast-paced, tech-enabled environment. Ability to use personal performance data and feedback to drive self-improvement. High comfort level with technology, including contact center platforms, CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce), documentation tools, and Google Suite. Openness and adaptability to new technologies, including responsible use of AI-enabled tools. Ability to effectively collaborate with multidisciplinary teams. Excellent organizational and prioritization skills. Strong attention to detail. Ability and willingness to travel up to 10% as needed for onsite meetings, team collaboration, and company events. Preferred: Familiarity with motivational interviewing and/or patient coaching strategies. Experience working with Medicare populations and a basic understanding of Medicare Health Plans. Knowledge of medical terminology. Previous experience with remote/telemedicine care delivery. descriptionText: About Us: Grow was born to tackle a critical challenge: making mental health care more effective and accessible for everyone. Since launching in 2020, 15 million sessions have started on Grow, and we've barely scratched the surface. We do it through a three-sided marketplace that empowers providers, augments insurance payors, and serves patients. Every solution we build reveals ten more waiting to be delivered, and that's just what gets us going. We've backed that ambition with more than $328M in funding, including our Series D at a $3B valuation from Sequoia Capital, Transformation Capital, TCV, SignalFire, Menlo Ventures, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, and others. At Grow, the work you do can literally change someone's life. Your work here doesn't stay on a screen; it impacts whether someone can find, afford, and access quality care. That ambition sets us apart, and offers you an endless runway to impact one of the world's most urgent issues. We don’t have passenger seats here. Everyone is driving something that matters. This work deserves real commitment. So if you thrive on meeting problems head on, untangling serious complexity, and working at pace with the sharpest yet kindest people around, you've come to the right place. About Us: Grow Therapy is on a mission to serve as the trusted partner for therapists growing their practice, and patients accessing high-quality care. Powered by technology, we are a three-sided marketplace that empowers providers, augments insurance payors, and serves patients. Following the mass increase in depression and anxiety, the need for accessibility is more important than ever. To make our vision for mental healthcare a reality, we’re building a team of entrepreneurs and mission-driven go-getters. Since launching in February 2021, we’ve empowered more than ten thousand therapists and hundreds of thousands of clients across the country and insurance landscape. We’ve raised more than $178mm of funding from Sequoia Capital, Transformation Capital, TCV, SignalFire, and others. The Opportunity: As Staff Product Manager for Grow's New Models & Markets team, you'll own new products and business offerings within Grow, particularly in the payor and EAP space. Behavioral health access is no longer the industry's biggest challenge — now payors (health insurers) are grappling with how to manage cost, quality, and outcomes at scale. As a Staff PM, you will be responsible for both deepening our partnerships with payors, as well as building an entirely new category of B2B offering for employers. You'll be expected to shape both the strategy and the build as you go. This role calls for someone who thinks in systems — not just features — and who can move fluidly between high-level strategy and the tactical complexities of the healthcare ecosystem. What You’ll Be Doing: - Own the next phase of Grow's strategic payor partnership roadmap, including deepening existing partnerships. - Define the product vision and MVP for Grow's next generation EAP offering, building on our existing early customers and first generation offering. - Design for the full pathway a client, employer, or payor takes through Grow's systems — thinking at the systems level, not just the feature level. - Partner directly with our VP of Corporate Development to shape how Grow approaches new payor and employer partnership models. - Navigate the tactical complexity of authorizations, contracts, and payor requirements as part of building something that's still early at Grow. - Shape an early-stage offering from the ground-up, contributing real strategic and product vision along the way – not just executing against a defined spec. You’ll Be a Good Fit If: - You've worked as a Staff-level Product Manager (or equivalent scope), with a track record of owning strategy for a full end-to-end surface area, not just a feature set. - You have experience in healthcare and are intellectually curious about solving hard problems within healthcare. - You've taken something early-stage and defined its direction in a high-ambiguity space before, and you're energized by defining scope rather than being handed it. - You have experience in a role that blends strategy, partnerships, and product execution. - You know how to balance short-term wins with long-term platform investments and focus on what drives the most impact. - A track record of owning outcomes, not just outputs — you care about whether the thing you shipped actually moved the needle. - Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and deliver impactful products in a fast-paced environment. - Excellent communication skills with the ability to influence across levels. Nice to have: - Deep familiarity with authorizations and payor mechanics — you understand how insurance contracts, claims, and reimbursement actually work. Employment Type: Full Time Base Compensation: The base compensation range for this position is $200,000–$250,000 USD Annually. This is a hybrid role with the expectation to work onsite from our NYC, San Francisco, or Seattle hub location three days per week (Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday) and travel 2–3 times per year (e.g., company and department offsites). The base compensation for this role will vary depending on several factors, including relevant experience, qualifications, and the candidate’s working location. descriptionText: GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We support high ownership and real professional growth. Curious about what it's really like to work here? Read our values and hear from the people who do. If they resonate, this could be a great fit! Background : GiveDirectly (GD) vise à remodeler les dons internationaux - et des millions de vies - en fournissant des subventions en espèces directement aux plus pauvres du monde. The Brookings Institution estime que 70 milliards de dollars de transferts en espèces seraient nécessaires pour éliminer le fossé de la pauvreté ; le secteur de l'aide dépense actuellement 135 milliards de dollars par an, dont une grande partie pour des interventions non fondées sur des données probantes. GiveDirectly veut changer cela, en faisant des transferts d'argent liquide une référence pour l'aide étrangère - comme le fonds indiciel est une référence pour l'industrie financière - et en accélérant ainsi la fin de l'extrême pauvreté. GD a levé plus de 700 millions de dollars depuis son lancement en 2011, distribué de l'argent à plus d'un million de personnes et ouvert des bureaux dans 10 pays. Nous avons également soutenu des recherches expérimentales à grande échelle qui indiquent un fort impact de nos programmes sur les bénéficiaires. En conséquence, GD a été reconnue comme l'une des organisations à but non lucratif les plus innovantes par Fast Company, tandis que le mouvement croissant des transferts d'argent liquide (et le rôle de premier plan joué par la GD dans ce cadre) a fait l'objet d'un article dans le magazine New York Times Magazine, This American Life, Foreign Affairs, et The Economist. GiveDirectly offre la possibilité de travailler avec des personnes originaires de 21 pays différents et parlant 69 langues différentes. Nous travaillons activement à la mise en place d'un environnement équitable et inclusif pour tous les membres de l'équipe, et notre personnel apporte des perspectives et des expériences diverses à notre organisation. Dans nos bureaux du monde entier, notre culture est franche, analytique, non hiérarchique et rapide. Nous valorisons les capacités, l'adaptabilité et la volonté d'apprendre. À propos de GiveDirectly en RD Congo : GiveDirectly RDC a été créé en 2018 afin de permettre des transferts monétaires aux populations pauvres et rurales via les téléphones portables, afin de promouvoir la sécurité alimentaire, la réduction de la pauvreté et l’inclusion financière. Nous souhaitions démontrer la faisabilité opérationnelle et la rentabilité du transfert d’importants volumes monétaires sous forme numérique dans l’un des pays les moins développés du monde. Depuis sa création, il y a quatre ans, GiveDirectly RDC a utilisé les téléphones mobiles pour transférer plus de 14 millions de dollars à plus de 65 000 bénéficiaires dans quatre provinces : Sud-Kivu, Nord-Kivu, Ituri et Kinshasa. Les activités de GiveDirectly en RDC se sont développées de manière à inclure, notamment : des preuves de concept convaincantes des transferts d’argent liquide basés sur les téléphones portables ; la mise en œuvre de technologies innovantes de ciblage des populations urbaines défavorisées de Kinshasa, en collaboration avec l’agence de protection sociale de la RDC, le Fonds Social de la RDC ; la livraison d’argent liquide sans contact aux bénéficiaires de Beni et Bunia affectés par les conséquences économiques de la COVID-19. Vous rejoindrez Give Directly RDC à un moment passionnant de son histoire, alors que nous mettons en place et espérons lancer plusieurs nouveaux programmes et renforcer notre partenariat avec le gouvernement de la RDC. SUPERVISEUR TERRAIN & CONTROLEUR DE RISQUE Taches et Responsabilitesa propos du rôle Le Superviseur terrain & Contrôleur de risque, sur le terrain joue un rôle essentiel pour garantir que GiveDirectly offre un service d'excellence aux donateurs et aux bénéficiaires. Véritable interlocuteur/trice privilégié(e) de l'organisation sur le terrain, il/elle sera chargé(e) de synthétiser régulièrement les informations relatives aux performances de l'équipe, ainsi qu'aux réussites et aux difficultés rencontrées. Ils travailleront en toute indépendance et séparément des autres équipes du programme. Ils seront totalement isolés des autres équipes de terrain. Le Superviseur terrain & Contrôleur de risque dirigera une équipe d'audit des programmes qui surveillera, détectera et résoudra les risques liés aux programmes, tels que la fraude et les violations des règles de sécurité, grâce à divers flux de travail, y compris des enquêtes sur le terrain.Ils seront responsables de l'ensemble du processus d'audit du programme, notamment du suivi des performances de leurs équipes, de l'atteinte des objectifs en matière d'enquêtes et de résolution de cas, de la mise en place d'une culture de mentorat et de développement professionnel, du suivi des tendances en matière de risques liés aux projets et de l'identification des opportunités d'atténuation des risques et d'amélioration des processus. Ce poste exigera un jugement sûr sur les questions et les défis opérationnels, de solides compétences en communication et en relations interpersonnelles, une gestion exceptionnelle du personnel et un engagement ferme envers les valeurs, la mission et le modèle de GiveDirectly. As the Sr. Compensation Strategy Manager, this role will independently own complex, high‑stakes work from concept through execution while shaping how executive rewards reinforce performance, leadership expectations, and business outcomes. The Sr. Compensation Strategy Manager is a senior individual contributor who serves as a trusted advisor of executive compensation programs aligned with the business strategy, performance outcomes, and leadership priorities. This role will lead: Enterprise-wide program design, governance & compliance Market intelligence & analytics Executive cycles & transactions Enterprise alignment & stakeholder Influence Without relying on formal authority, this role will offer the opportunity to influence senior leaders and cross‑functional partners through expertise, credibility, and sound judgment. This work will strengthen decision quality, governance, and alignment as part of a purpose‑driven organization that values collaboration, accountability, and long‑term impact while delivering joy to millions of fans worldwide. FLSA Classification (US Only): Exempt People Manager: No What you’ll Do Program Design, Governance & Compliance Plan and deliver executive and enterprise compensation program work within a 1–2 year horizon, by anticipating business, talent, performance, and governance needs. Design, administer, and iterate on executive and enterprise compensation programs (base salary, annual incentives, long‑term incentives, deferred compensation, and perks) aligned with company strategy and pay‑for‑performance principles. Apply enterprise systems thinking to ensure executive compensation programs integrate coherently with broader compensation architecture, including job levels, pay structures, incentive frameworks, and career progression models. Identify opportunities to improve program effectiveness, governance rigor, and alignment between performance outcomes and reward strengthening long‑term sustainability. Ensure compliance with regulatory, accounting, and internal governance requirements (including IRS Section 409A), partnering with Legal, Finance, Accounting, and Tax to assess implications and mitigate risk. Own preparation of executive‑ready materials for leadership and governance forums. Market Intelligence & Analytics Conduct executive market pricing using reputable surveys and peer benchmarking; maintain and evolve survey strategy, peer groups, and executive salary structures. Build and own advanced models and scenario analyses evaluating pay mix, incentive outcomes, performance metric calibration, affordability, and cost or risk under multiple business conditions. Analyze enterprise compensation data to assess downstream impacts of executive compensation decisions on internal equity, pay compression, talent differentiation, and sustainability. Monitor governance developments, regulatory changes, and proxy advisor trends; translate insights into practical, data‑backed recommendations that improve plan design, disclosures, and decision quality. ABOUT THE ROLE: We are seeking an experienced Principal Facilities Engineer to support critical facility and utility systems at our Mesa, Arizona site, a regulated pharmacy/manufacturing facility operating under cGMP requirements. This role requires hands-on engineering expertise across HVAC, electrical, compressed air, purified water, and building automation systems, with a deep understanding of GMP compliance, equipment qualification, and facility reliability. The ideal candidate will serve as the on-site engineering authority during the Wednesday–Sunday shift, working hand-in-hand with the Maintenance team as the engineering point of contact whenever an issue arises. YOU WILL: FACILITY & CRITICAL UTILITY SYSTEMS ENGINEERING - Serve as the on-site engineering lead for facility systems (HVAC, electrical distribution, compressed air, purified/RO water, EMS, BMS/BAS, generators, fire/life safety) during the Wed–Sun shift. - Review and redline design drawings, P&IDs, and specifications for new construction, renovation, and equipment installation projects to ensure code compliance, GMP suitability, and operational fit. - Engage with HVAC design during construction, evaluating equipment specifications and system selection to confirm the right systems are chosen and correctly installed against the facility's URS and regulated environment requirements. - Apply psychrometric analysis specific to the region's climate to validate HVAC system design, capacity, and performance. - Develop and maintain utility system design standards and basis-of-design documentation for the site. - Engage with vendors on existing equipment to optimize settings, evaluate upgrade opportunities, and improve system reliability. INSTALLATION, COMMISSIONING & COMPLIANCE - Provide on-site technical oversight during installation of facility and utility systems, serving as the point of contact between Hims & Hers and external vendors/contractors. - Lead or support commissioning and qualification activities (IQ/OQ/PQ) for critical equipment and utility systems in the regulated environment. - Manage acceptance testing, punch list closeout, and system turnover to operations for construction and capital projects. - Ensure facility equipment and utility systems remain qualified and compliant with cGMP, FDA 21 CFR Part 210/211, and applicable state and local regulations. - Ensure preventive maintenance contracts are in place for all facility equipment/utilities with appropriate SLAs and emergency dispatching protocols; Maintenance coordinates the resulting PMs and related CMMS work orders. RELIABILITY, MAINTENANCE PARTNERSHIP & ISSUE RESPONSE - Coach and support Maintenance Technicians on shift for system upkeep, preventive maintenance execution, and downtime/excursion remediation. - Lead root cause investigations for equipment failures or excursions affecting GMP-relevant systems; partner with Quality on CAPAs and change controls. - Manage change control processes for modifications to critical facility/utility systems, including impact assessments and requalification needs. - Respond to critical alarms and emergency events (HVAC excursions, environmental excursions, power loss, water system failures) during shift hours and off-hours, escalating and documenting appropriately. DOCUMENTATION, SAFETY & REGULATORY COMPLIANCE - Maintain accurate documentation: SOPs, work instructions, as-built records, validation records, and regulatory files. - Ensure ongoing compliance with OSHA, EPA, NFPA, and local building/fire codes. - Participate in EHS programs and support internal audits and regulatory inspections as a technical resource for facility and utility systems. CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION & CAPITAL PROJECTS - Manage relationships with contractors and vendors for specialized maintenance, calibration, and capital project work. - Support capital improvement and equipment installation projects — scoping, contractor coordination, and commissioning. - Work cross-functionally with Operations, Maintenance, Quality, and Validation teams to align facility and utility performance with operational needs. YOU HAVE: - Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field; equivalent hands-on experience considered in lieu of a degree. - 8-10 years of facilities engineering experience, including at least 7+ years in a GMP-regulated pharmaceutical, biotech, or manufacturing environment. - Working knowledge of cGMP, FDA 21 CFR Part 210/211, and validation lifecycle documentation (IQ/OQ/PQ). - Hands-on experience with critical building systems: HVAC (including cleanroom/controlled environments), electrical distribution, compressed air, purified water/WFI systems, environmental monitoring systems (EMS), and building automation (BMS) platforms. - Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, P&IDs, equipment specifications, and design documents. - Experience coordinating with Maintenance teams on PM program execution and/or managing contractors. - Strong troubleshooting skills and the ability to respond calmly and effectively to facility emergencies. - CMMS familiarity (e.g., Maximo, UpKeep, MaintainX) preferred. - Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint); familiarity with CAD tools (AutoCAD or equivalent) is a plus. - PE licensure is not required. - Must be able to work the scheduled shift — Wednesday–Sunday, 2:00 PM – 10:00 PM — with flexibility for on-call/emergency response outside scheduled hours (regular hours can adjust/shift when responding to on-call/emergency situations). - Ability to lift up to 50 lbs, stand/walk for extended periods, work in mechanical rooms and at heights (ladders/lifts), and wear required PPE in varying temperatures, noise levels, and controlled/cleanroom environments. OUR BENEFITS (THERE ARE MORE BUT HERE ARE SOME HIGHLIGHTS): - Competitive salary & equity compensation for full-time roles - Unlimited PTO, company holidays, and quarterly mental health days - Comprehensive health benefits including medical, dental & vision, and parental leave - Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP) - Employee discounts on hims & hers & Apostrophe online products - 401k benefits with employer matching contribution - Offsite team retreats Conditions of Employment: - This position will require working with Hazardous Drugs (HD) and would require that Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) be worn for the length of working with these drugs. These items would include gloves, respiratory protection, gown and other items as required. - This position requires medical approval to wear respiratory protection in the form of negative or positive pressure respirators, including N95, full face respirator, SCBA, or Powered Air Purifying Respirator (PAPR). - Physical exertion required. Including, but not limited to, walking up to 50% of the time, standing up to 100% of the time, squatting and bending up to 20% of the time and lifting up to 80% of the time for up to a twelve hour shift. Must be able to lift up to 50lbs. - Due to the risk of reproductive capability in handling or compounding certain Hazardous Drugs (HD) associates must be willing to confirm that they understand the potential risks (teratogenicity, carcinogenicity and reproductive effects) of handling hazardous drugs.
