title: 003-09-2026/GD-DRC AGENT CENTRE D'APPEL DRC -GOMA
descriptionText: GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We support high ownership and real professional growth. Curious about what it's really like to work here? Read our values and hear from the people who do. If they resonate, this could be a great fit! Background : GiveDirectly (GD) vise à remodeler les dons internationaux - et des millions de vies - en fournissant des subventions en espèces directement aux plus pauvres du monde. The Brookings Institution estime que 70 milliards de dollars de transferts en espèces seraient nécessaires pour éliminer le fossé de la pauvreté ; le secteur de l'aide dépense actuellement 135 milliards de dollars par an, dont une grande partie pour des interventions non fondées sur des données probantes. GiveDirectly veut changer cela, en faisant des transferts d'argent liquide une référence pour l'aide étrangère - comme le fonds indiciel est une référence pour l'industrie financière - et en accélérant ainsi la fin de l'extrême pauvreté. GD a levé plus de 700 millions de dollars depuis son lancement en 2011, distribué de l'argent à plus d'un million de personnes et ouvert des bureaux dans 10 pays. Nous avons également soutenu des recherches expérimentales à grande échelle qui indiquent un fort impact de nos programmes sur les bénéficiaires. En conséquence, GD a été reconnue comme l'une des organisations à but non lucratif les plus innovantes par Fast Company, tandis que le mouvement croissant des transferts d'argent liquide (et le rôle de premier plan joué par la GD dans ce cadre) a fait l'objet d'un article dans le magazine New York Times Magazine, This American Life, Foreign Affairs, et The Economist. GiveDirectly offre la possibilité de travailler avec des personnes originaires de 21 pays différents et parlant 69 langues différentes. Nous travaillons activement à la mise en place d'un environnement équitable et inclusif pour tous les membres de l'équipe, et notre personnel apporte des perspectives et des expériences diverses à notre organisation. Dans nos bureaux du monde entier, notre culture est franche, analytique, non hiérarchique et rapide. Nous valorisons les capacités, l'adaptabilité et la volonté d'apprendre. À propos de GiveDirectly en RD Congo : GiveDirectly RDC a été créé en 2018 afin de permettre des transferts monétaires aux populations pauvres et rurales via les téléphones portables, afin de promouvoir la sécurité alimentaire, la réduction de la pauvreté et l’inclusion financière. Nous souhaitions démontrer la faisabilité opérationnelle et la rentabilité du transfert d’importants volumes monétaires sous forme numérique dans l’un des pays les moins développés du monde. Depuis sa création, il y a quatre ans, GiveDirectly RDC a utilisé les téléphones mobiles pour transférer plus de 14 millions de dollars à plus de 65 000 bénéficiaires dans quatre provinces : Sud-Kivu, Nord-Kivu, Ituri et Kinshasa. Les activités de GiveDirectly en RDC se sont développées de manière à inclure, notamment : des preuves de concept convaincantes des transferts d’argent liquide basés sur les téléphones portables ; la mise en œuvre de technologies innovantes de ciblage des populations urbaines défavorisées de Kinshasa, en collaboration avec l’agence de protection sociale de la RDC, le Fonds Social de la RDC ; la livraison d’argent liquide sans contact aux bénéficiaires de Beni et Bunia affectés par les conséquences économiques de la COVID-19. Vous rejoindrez Give Directly RDC à un moment passionnant de son histoire, alors que nous mettons en place et espérons lancer plusieurs nouveaux programmes et renforcer notre partenariat avec le gouvernement de la RDC. AGENT CENTRE D’APPEL /CCA 1.Taches et Responsabilites Recevoir les appels entrants et fournir des solutions et des réponses aux demandes et aux plaintes des bénéficiaires GiveDirectly. Identifier et capturer toutes les plaintes des bénéficiaires et travailler sur la résolution des plaintes différentes Soulever/escalader tous les cas sensibles qui peuvent nuire à la sécurité de la vie/famille du bénéficiaire pour que des mesures soient prises. Capturer l'interaction entre le CCA et les bénéficiaires avec précision, sans omissions ni distorsions. Proposer de nouvelles idées au TL/QA/CCM en fonction des commentaires du bénéficiaire Mener des sondages téléphoniques pour s'assurer que les bénéficiaires ont reçu leurs transferts sans problème. Sensibiliser les appelants par rapport aux objectifs et conditions des projets menés par GiveDirectly Suivre le script de communication de l’organisation dans la communication avec les appelants pour répondre aux questions des appelants Collecter, confirmer et capturer toute nouvelle information provenant des appels. Comprendre le processus d'escalade et signaler les cas difficiles aux superviseurs. Gérer les autres canaux d'assistance aux bénéficiaires si nécessaire (par exemple, SMS) Expliquer les informations complexes d’une manière claire en langue Locale 2.Profil Recherché Diplôme universitaire dans un domaine pertinent Souhaitable: Au moins 1 an d'expérience dans les centres d'appels, de préférence dans une ONG internationale 3.Compétence et qualification souhaitables Capacité à traiter les plaintes avec politesse ; manière empathique et professionnelle Capacité à utiliser une approche positive, constructive et axée sur les solutions chaque fois qu'un conflit survient Attitude positive et enthousiaste face au travail de routine Capacité à effectuer plusieurs tâches Niveaux élevés d'intégrité et de confidentialité des informations des bénéficiaires. Excellente étiquette téléphonique Excellentes capacités de communication Un (e) apprenant (e) rapide qui a la passion de fournir des solutions. Une expérience passée dans des ONG est un atout supplémentaire. Parler couramment au moins l’une de ces langues LINGALA, KIKONGO, TSHILUBA, KIYOMBE ET KINTANDU , est obligatoire et exigible. Diligence pour suivre les instructions de manière fiable et méthodique Maîtrise de MS Word, Excel Respect des valeurs de GD (ci-dessous) Valeurs de GD : Priorité aux bénéficiaires : Nous privilégions les préférences des bénéficiaires, pas celles de nos donateurs ni même les nôtres. L’équipe avant l’individuel : Nous œuvrons pour le succès de l’organisation, pas celui des individus. Être proactivement franc : Nous parlons et communiquons les informations en toute franchise. Créer une énergie positive : Nous nous efforçons d’apporter de l’énergie positive à nos collègues, et pas de la leur prendre. Réfléchir rigoureusement, agir rapidement : Priorité à la rigueur et à l’action, pas au débat interminable. Se connaître et se développer : Nous sommes conscients de nos défauts, mais nous les exploitons. Accepter la réalité, Proposer des solutions : Nous ne nous attardons pas sur les problèmes. Nous créons des solutions. Être ambitieux de manière productive : Nous prenons des risques qui pourraient révolutionner le secteur. title: Associate Data Engineer (UMiami Only)
descriptionText: Radiology is the second most used healthcare service, used by over 51% of the workforce annually. Despite the critical role of radiology in healthcare, the process for undergoing a medical imaging exam has remained unchanged for decades. OneImaging is solving this with a concierge approach and a premium-quality radiology network of over 5,000 vetted providers across 48 states, which also reduces imaging costs by 60-80%. Our solution helps patients and families access essential radiology services at fair prices and without surprise bills, all while delivering immediate savings and ROI for employers and payers on every exam. We’re hiring Data Engineers graduating between December 2026 and June 2027 to join our data team in Miami, starting May or June 2027. This is not a rotational program and it isn’t a shadowing role. You’ll work on the pipelines and integrations that make OneImaging’s data the source of truth for the business - from the raw feed coming out of a payer, a provider, or our own platform, through the transformation logic, to the dashboard or automation that someone in operations, finance, or care navigation actually relies on every day. It also means you’ll be building alongside a team that has moved unusually early on AI-assisted engineering. We run a shared AI harness that every engineer’s agent builds on, and we’re explicit internally that writing code is no longer the slow part of the job - the slow parts are deciding what to build and verifying what comes out. We’ll expect you to use these tools heavily and to own everything they produce for you. What you'll do: Build and maintain data pipelines in Databricks (SparkSQL/PySpark) that ingest, transform, and validate data from sources like our platform databases, payer eligibility files, provider and claims systems, and third-party APIs - with a senior engineer as your mentor and reviewer Work across the full path a dataset takes - ingestion, transformation, modeling, and the Looker dashboard or downstream workflow it feeds - with guidance at first and increasing independence as you go Help build and maintain automated inbound/outbound file exchanges (eligibility, claims status, reporting) that other teams depend on to run their day-to-day operations Work with AI coding agents as a normal part of your workflow, and take full accountability for the output: you should be able to explain every file in your diff Write tests and validation checks for your pipelines, and treat data quality as part of shipping rather than a phase afterwards Participate in design reviews and code reviews from your first weeks - including reviewing other engineers’ work, because a bare approval with no comment isn’t a completed review here Ask why. We reason from first principles and we have an explicit norm that engineers are not implementation machines - if a requirement doesn’t make sense, we want you to say so Handle protected health information correctly, with data governance, access controls, and audit logging as first-class requirements rather than afterthoughts About you: Graduating with a B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Data Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical discipline between December 2026 and June 2027 You’ve built things nobody assigned you - side projects, coursework you took further than required, hackathon work, something with real data, however small Strong SQL skills and working knowledge of Python for data processing Some exposure to Databricks, Spark, or a similar distributed data processing tool - coursework, an internship, or a personal project is enough; we don’t expect production experience A basic mental model of how data moves from a source system into a warehouse or lakehouse and out to a report You use AI coding tools and you’ve formed opinions about them - including where they mislead you and how you catch it You can explain a technical decision you made and what you’d do differently, which matters more to us than the sophistication of the project Comfortable with ambiguity and with being told “we haven’t figured that out yet” Intellectually honest: you can change your mind when the evidence changes, and you’d rather delete your own work than defend it Clear written and verbal communication - you’ll be writing documentation and PR descriptions that other teams depend on Authorized to work in the United States, and able to be based in Miami Nice to have, and genuinely not required: An internship or co-op where you shipped a data pipeline or report to production Experience with a BI tool (Looker, Tableau, Power BI) or building a dashboard someone other than you used Exposure to AWS or another cloud provider Familiarity with relational or document databases (PostgreSQL, MongoDB) Anything you’ve built on top of LLM or agent APIs - tools, harnesses, evals, agents Curiosity about healthcare data standards (HL7, FHIR, DICOM) or claims/eligibility data - we’ll teach you these, and we’d rather you question how things are done in healthcare than arrive already knowing Coursework or projects involving statistics, data modeling, or data warehousing concepts What we'll give you A published career framework with written promotion criteria, so you can see the path from Associate Software Engineer through Senior, Staff and Principal, and know exactly what's expected at each step. A mentor from among our senior engineers, for whom mentorship is a written part of their job. Real ownership, quickly. And a mission that's easy to get behind with real life impact. We care much more about how you reason than about which technologies you've already used Familiarity with relational databases and SQL, and a basic mental model of how a web request becomes a database query You use AI coding tools and you've formed opinions about them — including where they mislead you and how you catch it You can explain a technical decision you made and what you'd do differently, which matters more to us than the sophistication of the project Comfortable with ambiguity and with being told "we haven't figured that out yet" Intellectually honest: you can change your mind when the evidence changes, and you'd rather delete your own work than defend it Clear written and verbal communication — you'll be writing design docs and PR descriptions that other people depend on Authorized to work in the United States, and able to be based in Miami Nice to have, and genuinely not required: An internship or co-op where you shipped to production Experience with PostgreSQL, Express, or a typed API layer Anything you've built on top of LLM or agent APIs — tools, harnesses, evals, agents Testing experience with Jest, Vitest, Playwright, or similar Exposure to AWS or another cloud provider Curiosity about healthcare data standards (FHIR, HL7, DICOM) — we'll teach you these, and we'd rather you question how things are done in radiology than arrive already knowing A background in accessibility or internationalization What we'll give you A published career framework with written promotion criteria, so you can see the path from Associate Software Engineer through Senior, Staff and Principal, and know exactly what's expected at each step. title: Senior Data Scientist, Product Analytics — Yahoo.com/Homepage
descriptionText: It takes powerful technology to connect our brands and partners with an audience of hundreds of millions of people. Whether you’re looking to write mobile app code, engineer the servers behind our massive ad tech stacks, or develop algorithms to help us process trillions of data points a day, what you do here will have a huge impact on our business—and the world. A Little About Us The Yahoo homepage is one of the most visited destinations on the internet. Our Yahoo News Group Analytics Team is the engine that powers its evolution, using rigorous experimentation and advanced analytics to improve the daily habits of millions of users. We are a high-autonomy team that values statistical integrity, clear communication, and an AI-forward approach to solving complex product problems. About the Role We're hiring a Senior Data Scientist to lead product analytics and experimentation for the Yahoo.com homepage. In this role, you will define how success is measured, design high-stakes experiments, and generate insights that directly shape our product roadmap. You'll partner closely with Product, Engineering, Design, and Data Engineering to guide high-impact decisions. Your work will span the full analytics lifecycle - from metric definition and instrumentation to experimentation and deep-dive analysis. This is a hands-on senior individual contributor role with significant ownership. You will operate as the analytical lead for your area, bringing structure to highly ambiguous problems and ensuring decisions are grounded in rigorous analysis. The person best suited for this role will be comfortable with vague metrics and energized by ambiguous problems. You've owned experimentation programs end-to-end — not just contributed to them — and you know the difference between a statistically significant result and a meaningful one. You treat AI tools as a core part of your workflow, not an add-on, and you're always looking for ways to work more efficiently without sacrificing rigor. Note: This role is focused on product analytics and statistical modeling. It is not an ML engineering role—you will not be responsible for building or productionizing machine learning systems. What You'll Do Influence product strategy and roadmap through data-driven storytelling, partnering closely with Product, Engineering, and Design. Define and own key product metrics (e.g., activation, engagement, retention) and the measurement frameworks behind them. Design, execute, and interpret complex, high-stakes A/B tests to inform product roadmaps. Proactively identify and implement AI-driven efficiencies in day-to-day analytics, automating repetitive SQL, Python pipelines, and report generation using approved tools like Gemini and GitHub Copilot. Apply advanced statistical methods (e.g., regression, cohort analysis, causal inference, churn/retention modeling) to solve complex business problems. Actively validate and QA AI-generated analytical scripts, database queries, and code blocks to maintain statistical integrity, error-checking for logical consistency and hallucinations. Partner with Data Engineering to build reliable, scalable datasets and establish robust event instrumentation. Lead and mentor junior analysts and project workstreams, championing best practices in experimentation, data quality, and statistical rigor across the team. Build dashboards and scalable data assets that enable self-service analytics across the organization. What We’re Looking For 5+ years of experience in product analytics, data science, or a related quantitative field with ownership of metrics and experimentation at scale. Strong statistical foundation, including hypothesis testing, regression, and causal inference. Demonstrated experience leveraging generative AI tools (e.g., Gemini, Claude) or AI-assisted coding tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot) to accelerate coding, debugging, and analytical workflows. Experience partnering with cross-functional teams to drive high-impact decisions through A/B testing and behavioral analysis. Proficiency in SQL and Python or R for data analysis and visualization. Experience partnering with Data Engineering to build reliable datasets and event instrumentation. Strong understanding of data modeling for both ad hoc and scalable analytics. Comfort operating in evolving, AI-augmented environments, viewing AI tools as a core mechanism to scale your analytical output and strategic impact. Preferred Qualifications Experience with consumer-facing or large-scale digital products (10M+ DAU). Experience establishing experimental design frameworks and data architectures for high-traffic environments. Advanced degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, etc.) or equivalent practical experience. The material job duties and responsibilities of this role include those listed above as well as adhering to Yahoo policies; exercising sound judgment; working effectively, safely and inclusively with others; exhibiting trustworthiness and meeting expectations; and safeguarding business operations and brand integrity. At Yahoo, we offer flexible hybrid work options that our employees love! While most roles don’t require regular office attendance, you may occasionally be asked to attend in-person events or team sessions. You’ll always get notice to make arrangements. Your recruiter will let you know if a specific job requires regular attendance at a Yahoo office or facility. If you have any questions about how this applies to the role, just ask the recruiter! Yahoo is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

title: Product Associate / Product Manager, Training & Enablement
descriptionText: GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. Job Type: Full-time Location: This role is fully remote but must be based in Mozambique or DRC only. Priority Application Deadline: October 5, 2026 or until we receive a critical mass of applications About this role GiveDirectly is planning to grow delivery roughly tenfold by 2028. Getting there means changing our programs faster and more often than we ever have: consolidating country programs onto a small number of common Salesforce builds through 2027, then layering on new enrollment models — large-group barazas, remote and self-enrollment — from 2028. Every one of those changes has to land with roughly 650 people in country operations. A new survey design is only as good as the Field Officer's understanding of it at seven in the morning, standing in a village with a tablet and no supervisor nearby. A Country Director needs to know why we changed something and what risk it carries. A Field Manager needs to know what changes about supervision and quality checks. A Field Officer needs to know exactly what to do differently tomorrow, and nothing else. That translation work is this role. You will turn new survey designs, program changes, and system releases into training materials, live training sessions, demo videos, release notes, and internal communications pitched at the right level for each audience — from Country Director down to Field Officer. We are looking specifically for someone who has been a Field Officer, or held a directly equivalent frontline role. Not as a nice-to-have: this role exists because materials written by people who have never run a registration are consistently too abstract, too long, and wrong about which details actually matter. You should know from experience what makes a training useful and what makes it a waste of a morning. Your work will be anchored on the 2027 rollout — supporting the consolidation of country programs onto common Salesforce builds, which is high-volume and has real deadlines — and will absorb 2028 pilot material as those designs become real. Beyond that, you will be a genuinely useful pair of hands to a small, fast-moving product team: expect a meaningful share of your time to go to ad-hoc support that doesn't fit neatly in a job description. We work across English, Portuguese and French. Materials that only exist in English do not reach Mozambique or DRC, and translating them after the fact is slow and lossy. We need someone who can write well in English and work in at least one of Portuguese or French. Explicitly not in scope: Designing the programs or surveys themselves — owned by the 2028 Design Lead, the STPM, Large Transfers, and the Senior Director, Product; this role makes those designs usable, and will often be the first person to notice when a design isn't explainable Salesforce configuration and technical build work — owned by the Technical Program Managers Deciding which change requests get built and when — owned by the STPM, Large Transfers Staff development, onboarding, and performance training — owned by the People team; this role covers product and program training only Reports to: Sarah Kenkuyu, Senior Manager Product, LLS Level: Open band — Associate to Manager, depending on the candidate. We would rather find the right person than fill a predetermined level. A candidate with deeper field experience, stronger writing, and the judgment to run their own queue and push back on a poorly explained design will be brought in at the higher end, with correspondingly more independence. Day-to-day work assignment: Requests come primarily from the STPM, Large Transfers (2027 build rollout) and the 2028 Design Lead, with the Senior Director, Product arbitrating priorities when they conflict. You are not expected to absorb every request that arrives — part of the job is flagging when the queue is over capacity. Travel Requirement: Regular — roughly once per quarter at minimum, and more during rollout waves, to deliver training in person and to see how materials actually perform in the field. What you'll do Build the training materials that make new designs usable in the field e.g., turning new survey designs, program changes, and Salesforce releases into practical training decks, job aids, quick-reference sheets, and step-by-step guides — written for someone who will use them on a tablet in the field, not read them at a desk Write internal communications pitched to the level of the reader e.g., taking a single change and producing the version each audience actually needs: the why and the risk for a Country Director; the timeline, staffing and cost implications for a Program Director; what changes about supervision and quality checks for a Field Manager or Assistant Field Manager; and exactly what to do differently tomorrow for a Field Officer — deciding what each group does not need to know is as much of the job as deciding what they do Deliver training live, and record it when live doesn't scale e.g., running training sessions with country teams before a rollout, in person or remotely; recording screen-capture demo videos of new builds and flows so teams can refresh without waiting for a session; and building a library that new staff can be pointed to rather than re-trained from scratch Own release notes and change documentation e.g., writing clear release notes as changes ship to the common Salesforce build, so country teams understand what changed, why, and what they need to do — and keeping documentation current rather than letting it drift from what the system actually does Work across English, Portuguese and French e.g., producing or adapting materials so Mozambique and DRC teams receive them in a usable language on the same timeline as everyone else, and managing translation support where your own languages don't reach Be a useful pair of hands to a small, fast-moving product team e.g., ad-hoc support across the Program Design team — pulling together a briefing, cleaning up a deck before a leadership check-in, taking notes and turning them into actions, chasing an open item across countries. Some of this will be unglamorous. It is also how you will learn the whole system faster than anyone else on the team Close the loop from the field back to design e.g., noticing when the same question keeps coming up in training, when a design cannot be explained simply because it isn't simple, or when field teams have quietly worked around a change — and bringing that back to the people who own the design First 90 days So the scope is unambiguous, here is what we expect the first three months to look like: Days 0–30: Get oriented on the 2027 common Salesforce build and the countries moving onto it first. Review the training and documentation that exists today and give us an honest read on what's working and what isn't — you will have a sharper view of this than we do. Days 30–60: Produce the full enablement package for one country's rollout: training materials, a live session delivered, at least one demo video, release notes, and the layered internal comms from Country Director to Field Officer. This becomes the template for everything after it. Days 60–90: Adapt that package for a second and third country, including at least one Portuguese- or French-speaking market. Establish a simple intake and prioritization method for training requests, so the queue is visible rather than negotiated ad hoc. title: Staff Software Engineer
descriptionText: Code for America believes government can work for the people, by the people, in the new digital age, and that government at all levels can and should work well for all people. For more than a decade, we’ve worked to show that with the mindful use of technology, we can break down barriers, meet community needs, and find real solutions. Our employees build and transform government and community tools and services, making them so good they inspire change. We merge the best parts of technology, nonprofit, and government to help support the people who need it most. With a focus on transparency and fairness, and deep empathy for partners in government and community organizations and the people that our partners serve, we’re building a movement of motivated change agents driven by meaningful results and lasting impact. At Code for America, you contribute to exciting work while learning and developing in a supportive and flexible environment. Our compensation and benefits are holistic and thoughtfully curated to represent our employees and our mission. Help us drive real generational change that lasts. Code for America is looking for a talented Staff Software Engineer who will help shape the technical direction of an engineering team that is contributing to high-impact government services. In this role you will drive reliable, high-quality software delivery — improving how the team builds, tests, and ships the systems that make public services more accessible and effective for the people who need them most. The pace of change in the policy and government landscape is accelerating at the same time that technology possibilities are shifting rapidly. Together, these shifts create new windows of opportunity to develop technical solutions that make critical public services more effective for the people who need them. Staff software engineers keep delivery moving through those moments, supporting staff and holding high delivery standards so that what we ship stays reliable and effective. About the role: All Code for America software engineers are involved in every stage of our products' lifecycle, from prototyping and design to developing features in response to user feedback, to operating technical systems at scale. Staff Software Engineers pair hands-on engineering with leadership — guiding their team’s technical direction, demonstrating sound judgment, and enabling their fellow engineers through collaboration and mentorship. Staff Software Engineers strengthen their team's delivery practices and help other engineers on their team grow, setting a standard for technical judgment and collaboration within their project. This role will report to the Engineering Manager and is expected to travel no more than 10% of the time. Code for America is based in California and can employ those who reside full-time within the United States. This is a remote position. In this position you will: Technical Delivery Craft new features that help users more easily navigate government services and receive a dignified experience. Write automated tests and develop monitoring strategies to ensure a high level of service quality. Work iteratively to ship minimal features, learn, and harden them to scale once proven Contribute to design, implementation, and code review, and make technical trade-offs alongside your team, responsibly using AI-assisted development. Own architecture and data-modeling decisions for significant parts of a production system, weighing tradeoffs across competing priorities — speed vs. maintainability, the familiar tool vs. the right one, ideal vs. feasible. Support Engineering's culture of writing by producing quality documentation and learning materials for internal and external audiences. Technical Leadership & Enablement Establish direction for technical work within your team or project, anticipating challenges, documenting decisions, and helping the team understand the why behind approaches, not just the what. Collaborate with Product Managers and other cross-functional peers and adapt your approach as priorities, technology, and team needs shift — and actively help others do the same when facing major changes in direction or tooling. Biasing to action when the team is stuck, committing to a path forward and revising as new information emerges. Mentor engineers on sound technical judgment and engineering practice, and create conditions for them to grow into unfamiliar problem spaces through pairing, documentation, structured learning, or direct coaching. Act as connective tissue within your team—guide team norms, surface dependencies early, align on shared patterns, and bring in practices that have worked well elsewhere to strengthen how your team delivers Other duties as assigned About you: 7+ years of software engineering experience, with strong expertise in system architecture, data modeling, web technologies, and API design. Experience working across multiple languages, frameworks, and tech stacks — or a demonstrated ability to ramp quickly into unfamiliar ones. Demonstrated ability to use AI coding tools judiciously, validating and refining generated code for quality, and modeling that discipline for teammates is needed for this specific role; organizationally, a curiosity about emerging AI tools and a commitment to using them responsibly and effectively Experience with Agile Software Development models like Scrum, XP, TDD, or BDD Demonstrated technical leadership in a team environment: setting direction and guiding sound decision-making in constrained or ambiguous contexts Experience with cloud infrastructure and IaC tooling Eager collaboration with peers, and in providing technical and professional mentorship Truly excellent written and verbal communication skills in English Expert understanding and experience communicating with cross-functional peers, and in translating those conversations into actionable tasks A deep commitment to Code for America's mission of making government services work well for the people who need them most It’s a bonus if you have: Deep expertise in one or more specific technology or domain areas relevant to Code for America's product portfolio. title: Marketing Operations Manager
descriptionText: Radiology is the second most used healthcare service, used by over 51% of the workforce annually. Despite the critical role of radiology in healthcare, the process for undergoing a medical imaging exam has remained unchanged for decades. OneImaging is solving this with a concierge approach and a premium-quality radiology network of over 5,000 vetted providers across 48 states, which also reduces imaging costs by 60-80%. Our solution helps patients and families access essential radiology services at fair prices and without surprise bills, all while delivering immediate savings and ROI for employers and payers on every exam. We’re looking for a Marketing Operations Manager to support the execution and day-to-day operations of our member engagement marketing across the full member journey, from enrollment and activation through ongoing lifecycle communications. You’ll help run multi-channel campaigns, coordinate direct-mail and event logistics, keep projects on track, and make sure work moves smoothly from request to launch. You’ll work cross-functionally with Customer Success, Member Services, and Product, and coordinate with external creative and print/mail partners. You’ll operate within our existing marketing platforms and systems, which are owned and administered by the marketing lead, so your focus is execution and coordination rather than platform administration. A growing share of the repetitive work is handled by automated and AI-assisted workflows, so you’ll spend your time keeping campaigns moving, guaranteeing quality, and coordinating the people and vendors who bring them to life. What you'll do: Campaign execution across channels. Execute and QA member campaigns across email, SMS, landing pages, and direct mail, building and testing journeys in Braze and launching them against documented QA checklists and naming standards. Direct mail and vendor coordination. Coordinate direct-mail production with our print and mail vendor, including job submission, proofs, the pre-send QA checklist, and in-home tracking, and manage benefit-fair materials, swag inventory, and shipments to field teams. Marketing intake and project coordination. Manage marketing intake and triage in Linear, classifying, prioritizing, and routing requests and driving them to completion, and keep calendars, timelines, and documentation current so nothing slips. Experiment pipeline coordination. Build our backlog of marketing ideas and tests, working with the marketing operations leader to move prioritized concepts into execution. Coordinate variants, approvals, and launch dates, and keep each experiment’s hypothesis, status, result, and next action documented. New customer launch support. Drive the new-customer launch checklist end to end, coordinating landing pages, cobranded toolkits, journeys, and mailers across Customer Success, Product, and creative partners to hit launch dates. Content and asset support. Create and update straightforward member-facing content and assets in Canva, and coordinate larger creative work with our design partners so materials stay clear, consistent, and on-brand. Reporting and optimization support. Pull campaign and channel performance data, help run A/B tests across subject lines, creative, and calls to action, and summarize results to support decisions. Working with automation. Partner with our automated and AI-assisted workflows, owning the QA and coordination steps where they hand off, and flag repetitive work worth streamlining. About you: 2-4 years in a marketing coordinator, marketing operations, or lifecycle marketing execution role. Experience supporting multi-channel campaign execution across email, SMS, landing pages, and/or direct mail. Comfortable working hands-on in a customer engagement platform such as Braze or Iterable, building and QAing campaigns and journeys (platform administration is owned by the marketing lead). Strong organizational and project-coordination skills, with the ability to manage many workstreams at once in a ticketing system such as Linear, Asana, or Jira. Experience coordinating external vendors and print/direct-mail production, and comfort with hands-on logistics such as events, fulfillment, and inventory. Strong writing and communication skills, with the ability to create clear, member-friendly, brand-aligned content. Familiarity with design tools such as Canva, Figma, or Adobe Creative Suite for light asset updates. Comfortable working alongside automation and AI tools, and motivated to streamline repetitive work rather than only execute it. Detail-oriented and organized, and able to thrive in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment. Interest in healthcare, digital health, or improving the consumer healthcare experience is strongly preferred. The base salary range for this position is $80,000 - $100,000. Individual compensation will depend on various factors, including qualifications, skills, experience, location, and applicable laws. In addition to base salary, this role is eligible to participate in our equity incentive and competitive benefits plans. Fraud and Security Notice: Please be aware of recent job scam attempts. Our team uses the oneimaging.com email domain exclusively. If you have been contacted by someone claiming to be a OneImaging recruiter or a hiring manager from a different domain about a potential job, please report it to law enforcement here and to candidateprotection@oneimaging.com. Equal Employment Opportunity: OneImaging is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer and values diversity in the workplace. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, reproductive health decisions, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, political views, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. OneImaging is committed to providing accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities in our recruiting process. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us at talent@oneimaging.com.

Excellent problem solving skills and attention to detail PCIe (Gen3/4/5) protocol experience preferred including knowledge of LTSSM, system enumeration and configuration space format. descriptionText: Description Keeper Security is hiring a Senior Software Engineer, Team Lead to guide the architecture, development and evolution of Keeper Commander, including its SDKs, CLI tooling and developer automation capabilities. This is a 100% remote position, with an opportunity to work a hybrid schedule for candidates based in the El Dorado Hills, CA metro area. Keeper’s cybersecurity software is trusted by millions of people and thousands of organizations globally. Keeper is published in 23 languages and sold in over 150 countries. Join one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity companies and help build the tools developers, administrators and DevOps teams use to securely automate and integrate with Keeper’s platform. About Keeper Keeper Security is one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity software companies that protects thousands of organizations and millions of people in over 150 countries. Keeper is a pioneer of zero-knowledge and zero-trust security built for any IT environment. Its core offering, KeeperPAM®, is an AI-enabled, cloud-native platform that protects all users, devices and infrastructure from cyber attacks. Recognized for its innovation in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management (PAM), Keeper secures passwords and passkeys, infrastructure secrets, remote connections and endpoints with role-based enforcement policies, least privilege and just-in-time access. Learn why Keeper is trusted by leading organizations to defend against modern adversaries at KeeperSecurity.com. You will remain deeply hands-on in architecture, coding, debugging and design while also guiding a small team of engineers and raising engineering standards across the platform. You will work closely with Product, QA, Security and other engineering teams to ensure Commander remains secure, reliable, extensible and easy to integrate into modern DevOps and enterprise workflows. This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys building developer-facing tools, APIs and automation platforms and who can move comfortably between low-level implementation details and broader architecture decisions. Collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams, both internal and external, to achieve project objectives. What You'll Bring Experience 4+ years of experience in the digital product space, with a focus on business and/or technology consulting. Product management & product owner experience Leadership Skills Demonstrated ability to lead and manage teams in a dynamic and fast-paced environment. Product and Advisory Expertise Deep knowledge of digital product management and strategy Expertise across all aspects of the product development life cycle. Competitive Research & Analysis Strategic Business Case Creation Decision Analysis & Modeling Hypothesis-driven Research & Analysis Ability to provide strategic guidance to clients and internal teams. Ability to use AI-powered tools and techniques through the product life cycle Relationship Building Strong interpersonal and communication skills to build and maintain trusted relationships with clients and team members. About Us Slalom is a fiercely human business and technology consulting company that leads with outcomes to bring more value, in all ways, always. In addition, individuals may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus. title: Enterprise Salesforce - Technical Architect / Account Leader
descriptionText: Who You'll Work With Slalom’s Enterprise Capability designs intelligent, human-centered business applications that help organizations serve customers with greater speed, agility, precision, and purpose. Partnering with leading platforms, including Salesforce, ServiceNow, Adobe, Anaplan, Workday, Contentful, Boomi, and Workato, we deliver scalable solutions that unify data, streamline operations, and turn insights into action. More than technologists, we connect strategy to execution by modernizing infrastructure, integrating critical functions, and activating AI-powered innovation to deliver measurable impact through partnership and experimentation. Job Title: Enterprise Salesforce - Technical Architect / Account Leader Slalom is seeking an experienced, solution-oriented Technical Architect / Account Leader dedicated to driving holistic customer value through innovative Salesforce and Customer Experience solutions. This role will be a senior technical partner to the Amazon account team and a trusted advisor to client stakeholders, from developers through C-level executives. The Technical Architect / Account Leader will lead discovery, design cross-cloud blueprints, and build high-impact demonstrations and proofs of concept that connect business outcomes to practical, scalable AWS-Salesforce solutions. This person will bring broad technical experience and deep Salesforce platform knowledge, with a focus on shaping sales solutions and ensuring delivery of complex programs from discovery through deployment and will collaborate closely with account leadership, client partners, alliance teams, and delivery leaders to grow the account and strengthen Slalom's technical point of view with Amazon. They are self-driven, operate with a “get it done” attitude, and have a passion for solving complex business and technology challenges. Responsibilities: Business Development & Sales Solutioning Partner with Amazon account leadership, client partners, sales executives, alliance teams, and capability leaders to identify, qualify, and pursue opportunities requiring strong technical solutioning. Shape and maintain a technical account strategy and roadmap that aligns Salesforce, AWS, and adjacent platform capabilities to Amazon’s business priorities, adoption goals, and measurable outcomes. Support solution economics by providing accurate architecture, staffing, estimation, and delivery-risk inputs for strategic pursuits. Help account and engagement leaders identify scope levers, sequencing options, and technical dependencies that protect client value, delivery quality, and project economics. Partner with Amazon account leadership, client partners, sales executives, and capability leaders to identify, qualify, and pursue opportunities that require strong technical solutioning. Lead client-facing discovery workshops to understand current-state architecture, business priorities, customer journeys, constraints, and desired outcomes; translate findings into clear, compelling solution approaches. Develop cross-cloud solution architectures, technical narratives, tailored demonstrations, proofs of concept, and point-of-view materials that bring Slalom's AWS-Salesforce capabilities to life for client stakeholders. Define and communicate technical scope, delivery approach, dependencies, assumptions, risks, and estimation inputs for proposals, work orders, and statements of work. Serve as a technical thought partner during pursuits, aligning diverse experts across Salesforce, AWS, Slack, Amazon Quick, ServiceNow, data, AI, cloud, and adjacent platforms into an integrated solution. Support pursuit leads and proposal managers in developing client-facing proposals, including solution diagrams, resource-model inputs, technical requirements, and delivery sequencing. Build trusted relationships with Amazon technical and business leaders, as well as key technology partners, to cultivate new opportunities and improve Slalom's competitive position. Develop reusable solution patterns, demo assets, and sales accelerators that improve pursuit speed, consistency, and quality across the account. Technical Architecture Lead end-to-end solution architecture for strategic pursuits, balancing client value, platform capabilities, security, scalability, maintainability, and time-to-value. Lead technical design sessions; document solutions aligned with client objectives; and identify gaps between current and desired end states. Establish responsible AI architecture practices, including evaluation criteria, grounding, human oversight, security, privacy, fallback and escalation patterns, and monitoring of quality and business impact. Lead the use of Slalom’s AI-driven accelerated engineering framework during pursuits and project implementations. Create and present cross-cloud reference architectures that articulate key capabilities, integrations, data flows, environments, governance, and technical tradeoffs in language appropriate for executive and technical audiences. Author and govern architectural standards for data modeling, identity and access management, single sign-on, secure API patterns, OAuth, middleware, and event-driven architectures. Assess technical feasibility and identify architecture, integration, data, security, and operational risks early; recommend practical mitigation strategies and phased delivery approaches. Apply current knowledge of Salesforce, AWS, customer experience, data, AI, automation, and collaboration technologies to guide fit-for-purpose recommendations rather than one-size-fits-all solutions. Guide clients through emerging technology patterns, including generative AI agents, Amazon Bedrock, Salesforce Agentforce, Salesforce Data Cloud, and real-time data and event-streaming use cases. Provide technical continuity from pursuit through mobilization, helping delivery teams validate assumptions, refine designs, and establish a strong architecture foundation for execution. Act as the architecture escalation point and technical liaison among client stakeholders, delivery teams, Salesforce, AWS, and other product or support organizations. Delivery Excellence Provide technical oversight and architecture guidance for strategic Amazon engagements to support delivery quality, sound decision-making, and alignment to the sold solution. Partner with engagement leaders and delivery teams to resolve technical issues, manage solution changes, and maintain a clear connection between business outcomes and technical execution. Manage client expectations and collaborate on viable solutions to complex problems. Leadership Act as a mentor and technical coach to practitioners supporting Amazon pursuits and engagements. Mentor and upskill team members through architecture reviews, pursuit coaching, reusable leading practices, and hands-on technical guidance. Contribute actionable feedback on technical team members and help build a strong, collaborative sales and delivery culture. Facilitate knowledge-sharing sessions and contribute reusable patterns, decision guidance, and lessons learned to Slalom’s architecture and engineering communities of practice. Qualifications 8+ years of CRM and enterprise technology experience, with the majority focused on Salesforce, including at least 5 years in client-facing technology sales, pre-sales engineering, technical enterprise consulting, solution architecture, or a comparable role. 3+ years of practical architecture or implementation experience with Salesforce, including Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Experience Cloud, Data Cloud, or related customer experience capabilities, alongside cloud computing platforms. Demonstrated success shaping and presenting complex technology solutions for enterprise clients, including discovery, architecture, demonstrations, proofs of concept, proposals, and technical storytelling. Hands-on experience with API integration patterns, middleware, secure authentication and authorization, and coding or scripting in languages such as Python, Java, JavaScript, or Apex. descriptionText: R1001835 Posted 09/24/2026 Senior Manager, Product Manager, Deposit Fraud Decisioning Lead New York, New York | McLean, Virginia Save Job Apply Category Product Experience Sr. Manager Primary Address New York, New York | McLean, Virginia Overview Senior Manager, Product Manager, Deposit Fraud Decisioning LeadAt Capital One, we believe great products begin with a deep understanding of our customers. From our earliest days, we pioneered the use of predictive modeling to individually personalize credit card offers, turning the entire industry on its head. As we’ve grown bigger, we’ve found more and more ways to use technology and face-to-face conversations to understand the human problems associated with money and finances.In the Consumer Bank, we’ve combined this human-centered approach with our heritage of data-driven decision making to design, build and test our way to truly enabling financial experiences. We’ve challenged ourselves to spend less time planning, more time doing, and, above all else, to see the world through the eyes of our customers as they work to understand and manage their money.Are you passionate about improving the way people interact with their money? Are you driven by the delight you bring to customers? Do you keep asking, “why,” until you hit the root? It’s common to fall in love with solutions, but have you ever fallen in love with the problem? Do you have an opinion on whether shipping is more important than perfection? Do you have a healthy dose of skepticism for the impossible? If you’re nodding your head, then we want you!About the Team: At the heart of any bank account, customers move and manage their money—transferring money between their accounts, wiring money to purchase a home, and more. At the same time, bad actors are constantly evolving to scam or steal from our customers. Our mission is twofold: make it seamless for good customers to use their account day in, day out, while making it impossible for those bad actors to get in.To accomplish this, we build the intelligent data-driven brain behind those customer experiences, managing the policies, models, and data integrations that power our automated decisions. We also design empathetic, trust-building experiences for customers and associates when a decision requires a human touch. We are a team of strategists, builders, and customer advocates who thrive on solving complex problems at the intersection of technology, data, and human experience. Role Overview:The Deposit Fraud Decisioning Product Manager will focus on protecting customers from account takeover and scams in key customer experiences. This role will be responsible for working across engineering, business analysts, data science, and with partner teams to craft journeys that aim to perfectly predict the potential risk, and guide customers and associates after an automated decision flags them for risk. This is a highly collaborative role, who will work closely with product managers across Capital One in the Retail Bank and Enterprise teams, designers, engineers, data scientists, operations, and business partners to continue to evolve our strategy.On any given day in the Bank you’ll be:Empowered. Part of a team driving the bank’s omni-channel acquisitions strategy responsible for setting and delivering the decisioning and treatment framework to ensure our business is gaining profitable customers through both digital and digital-human interactionsLearning constantly. title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer
descriptionText: About TailorCare TailorCare is transforming the experience of specialty care. Our comprehensive care program takes a profoundly personal, evidence-based approach to improving patient outcomes for joint, back, and muscle conditions. By carefully assessing patients' symptoms, health histories, preferences, and goals with predictive data and the latest evidence-based guidelines, we help patients choose and navigate the most effective treatment pathway for them every step of the way. TailorCare values the experiences and perspectives of individuals from all backgrounds. We are a highly collaborative, curious, and determined team passionate about scaling a high-growth start-up to improve the lives of those in pain. TailorCare is a remote-first company with our corporate office located in Nashville. About the Role TailorCare is building a world-class engineering culture, and we are looking for a Senior Site Reliability Engineer to help build and scale our infrastructure. As an early hire in our newly formed Infrastructure & SRE department, you will work directly with the Director of Infrastructure & SRE, who sets our technical direction, and you will play a hands-on role in translating that vision into a resilient, scalable, and secure platform. You will have opportunities to shape how the work gets done and to influence technical decisions through strong execution and informed recommendations. This is not a traditional "ops" role where you just close tickets. We are looking for an empathetic engineering advocate who partners closely with product engineering teams. You will help us execute on major initiatives in 2026 and 2027, including rolling out universal CI/CD systems, standardizing Terraform, tracking and driving improvement of DORA metrics, leveraging AI for automation, and establishing SLOs/SLIs and error budgets. If you love building paved roads for developers and bringing calm, automated discipline to production environments, this is the role for you. Primary Responsibilities Implement the standardization of our AWS footprint using Terraform. Eliminate manual provisioning, establish reproducible environments, and integrate AI-assisted tooling (e.g., automated PR reviews, intelligent infrastructure operations) to accelerate our workflows. Build and maintain universal CI/CD pipelines (e.g., GitHub Actions) that remove friction from the SDLC. Track and improve DORA metrics across engineering teams to ensure we are shipping quickly and safely. Implement observability improvements across AWS and third-party integrations. Monitor and support SLOs, SLIs, and error budgets for key services, ensuring high availability for our web/mobile apps, telephony stack, and data processing. Act as a bridge between SRE and software/data engineering. Advocate for operations-focused engineering in an empathetic, contributory spirit. You will treat developers as your customers and build self-service tooling so they can ship without filing tickets. Because our business operates across all US time zones (ET, CT, MT, and PT), you will help stand up the on-call rotation and contribute to shaping sustainable core on-call hours and escalation paths alongside the Director. title: Senior Developer Advocate
descriptionText: 1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $400M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing. About 1Password At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work. If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future. Developer interactions and conversations have changed. They have shifted away from owned web properties and in-person events toward just-in-time learning via generative AI and engagement with online communities via social channels. Developer advocates will build an advocacy strategy that works with this new context to support awareness and adoption of 1Password's developer tools, through technical depth, authenticity, and by advocating for users and their needs wherever they are. The Principal Developer Advocate is an individual contributors who will report to the Director of Developer Relations. You will shape 1Password's advocacy function for a new era of developer learning. You will foster and participate in direct, public conversations about AI security, publish authoritative content, and prioritize high-impact channels that drive product awareness, adoption and feedback at scale. You will be the face of 1Password Developer Relations at major, high-impact developer conferences: AWS re:Invent, KubeCon, and others, and leverage those in-person interactions for longer term impact. How we’re using AI today Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers. This is a remote opportunity within Canada, the US, and the UK. What we're looking for: - Technical Fluency: 10+ years in technical roles including software or platform engineering, developer advocacy, solution engineering, or other fields. You are deeply familiar with modern development workflows and patterns. - Advocacy Experience: 5+ years experience engaging with developers in visible, public facing roles, and advocating for their needs cross-functionally within your organization. - Community Leadership: Experience engaging in sensitive and complex community situations with humility, empathy, judgment, tact, and humor. - Partner Engagement: Experience collaborating with partners on technical and product marketing integrations and other partnership activities. - Communication: Exceptional skills at written and verbal communication. You communicate well in multiple formats including conference talks, blog posts, tutorials, books, videos, social media, and through technical assets including demo code or reference architectures. You are good at talking and listening. - Connection: You are a trusted and credible voice in the industry and have a large technical audience who use your perspective to shape their real-world technical and architectural choices. Bonus points for: - Security Focus: Experience dealing with security-conscious developer communities or products (Identity, Auth, DevSecOps) is a strong plus. What you can expect: - Engage: Create content that sparks engagement with current and potential 1Password developer community members, at scale, across channels. Generate awareness, engage in great technical conversations, and help users try, contribute to, and give feedback about product workflows. - Build: Engineer solutions to unsolved user needs that fill gaps, validate approaches, and inspire secure engineering practices in the real world, in collaboration with users and 1Password partners. - Advocate: Synthesize feedback and conversations with community members and partners into actionable insights for 1Password, that we can use to improve our user-facing workflows. - Strategize: Use data to evaluate engagement channels, and prioritize ones that effectively generate awareness and adoption at scale. Maximize the impact of targeted, high-investment activities like conference speaking to generate impact beyond their normal lifespan. - Speak: Use your speaking experience at the largest and highest-stakes developer conferences, including KubeCon, re:Invent, and others. - Enable: Build tools and training to help other 1Password employees engage effectively with the community. These could be speaking training, talk templates, community engagement guidelines, or other tools that can scale advocacy beyond the DA team. Collaborate with other teams to raise the technical bar for their content. Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $212,000 CAD and $318,000 CAD, plus immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs. UK-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between £136,000 GBP and £204,000 GBP, plus immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, pension, and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs. At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set. This posting is for an existing vacancy. Our culture At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone https://blog.1password.com/inside-the-culture-powering-1passwords-next-chapter/. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. The Job: As a part of the SLP program, you’ll be part of our Engineering team. You’ll get to: Design and develop electronic firmware and specifications for power tools including brushless DC motor controls, Li-Ion battery management systems and battery chargers. Implement and validate electronic designs through software development, test and simulation. Develop software verification and validation procedures using unit and integration tests. Provide leadership in achieving cost, performance and quality objectives of all related electronic systems, components and sub-assemblies. Develop solutions for electronic systems related issues as an integral member of a larger team. Maintain appropriate documentation for work performed. descriptionText: Essential Job Functions: Collaborate with development teams to design and implement CI/CD pipelines that automate building, testing, and deployment for .NET APIs and Node/Nx monorepos. Build and maintain Azure infrastructure including App Service, Functions, APIM, Front Door, Load Balancers, VNets, Key Vault, SQL, Storage, and ACR. Proven expertise with Terraform and Bicep/ARM; experience implementing policy-as-code (OPA/Conftest, Azure Policy) is beneficial. Deep experience with Azure DevOps Pipelines (multi-stage YAML, environments, library groups) and familiarity with GitHub Actions. Proficient scripting skills in PowerShell and Bash; working knowledge of .NET (C#) and Node.js build pipelines. Container experience with Docker and ACR; familiarity with containerized IoT Edge workloads is a plus. Solid understanding of identity and security patterns: Entra ID, managed identities, Key Vault patterns, service principals, RBAC. Demonstrated troubleshooting skills across CI/CD, application runtime, network, and infrastructure layers. Experience with patch management, capacity planning, and performance engineering projects. Hands-on experience with vulnerability management tooling and processes (Qualys, Mend, Wiz) and proven ability to drive remediation programs. Potential Certifications: Azure DevOps Engineer Expert (AZ-400) — highly desirable. Azure Solutions Architect Expert (AZ-305) — a plus. Azure Administrator (AZ-104), Azure Security Engineer (AZ-500), or other relevant Azure certifications — beneficial. Nice to Have: Experience with Azure IoT Edge or comparable edge platforms. Experience with Azure Arc and policy-as-code tooling. VM stack / virtualization knowledge (Hyper-V, VMware, or equivalent) and on-prem VM migration experience. Exposure to Azure Data services (Azure Data Factory, Synapse/SQL DW). Familiarity with managed identity transitions, private endpoints, and Zero Trust networking patterns. Traduire des analyses complexes en messages clairs et prêts pour les exécutifs, en présentant les arbitrages, les causes fondamentales et des recommandations appuyées par les données afin de soutenir la prise de décision de la haute direction de la chaîne d’approvisionnement. Définir et opérationnaliser un modèle de gouvernance de la performance pour les Opérations d’approvisionnement, incluant les définitions des KPI, la cadence de reddition de comptes, les mécanismes d’escalade et les forums de revue avec la direction. Collaborer avec les équipes TI et Analytique pour améliorer les rapports, tableaux de bord et la visibilité de la performance, soutenant ainsi la gouvernance, les revues de leadership et la qualité durable des décisions. Identifier et piloter des opportunités de simplification visant à réduire la complexité opérationnelle et à renforcer les contrôles. Gestion et gouvernance du portefeuille et du cycle de vie des produits Assurer une supervision stratégique des processus d’inscription et de retrait des produits afin de garantir l’alignement avec les objectifs du portefeuille et les capacités des fournisseurs. Assurer une coordination transversale étroite avec les équipes telles que la Gestion des catégories, la Planification de l’approvisionnement, les Ventes et la Stratégie d’approvisionnement afin de soutenir des transitions fluides et de minimiser les perturbations. Surveiller et valider l’exactitude des données relatives aux dossiers produits, en assurant des mises à jour en temps opportun dans les systèmes et une visibilité complète à travers la chaîne d’approvisionnement. Soutenir la prise de décision en révisant les propositions d’inscription et de retrait, en évaluant les impacts opérationnels et en assurant l’alignement avec les stratégies globales de l’entreprise et de la chaîne d’approvisionnement. Identifier et atténuer les risques opérationnels, mener des analyses post‑mortem et mettre en œuvre des plans d’action. Gouvernance et pilotage logistique Surveiller et soutenir l’exécution des activités liées aux allocations fournisseurs, à la disponibilité des produits et à l’intégrité des données dans les systèmes. Fournir l’orientation et la supervision nécessaires pour assurer une gestion exacte et ponctuelle des données produits et fournisseurs soutenant les opérations logistiques. Fournir des orientations concernant les activités de diversion des centres de distribution afin d’assurer l’alignement avec les priorités de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et les attentes en matière de niveau de service. Agir comme point d’escalade pour les scénarios complexes de diversion, en veillant à ce que les résolutions soutiennent les objectifs opérationnels et les engagements clients. Faciliter la collaboration interfonctionnelle pour résoudre les enjeux, éliminer les obstacles et assurer la cohérence des messages logistiques avec les stratégies globales de la chaîne d’approvisionnement. title: Client Executive
descriptionText: WHY CLARIUM? The healthcare industry overspends on its supply chain by over $25B each year, the result of fragmented data, inefficient workflows, and wasted supplies. Clarium is fixing that. Our AI-powered platform, Astra OS, gives hospitals end-to-end visibility into their supply chain operations, automating workflows and surfacing actionable insights so supply chain teams can focus on what matters most: patient care. We're trusted by some of the world's leading health systems, including Yale New Haven Health, Stanford, Geisinger, and Kaiser Permanente. Founded in 2020, Clarium has raised $43M in total funding. You'll take a set of existing accounts and answer the questions that matter most: is this health system realizing the savings it bought, does its executive team believe it, is that story public, will they renew, and what should we be doing together next? You'll be the single person accountable for the commercial outcome of each account; gross retention, the renewal signature, and expansion inside the system. You'll lead strategic planning with the owners on each account across Implementation, Customer Success, Product, and Engineering, directing the work rather than doing it, and you'll engage Clarium leadership when it strengthens alignment with the customer. By day 90, you'll have taken over your portfolio, built a validated value baseline for each account against what the customer actually contracted for, delivered your first executive business reviews, mapped every account's stakeholder landscape (including who's new since the deal closed), identified at least one qualified expansion opportunity per account, and owned your renewal forecast. At 12 months, you'll have delivered gross retention on your book, closed expansion in multiple health systems, established the value reporting model Clarium uses across its customer base, and converted at least one customer into a public reference. IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL - Own the commercial relationship and account plan for a named portfolio of live health systems with $5–7M in revenue potential, building relationships across operational, managerial, and executive stakeholders and holding them through personnel, process, and technology turnover - Run quarterly and annual executive business reviews with supply chain, finance, and clinical leadership covering performance against baseline, peer benchmarking, and the agenda for the next quarter - Carry gross and net retention targets across your portfolio, own the renewal and upsell narrative, terms, and closing, and maintain an accurate renewal forecast - Define, instrument, and report the financial and operational outcomes each health system contracted for, and build a savings case that holds up in front of executives and sponsors — including owning the numbers that determine what Clarium is paid where revenue is tied to validated savings - Direct each account through the CSM, Implementation, and Product/FDE leads on it — set strategy, sequence the work, escalate what needs escalating, and make sure those leads have what they need to hit their goals - Source, build, and close expansion end to end inside existing accounts — new modules, new service lines, and new entities within a customer's ecosystem — and cultivate customer advocates for case studies and references - 10+ years in a commercial role in healthcare SaaS or health technology — client executive, strategic account management, account management, or equivalent — serving hospitals, health systems, or IDNs - Past personal responsibility for a renewal, expansion, or growth quota, with specific results you can walk us through - A track record of running business reviews and commercial conversations with C-suite and VP-level health system leaders - The ability to build and defend a quantified financial case in front of an audience whose job is to poke holes in it - Comfort operating through others and being accountable for outcomes you don't directly execute NICE TO HAVE - Health system supply chain domain experience — sourcing, contracting, value analysis, clinical resource management, or supply chain leadership — as an operator or vendor-side at a supply chain technology company; direct or vendor-side perioperative experience is just as valuable - Experience with outcomes-based, at-risk, or shared-savings commercial structures - Healthcare consulting or transformation experience with provider clients - Experience at a scaling company where the playbook didn't exist yet and you helped write it SKILLS & TOOLS YOU'LL USE Nice to Know: Familiarity with health system ERP and supply chain systems (Workday · Oracle · Infor · GHX) and EHR environments (Epic), and how they shape what's operationally possible WHAT YOU GET AT CLARIUM Target Base Salary Range:$160K - Self-Service Support Tools: Oversee the development, deployment, and management of user-facing automation tools, including the enterprise Password Reset Tool, reducing helpdesk ticket volume and improving employee self-service capabilities. 2. Endpoint Security, Hardware & Hardware Security Collaboration with Security Teams: Work in close Collaboration with The Security organization (InfoSec, Threat Management, and Security Operations) to enforce endpoint protection baseline standards, hardware encryption, zero-trust policies, and continuous vulnerability management. MDM & Endpoint Management Strategy: Define and execute the multi-year vision for enterprise Mobile Device Management (MDM) platforms (Jamf, Microsoft Intune) and automated provisioning pipelines. 3. Identity & Security Integration: Strong experience with hardware authentication tokens (Yubikey), identity providers (Okta), password self-service platforms, and zero-trust security frameworks. Service Desk Governance: Hands-on experience establishing verification standards for IT Support/GSD, incident response workflows, and ticketing platforms (Jira Service Management, ServiceNow). First 90 Days: Deliver a 12-to-18-month strategic roadmap for Desktop System Management, setting clear milestones for zero-touch onboarding automation, endpoint security compliance, and frictionless employee tech experience.
